get.description: Carries `name` and `nickname` — the entry gate's first destination is *not named in full*, either missing — `has_player_profile`, its fourth, and `adult_attested`, all read from the account's own event streams rather than from a projection, so a player who has just named themselves or committed their profile is never sent back to a step they just finished by a read model that has not caught up. And `profiles` (docs/adr/0185 §2), which the gate reads **ahead of every destination**: whether the account acts as a player, the clubs it administers, and any invitation pending for its email.

post.summary: Attest that you are an adult — Start playing's first step
post.description: For an account that exists without the Adult attestation: one an invitation opened, which gives it the first time it acts as a player (docs/adr/0185 §5). Once given, giving it again records nothing — so an account that attested at sign-up is answered the same.

400.description: `adult_attestation_required` — the answer was not yes; `details.field` is `adult_attested`. Nothing was recorded.

put.summary: Name yourself — how should people see you?
put.description: **The naming**: one act carrying a name and a nickname, for the authenticated player, and repeatable — a later change is the same act, and keeping the nickname you already hold is admitted. Refused with `409 nickname_already_taken` when the handle is another player's; the name is checked against nobody. Answers the pair as recorded — the name trimmed and collapsed — and the client re-reads `GET /me` before moving on, which is where the entry gate reads it.

409.description: `nickname_already_taken` — the handle is another player's, `details.field` is `nickname`, and nothing was recorded: the act is one event, so the name is not kept either. The client writes the sentence under the field.

post.summary: Authenticate and obtain an access/refresh token pair
Forgot password?: email a link and a code
post.description:
Sends an email with a button and an 8-character code, valid for **one hour** and usable once. The button opens the public site's `/reset/<token>` page, for a player or an administrator; the code does the same from wherever the person asked.

**Nobody can use this to learn who has an account**: the answer is `202` with no body for an address with an account, without one, and for one asked for too often. **Throttled per address** — past three emails in an hour, a request sends nothing and says so to nobody. A newer email replaces the older one's link and code.

202.description: Accepted — **the same answer whether or not the address has an account**, and whether or not an email was sent.

post.summary: Exchange the emailed code for a ticket
post.description:
The address and the code from the email, exchanged for a short-lived `ticket` the new password is then set with. A claim is not a use: until a password is set, the same code can be claimed again.

Only a **right** code learns why it cannot be used; a wrong one is `code_incorrect` whatever else is true.

400.description: `code_incorrect` (`details.field`: `code`) — not the code sent to that address, **or nothing was sent to it**: the two are one answer. Five wrong codes lock the credential.

409.description: The code is right, and it can no longer be used: `credential_expired` (ask again), `credential_used` or `credential_locked` (five wrong codes).

post.summary: Set a new password, sign out everywhere, and sign in
post.description: Sets the new password with **exactly one** of the email's link `token` or a claimed code's `ticket`, then **signs out everywhere** and signs this session in: every access token issued before this moment is refused (`access_token_revoked`) and every refresh token revoked, so another phone still signed in is signed out on its next request. The answer is this session's new token pair. The link, the code and the ticket are spent.

400.description: `password_too_weak` (`details.field`: `password`) — 8 to 128 characters with a letter and a digit. The link and the code still work.

404.description: `credential_not_found` — a link or a ticket this surface never issued.

409.description: `credential_expired` (ask again), `credential_used`, `credential_locked`, or `ticket_expired` — the code was right and the password came too late; claiming the code again is a fresh ticket.

post.summary: Start an assessment and receive its opening question
post.description:
Idempotent per player and sport. Starting a sport that already has an unfinished run returns **that** run and its outstanding question with a 200, rather than opening a second one — so a double-tapped confirm, or a retry after a lost response, costs nothing. A sport whose previous run was abandoned still starts a new run, with a 201.

Both outcomes carry the same body, so a client that only routes on the step needs no branch; the status code is there for one that wants to tell the two apart.

**A sport this player is already rated at is refused with a 409** (`sport_already_rated`). A rating stream is keyed by player and sport and initialisation is its only transition, so a second completed run for one sport cannot be stored — and refusing at the start is the only point at which refusing costs the player nothing rather than a whole questionnaire. The picker offers unrated sports, so no shipped flow reaches this.

201.description: A new assessment was started; its opening question is returned.

200.description: An assessment for this sport was already in progress; its outstanding question is returned and nothing was created.

403.description: `adult_attestation_missing` — this account has not given the Adult attestation, which playing requires: an account an invitation opened, before *Start playing*'s first step.

409.description: `sport_already_rated` — this player already holds a Skill rating for this sport, so no assessment is started.

get.summary: Resume: one sport's in-progress assessment, or every sport's
get.description:
One question — *which of this player's runs are unfinished* — asked two ways.

**With `sport`,** the answer is that sport's outstanding run as an `AssessmentStepResponse`, carrying its outstanding question, or a 204 when there is none. This is the resume read, unchanged.

**Without `sport`,** the answer is an `InProgressAssessmentsResponse`: every unfinished run this player holds, at most one per sport, ordered by the sport registry, and an empty list — with a 200, never a 204 or a 404 — when there are none. Each entry carries the assessment id and its sport, which is what a router needs; it carries no question, because the caller re-reads the run it routes to and the empty answer is the common one.

Which shape comes back is decided by the parameter, so a caller that always omits `sport` always sees the collection.

schema.title: Response Find In Progress Api V1 Assessments In Progress Get

204.description: No assessment in progress for that sport. Only ever returned when `sport` is supplied.

get.summary: Fetch an assessment's current state — its question or its result

post.summary: Finish a stopped assessment: create its Skill rating
post.description:
**The irreversible one.** The questionnaire *stopping* and the assessment *completing* are two moments: answering the question that stops the run creates nothing and leaves every answer revisable, and this request is what turns those answers into a Skill rating. So a client can show the whole set of answers back to the player, still changeable, before anything is committed.

Callable only on a **stopped** run — one whose step carries neither a `question` nor a `result` while `status` is still `in_progress`. A run with a question outstanding, and one that was abandoned, are both refused with `assessment_not_stopped`.

The finished step comes back inline, `result` and all, because the player is shown their rating on the very next screen. **Calling it twice is safe**: the second call records nothing and returns the same result, so a double-tapped submit produces one rating rather than a conflict the client has to translate.

Once this has been called the run's answers are settled: a change is refused with `answer_not_revisable`.

409.description: `assessment_not_stopped` — the questionnaire has not finished asking, or the run was abandoned. Refetch the current step and render it.

post.summary: Abandon an in-progress assessment, freeing the sport to start again
Answer the outstanding question, or change an answer already given
post.description:
**One request, decided by what the run has already answered.**

- A `question_id` the run has *not* answered must be the outstanding one: this is an ordinary answer, and the next question comes back — or **no question at all**, which is the questionnaire stopping.
- A `question_id` the run *has* answered with a **different** `option_id` is a **revision**. The answers given after it are discarded, because each was pitched at a difficulty chosen from the estimate as it then stood, and the response is whatever the questionnaire asks next given the shortened set of answers. That may be a question, and it may be the stop — changing the opening answer to *I have never played* ends the questioning there.
- A `question_id` the run has answered with the **same** `option_id` records nothing and returns the current step. So a retry after a lost response is free, and so is changing your mind and changing it back.

**`question` and `result` both null, with `status` still `in_progress`, is the stop.** No further question would meaningfully tighten the estimate, and nothing has been rated: the run waits, with every answer still revisable, until `POST /completion` is called. Answering never creates a Skill rating, so a client need not — and cannot — predict which question is the last one.

The `transcript` on every response is the answers as they now stand; after a revision it is **shorter**, and a client showing the run's progress should read it rather than remember what it last drew.

**Answers are revisable for as long as the run is, and no longer.** Once the run has produced a Skill rating, a change is refused with `answer_not_revisable` — a code of its own, because the recovery is to show the rating rather than to re-render a question.

400.description: `invalid_answer_option` — the chosen option is not one that question offers.

409.description: `question_not_outstanding` — the question is neither the one awaiting a response nor one this run has answered; refetch the current step and re-render it. `answer_not_revisable` — this run's Skill rating already exists, so its answers are settled; show the rating instead.

get.summary: The Skill ratings this player holds, one per rated sport
The Social tag vocabulary and how many to pick, and the Search radius bounds
get.description:
Read-only, unauthenticated, no request body. Tag **ids** and their grouping cross the wire; the label a player reads is the client's own copy.

A tag id is permanent — it is persisted on profiles, so retiring a tag means dropping it from this response while continuing to honour it on the profiles that hold it. Ids are never reused and never renamed.

Both the group order and the tag order within a group are part of the contract: the picker renders what it is given rather than sorting.

`social_tag_selection` carries how many tags a profile must hold — both ends included. The profile commit re-validates against the same numbers, so a picker that reads them here cannot disagree with it.

post.summary: Commit every answer from onboarding's second part
post.description:
Idempotent per `Idempotency-Key`. The same key twice creates one profile and returns the same body — the second call answers 200 and records nothing.

**Every rule the picker enforced is re-validated here.** The tag vocabulary, the tag floor and ceiling and the radius bounds are all served by `GET /player-profile/options` so a client can build controls that cannot produce an illegal value — and a disabled button is not a validation. Photo ids are checked to exist *and* to belong to the caller.

**`weekly_hours` are required**, at least one hour of the 7 × 16 week (07:00 to 23:00). Silence about when a player usually plays is never scored as a zero, so it is asked for rather than guessed at. The minimum is exactly one and is not served — it is fixed, and a client holds it as a constant.

**The proposals opt-in has no default.** Send the player's actual answer; `null` is refused rather than treated as a no. The answer is recorded with the moment, the copy version shown and the surface, because consent is evidenced rather than asserted.

**`gender` is required and `gender_preference` is not.** The first is asked once, here, with `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY` a first-class answer — there is no unanswered state to send, so a missing or unknown value is a 422 rather than a coded refusal. The second defaults to `ANY`, is durable, and gates **both directions**: narrowing it also hides this player from the side it excludes. Neither value ever comes back out of this API.

**`intro` is optional and fenced at the write.** One line about yourself, at most a hundred characters, any language; a player who skips sends nothing and has no intro rather than an empty one. A line carrying a phone number, an email, a URL or an `@handle` is refused with `intro_not_admitted` before anything is stored. It crosses on the player card and on the record, and is not echoed here.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: What the client calls this commit. Sending the same key again returns the profile the first call created, with a 200 — one profile, one consent answer, whatever a flaky connection does to the response.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: What the client calls this commit. Sending the same key again returns the profile the first call created, with a 200 — one profile, one consent answer, whatever a flaky connection does to the response.

200.description: This idempotency key has already been committed; the profile the first call created is returned and nothing was recorded.

400.description:
`unknown_social_tag` — an id this platform does not serve; re-read `GET /player-profile/options`.

`social_tag_selection_out_of_bounds` — too few or too many tags for the served floor and ceiling.

`duplicate_social_tag` — the same tag id arrived twice.

`search_radius_out_of_bounds` — outside the served range, or off its step.

`weekly_hours_empty` — nothing ticked on the week. At least one of its 112 hours; the minimum is exactly one and is not served.

`proposals_opt_in_not_answered` — the answer was `null`. Ask the question; do not send `false` on the player's behalf.

`too_many_photos` / `duplicate_photo` — the photo list is not one a profile may hold.

`intro_not_admitted` — the line is not one the platform admits, with one coarse `details.reason`: `too_long` (over a hundred characters after trimming), `multiline` (a line break), or `contains_contact` (a phone number, an email, a URL or bare domain, or an `@handle`). Refused before anything is stored; the client says what to change and the server never says what it matched.

403.description: `adult_attestation_missing` — this account has not given the Adult attestation, which playing requires: an account an invitation opened, before *Start playing*'s first step.

404.description: `photo_not_found` — a photo id that does not exist, or belongs to another player. The two answer the same way deliberately.

409.description:
`player_profile_already_exists` — this player has a profile and this is a **different** idempotency key, so it is a second commit rather than a retry of the first.

`concurrent_modification` — two commits for this player raced and this one lost. Retry: the retry replays the winner.

get.summary: Every fact this player declared — what the Play screens and You read
get.description:
One read for everything a player declared, across the two aggregates that own it: the week, the radius and the per-sport Play intent the Play screens edit, and — since the *You* tab — the tags, the photos with their verdicts, the intro, the standing proposals answer, and the owner's own gender and preference. The one fact a search screen still needs from elsewhere — **which sports am I rated in** — is `GET /api/v1/ratings` and is not re-served here.

**`play_intents` holds only what was declared.** An undeclared sport is absent, never `null`: `NO_PREFERENCE` is an explicit answer, so there is no unanswered value to send. *Rated but undeclared* is a set difference against `GET /ratings`, and it is what a client uses to open the declaration interstitial **before** a search is refused with `play_intent_not_declared` rather than after.

**An empty `weekly_hours` is a real answer.** A player may clear their week; it means *we do not know when they play* and never *never*. **An empty `photos` list is one too**: a profile may hold none.

**Absent means omitted, never `null`.** `intro` is omitted where no line was written; a photo's `review` is omitted where nobody looked — which is not `allowed`; `gender` is omitted on a profile committed before the question existed — which is not `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY`.

## Who is told what

**`gender` and `gender_preference` are withheld from everybody but their owner.** No response that describes one player to another carries either — not a card, not a record, not a seat — and that walk is asserted over the whole emitted contract. This route is the one shape that carries them, to the person who set them, so the screen that asks *who should we match you with* can open on the answer already given (`docs/adr/0179` §4).

**The location area is not served, and neither is a flag for it.** A profile cannot be committed without an area, so `has_location` could never be false; the tab branches on the phone's permission state, which is the device's.

404.description: `player_profile_not_found` — this player has not finished onboarding's second part. The recovery is that part, which `GET /users/me` already sends a cold launch into.

put.summary: Replace this player's weekly hours — Save your week
put.description:
The whole week, every time — the list **is** the week, and what is absent from it is unticked. An hour is a day and the hour its cell starts at, 7 to 22: the week runs 07:00 to 23:00. Unkeyed and safe to send twice: the same week twice lands the same state, and a transition that changes nothing records nothing.

**An empty list is a legal value and clears the week.** The floor of one ticked hour binds the *commit*, which is the answer a player is asked for at the end of onboarding, and not every later edit of it. A cleared week is read as *absent* by the matcher, never as a zero — silence is never scored (`docs/adr/0102`).

**This is where a `KEEP_THESE_TIMES` prompt is answered.** The engine notices that a search ran on a week the profile does not hold and asks; nothing in the matcher writes a profile, so a *yes* is this request. Declining writes nothing anywhere.

Repeated hours are collapsed and the response carries the week as stored, in the platform's reading order — so a client can see what the profile now holds rather than assuming it kept what was sent.

It replaced `PUT /players/me/availability`, whose week was mornings, afternoons and evenings (`docs/adr/0189` §5).

404.description: `player_profile_not_found` — this player has not finished onboarding's second part. The recovery is that part, which `GET /users/me` already sends a cold launch into.

409.description: `concurrent_modification` — two writes reached this player's profile and this one lost. Retry: the retry reads the winner, and lands the same state or nothing.

put.description:
Whole kilometres, unkeyed, and idempotent for the reason the week is.

**This is where a `KEEP_THIS_RADIUS` prompt is answered**, and where taking a relaxation rung becomes durable. A rung is *"an ask and never a correction"* — running a wider search writes nothing — and this is the request the offer to keep it turns into. Accepting is also what stops the prompt: a profile that holds the wider radius takes no rung on the next search, so the condition that raised the question is gone rather than suppressed.

400.description: `search_radius_out_of_bounds` — outside the range served by `GET /player-profile/options`, or off its step. Re-checked here even though a slider built from those numbers cannot produce one: a control is not a validation.

404.description: `player_profile_not_found` — this player has not finished onboarding's second part. The recovery is that part, which `GET /users/me` already sends a cold launch into.

409.description: `concurrent_modification` — two writes reached this player's profile and this one lost. Retry: the retry reads the winner, and lands the same state or nothing.

put.summary: Move this player's Location area to where the phone is
put.description:
**The cold start's write, and no screen's.** The client re-reads the phone's position on every cold start and on return from the background after more than 24 hours — never merely on foreground — with the accuracy onboarding used, and puts it here silently. A revoked permission sends nothing: the stored area stays.

**What is sent is never what is kept.** The fix is rounded to the cell about a kilometre across before anything is recorded, exactly as the profile commit rounds it, so the precise fix never reaches the platform's records. A fix that rounds to the cell already stored records nothing and still answers `204` — which is what makes a write on every launch free, and why there is no `Idempotency-Key`.

**Nothing else moves.** A trip is a trip: the next deal deals around the new area, the radar refetches, *In your area* answers for the new cell — and nothing is reset, no radius changes and no prompt is raised. `204` and no body: no route on this surface serves the area yet, and a silent write on every launch is not the one to start.

404.description: `player_profile_not_found` — this player has not finished onboarding's second part. The recovery is that part, which `GET /users/me` already sends a cold launch into.

409.description: `concurrent_modification` — two writes reached this player's profile and this one lost. Retry: the retry reads the winner, and lands the same state or nothing.

put.description:
The whole selection, every time — the list **is** the selection, and what is absent from it is dropped. Unkeyed and safe to send twice: the same selection twice lands the same state, and a transition that changes nothing records nothing.

**Re-validated exactly as the commit re-validates** — against the served vocabulary and the served floor and ceiling — so the tab's picker and onboarding's cannot disagree about what a selection may be (`docs/adr/0179` §6).

The response carries the tags **in the vocabulary's order**, which is what the profile read serves and what a card draws, so a client can see what the profile now holds rather than assuming it kept the order it sent. The next deal anybody runs reads the new tags off the candidate index, as it always has.

400.description:
`unknown_social_tag` — an id this platform does not serve; re-read `GET /player-profile/options`.

`social_tag_selection_out_of_bounds` — too few or too many tags for the served floor and ceiling.

`duplicate_social_tag` — the same tag id arrived twice.

The commit's three refusals under the commit's codes: the picker on the tab is the onboarding step reused, and a control is not a validation.

404.description: `player_profile_not_found` — this player has not finished onboarding's second part. The recovery is that part, which `GET /users/me` already sends a cold launch into.

409.description: `concurrent_modification` — two writes reached this player's profile and this one lost. Retry: the retry reads the winner, and lands the same state or nothing.

put.summary: Replace this player's photographs, in order
put.description:
The whole list, every time, **in the order the player arranged it** — the first is the one a player card shows, so promoting the second photograph is a change even though the set is the same. Unkeyed and safe to send twice: the same order twice records nothing.

**An empty list is a legal value and clears.** A profile may hold no photograph; the poster returns on the card, and the photographs let go of become what the uncommitted-photo sweep collects.

**Photos write on every change** (`docs/adr/0179`): a player rearranging three photographs sends three of these, each idempotent, and the last one is the state — the row is the truth and a draft of it would be a second one. The verdict beside each photograph is the profile read's to serve, not this response's.

400.description: `too_many_photos` / `duplicate_photo` — the list is not one a profile may hold.

404.description:
`player_profile_not_found` — this player has not finished onboarding's second part.

`photo_not_found` — a photo id that does not exist, or belongs to another player. The two answer the same way deliberately, and it is the commit's check through the commit's port.

409.description: `concurrent_modification` — two writes reached this player's profile and this one lost. Retry: the retry reads the winner, and lands the same state or nothing.

put.summary: Replace this player's intro — or withdraw it
put.description:
**The day ADR-0170 §5 deferred to** (`docs/adr/0179` §6): the intro becomes editable with the tags and the photos, as one piece of work. The line is trimmed and fenced exactly as the commit fences it, and the fence is contact — nothing else is read.

**`null` withdraws the line.** The stream records that it was taken back and the profile folds to none — the same absence a player who skipped the step has, which the profile read spells by omission. Whitespace is `null`. The field is required, so `{}` is a 422: withdrawing has to be said.

**`204` and no body.** The intro reaches the card, the record and its author's own profile read and nowhere else (`docs/adr/0170` §3), and the write does not become a fourth shape: read the line as stored — trimmed — back from `GET /players/me/profile`, as the two gender writes are read back.

Unkeyed and safe to send twice: the same line twice records nothing, and so does withdrawing a line that was never written. The next deal reads the new line — or none — off the candidate index; search records already kept quote the line as it stood at the deal (`docs/adr/0104`).

400.description: `intro_not_admitted` — the line is not one the platform admits, with one coarse `details.reason`: `too_long` (over a hundred characters after trimming), `multiline` (a line break), or `contains_contact` (a phone number, an email, a URL or bare domain, or an `@handle`). The commit's fence exactly; refused before anything is stored, and the server never says what it matched.

404.description: `player_profile_not_found` — this player has not finished onboarding's second part. The recovery is that part, which `GET /users/me` already sends a cold launch into.

409.description: `concurrent_modification` — two writes reached this player's profile and this one lost. Retry: the retry reads the winner, and lands the same state or nothing.

put.summary: Correct this player's answer to the gender question
put.description:
*Self-declared, freely changed* (`docs/adr/0096`): a value a player may not correct is a value the platform has ruled on, which is the one thing this field is not. Unkeyed; an unchanged value records nothing, and a first answer on a profile committed before the question existed is a change and records one.

**`204` and no body, deliberately.** The owner's own profile read is the one response shape that carries a gender value out (`docs/adr/0179` §4), and the contract walk holds it to being the only one; the write answers nothing rather than becoming a second. Read the answer back from `GET /players/me/profile`.

The mutual gate reads the new answer on the next search either side runs: the searcher's own live, everybody else's off the candidate index, which follows the event as it always has.

404.description: `player_profile_not_found` — this player has not finished onboarding's second part. The recovery is that part, which `GET /users/me` already sends a cold launch into.

409.description: `concurrent_modification` — two writes reached this player's profile and this one lost. Retry: the retry reads the winner, and lands the same state or nothing.

put.summary: Change who this player is willing to play with
put.description:
A new durable answer to *who am I willing to play with* (`docs/adr/0096` §3). Unkeyed; an unchanged value records nothing.

**It is mutual and durable, and narrowing it has an effect the player must be told about at the moment of setting**: they become invisible to the excluded side entirely — including to searchers who asked for anybody. The client says so from a reason code; learning it from silence is not acceptable. Seats already accepted are facts, not candidates: nothing already agreed is undone.

**`204` and no body**, for the gender write's reason: the setting is served on the owner's profile read and on no other shape (`docs/adr/0179` §4). It gates the next search in both directions — this player's own, read live, and everybody else's, off the candidate index once the projection has followed the event.

404.description: `player_profile_not_found` — this player has not finished onboarding's second part. The recovery is that part, which `GET /users/me` already sends a cold launch into.

409.description: `concurrent_modification` — two writes reached this player's profile and this one lost. Retry: the retry reads the winner, and lands the same state or nothing.

put.summary: Answer the proposals question again, from the profile screen
put.description:
**The one write on this surface that always records.** Every other `PUT` here is a preference and a no-op when nothing changed; this one is a consent, and *the player was asked again, against these words, on this surface, and answered the same way* is a fact a consent log has to evidence (`docs/adr/0089`). So the same yes twice appends two answers, and there is deliberately nothing to deduplicate.

**The surface is this route's — `PROFILE` — and never the body's.** The commit records `ONBOARDING` because the commit is the end of onboarding; a client that could assert where a consent was gathered could assert one it never gathered. `copy_version` is the client's, because the words are.

`accepted` is required and **not** nullable, unlike the commit's: there, *unanswered* is a state a client can be in and is refused with a code that says *ask the question*; here the screen is the question and pressing is the answer. The response is the standing answer as the profile read serves it, with the moment it was recorded.

404.description: `player_profile_not_found` — this player has not finished onboarding's second part. The recovery is that part, which `GET /users/me` already sends a cold launch into.

409.description: `concurrent_modification` — two writes reached this player's profile and this one lost. Retry: the retry reads the winner, and lands the same state or nothing.

put.summary: Declare what kind of game this player wants, in one sport
put.description:
Unkeyed and idempotent. The same value twice lands the same state and records nothing the second time — intent is a **preference, not a consent**: there is no wording to evidence it against, so a stream that grew an event for an unchanged answer would be recording that a player did not do anything.

**There is no null and no unanswered state.** `NO_PREFERENCE` is an explicit answer — *either kind of evening suits me* — and the matcher must be able to tell it from *I never opened that screen*, which is what an absent declaration means. Nobody is ever backfilled to it.

**A declaration is not a search mode.** Mode is which tab you are on right now and has two values; intent is what you told the platform about this sport and has three. Switching the toggle for one search changes nothing here — this route is what *make this my intent* means.

**It needs no profile.** Intent is asked for at the tail of a rating run, which happens before onboarding's second part, so a declaration with no profile behind it is the ordinary first case.

parameters.name: sport

schema.description: The sport this declaration is about. Intent is per sport and never transfers between them — no object in the system holds two sports' intent at once.

parameters.description: The sport this declaration is about. Intent is per sport and never transfers between them — no object in the system holds two sports' intent at once.

409.description: `concurrent_modification` — two declarations for this player in this sport raced and this one lost. Retry: the retry reads the winner and either changes it or is a no-op.

post.description:
One photo per request. The body is the raw image and `Content-Type` names its format; JPEG, PNG and HEIC/HEIF are accepted.

**What is stored is not what was sent.** Every image is decoded and re-encoded to JPEG with its long edge capped, which is how EXIF — and with it the GPS coordinates a phone writes into a photo — is removed reliably rather than best-effort.

The returned id is what a profile commit carries; a photo becomes part of a profile only when a commit names it. Uploaded photos that are never committed are intended to be swept, and that sweep is not running yet.

**Every upload is checked against the on-court rule, and `review` says what the check concluded.** It never refuses: a `flagged` photo is stored, answers `201` and is committed like any other, and the warning is the client's to word. A photo the check could not be run on answers **nothing at all** — the field is `null`, because the reviewer's own outage is neither a reason to tell a player something about their photograph nor a reason to say it passed. Warn on `flagged` and on nothing else.

get.summary: A signed URL for one of your photos
get.description:
Returns a short-lived signed URL rather than the bytes: the store serves the image directly, so a photo never crosses this API twice.

A photo id that does not exist and one belonging to another player both answer `photo_not_found`, deliberately — the alternative is an endpoint that confirms whether a stranger's id is real.

**`review` is always `null` here**, and that is not `allowed`: this route does not read what the store holds beside the bytes. The on-court check's verdict crosses on the upload, where a player has just chosen the photograph it is about.

post.description:
The two of you disappear from each other's view everywhere, immediately, silently, in **both** directions.

**Idempotent.** Blocking somebody already blocked records nothing and answers 204.

**No cap, no cooldown and no rate limit**, and none will be added.

**There is no reason field.** A reason belongs to a report, and this is not one.

**Neither side is notified**, in either direction, and no response in this API reveals a block to the blocked party.

**The record is directed and the effect is symmetric.** Your block of them and their block of you are independent: lifting yours never lifts theirs, and neither of you can discover which way one went.

**It is forward-looking.** It removes each of you from the other's future listings; it does not reach into anything already agreed.

204.description: The block stands. Also the answer when it already stood — blocking is idempotent and a second call records nothing.

400.description: `cannot_block_yourself` — the caller named themselves as the other party.

409.description: `concurrent_modification` — two blocks of this player raced and this one lost. Retry: the retry is the idempotent no-op.

delete.description:
Lifts **your** block of this player, immediately.

**It lifts one direction.** If they have also blocked you, that block stands and the two of you stay invisible to each other — and nothing here tells you so.

**Idempotent, and it never 404s.** Unblocking somebody you never blocked answers 204 and records nothing, because a different answer would be this API reporting on somebody else's state.

204.description: Your block of this player is lifted. Also the answer when there was nothing to lift — the two cases are deliberately indistinguishable.

post.description:
Returns a ranked shortlist of at most **twenty** people worth messaging, **unpaginated** — there is no page two, and past the last row there is an honest empty state.

**The breakdown ships with the search, not behind a tap.** Every term, its weight, its value, its contribution and the evidence it read ride on every row, because *Why 78?* has to open instantly.

**Send asks, never facts.** Your radius, grid, tags, rating, intent and gender preference are read from your profile at request time. There is no per-search radius input.

**Relaxation is offered, never applied.** When the shortlist comes back short the envelope carries `rung_offers` — your times, then your radius x1.5, then x2.0 — each with a **real** count from a genuine re-run and its own window. Taking one is a **new search citing this one**: post again with `offered_by_search_id` and `rung`. Your saved preferences stay yours, and **the quality floor is never relaxed**, so *nobody tonight* stays a real answer.

**Competitive and for fun select different weight vectors**, and the list visibly inverts between them.

**Deliberately not idempotent.** Two taps are two searches.

**Re-sorting costs no round trip:** `search.sorts_available` says which controls to draw, and a sort that would reorder nothing is not in it.

200.description: A ranked shortlist of at most twenty, each row carrying a Fit out of a hundred and the complete breakdown that produced it. **An empty list is also a 200** — the honest empty state is an answer, and the pool it came from is described either way.

403.description: `account_held` — this account is under a live hold.

409.description:
`sport_not_rated` — you hold no rating for this sport.

`play_intent_not_declared` — you have not said what kind of evening you are after for it.

`player_profile_not_committed` — there is no profile to read a radius, a grid or an area from.

`rung_offer_not_found` — you cited a rung no search of yours offered. The widening is read off the offer, never off the request, so an unknown citation is refused rather than run narrow and recorded as widened.

503.description: Four distinct codes at one status, so a client can tell a transient outage from a refusal about *you*: `matchmaking_unavailable`, `gate_data_unavailable`, `index_too_stale`, `search_not_recorded`.

get.description:
Returns a search you ran earlier, in **the same shape the `POST` returned it**, so *Why 78?* opens as fast a month later as it did on the day.

**The record is immutable; the gates are live.** Blocks, holds, account state and the mutual gender preference are re-evaluated at read time, and nothing is rewritten by doing so.

**A row those gates now exclude is stated as withheld** — it keeps its place in the list, carries no person, and does not say which gate fired. Branch on `withheld`.

**A searcher may read their own search and nobody else's.**

parameters.name: search_id

schema.description: The answer's identity, from the POST
schema.title: Search Id

parameters.description: The answer's identity, from the POST

200.description: The recorded answer, **plus live gate state**. The same schema the `POST` returned — not a fuller one and not a slimmer one — with any row the fail-closed gates no longer admit **stated as withheld** rather than quietly missing.

403.description: `account_held` — this account is under a live hold. The hold points both ways, and it points at old answers too.

404.description: `search_not_found` — no search of **yours** has that id. A search belonging to somebody else answers exactly as one that never existed.

503.description:
`gate_data_unavailable` — a fail-closed gate could not be re-evaluated, so the answer is refused rather than served unverified.

`matchmaking_unavailable` — there is no index in this process to read the other side of the gender gate from.

post.description:
Seats a four — you and three others — chosen together rather than one at a time, and returns **all three arrangements** with a forecast each.

**Every gate binds all six pairs.** A block, a gender preference and the level tolerance are checked between *every two* of the four, not just between you and each of them. That is stricter than a shortlist and it compounds: a four can be impossible where candidates are plentiful, and the honest answer is a partial line-up carrying `NO_ADMISSIBLE_COMBINATION`.

**A seat is never filled below the quality floor** to complete a four, a newcomer least of all. *Three of four* is a real answer.

**Swapping sides costs no round trip.** All three arrangements cross, each with `is_best` and `is_evenest` — two separate booleans, because they can differ, which happens precisely when the four's levels are near-equal and balance has nothing left to say.

**Send `locked_seats` to hand-seat people.** From that moment the engine optimises **for the group** and says so in `search.optimised_for`, because you may end up with a worse individual match than an empty court would have given you.

**Send `completing_challenge_id` to finish a half-built court**, and send nothing else about it: the sport, the kind of evening and the locked seats are read off that challenge. **Any live member may fill it** — only the withdraw is the organiser's. The people who accepted come back as ordinary rows so the builder can draw them, everybody who has already answered that challenge is out of its own pool, and the window is never re-stamped.

**Somebody who let your invitation run out is out of that court's own pool, and out of nothing else.** Nobody is asked twice on one challenge, so they are not a candidate for this fill for as long as that court stands. Every **other** search of yours reaches them immediately, in any sport: their seat reopened and the open-challenge rule released them with it, because that rule holds the people still arranging a game and they are not one of them.

**A seated card shows the same number the shortlist showed.** Nothing is re-scored when somebody sits down.

**`candidates` is the pool the four were drawn from**, in Fit order, with the seated among them — look a seat's `player_id` up there. It is the list a pool opened on this answer draws, and the list `POST /forecasts` and the send resolve a pick against, so a court reached from a challenge has people to offer for its open seats without a shortlist of its own.

200.description: A seated line-up, every arrangement with its own forecast, and one reason this four beat the runner-up. **A seat may be unfilled and this is still a 200** — the empty seat says why.

403.description: `account_held` — this account is under a live hold.

409.description:
`sport_not_rated` — you hold no rating for this sport.

`play_intent_not_declared` — you have not said what kind of evening you are after for it.

`player_profile_not_committed` — there is no profile to read a radius, a grid or an area from.

`rung_offer_not_found` — you cited a rung no search of yours offered.

`locked_seat_not_available` — somebody you seated by hand cannot be seated in this line-up. **Which one is deliberately not said.** Completing a challenge, this means somebody on your court has been blocked, held or deactivated since they accepted — re-read the challenge.

`challenge_not_yours_to_fill` — the challenge you named is not one of yours to complete. **One code for three cases**: no such challenge, you hold no live seat on it, or nobody is arranging it any more.

503.description: `matchmaking_unavailable`, `gate_data_unavailable`, `index_too_stale`, `search_not_recorded`. The second one covers the **pairwise block mask**: a four is never seated on a gate that could not be evaluated.

post.description:
Returns every arrangement of a four **you** put together, each with its own forecast — for the builder, where you swap somebody in and the number has to move.

**This creates no search and records nothing.** Six swaps are not six searches, and recording them as such would put a lie in the one table the product judges itself by. There is no `search_id` in the response and nothing to read back.

**Seats may be empty.** A side with one player is read as if the missing player matched the one already there; the forecast comes back `provisional` with its `assumption`, and the moment you fill the seat the number is **exactly** the same as the final one.

**It is bound to a search you ran.** Every player you name must have appeared in that search's returned rows.

**No forecast arithmetic belongs on the client.** Every figure the builder can show comes from here or from `/lineups`.

200.description: Every arrangement of the four you composed, each with its own forecast. **Provisional while a seat is empty**, and the provisional figure becomes exactly the final figure the moment the seat fills.

403.description: `account_held` — this account is under a live hold.

404.description: `search_not_found` — no search of yours showed all of those players. **One code for four cases**: the search does not exist, it is somebody else's, it was for another sport, or it never showed one of these people. Telling them apart would answer questions about strangers one probe at a time.

409.description: `sport_not_rated`, `play_intent_not_declared`, `player_profile_not_committed` — the same three the search route owes, for the same reason: a forecast puts **you** on the court.

503.description:
`gate_data_unavailable` — blocks and holds are re-read live and a gate that cannot be evaluated excludes.

`matchmaking_unavailable` — the engine raised.

get.description:
**Outgoing and mutuals only.** There is no inbox: a yes nobody has answered stays silent, in both directions, which is what makes saying yes low-stakes. You are never told that somebody declined you, and you are never shown who said yes to you unless you said it back.

**Every outgoing row carries its own `expires_at`**, so the screen can show what is still live without knowing the window.

**`outstanding` carries the count, the cap and `ttl_days` for every sport**, before you are near either — a cap you cannot see is a refusal you cannot predict, and how long a yes lives is the number the deck's ending prints. Render these; never hardcode the numbers.

200.description: Your outgoing yeses, the ones that came back, and where each sport stands against its cap.

503.description: `gate_data_unavailable` — the block set could not be evaluated, so the list is refused rather than served unverified.

post.description:
One tap, costing nothing — and it actually does something: you rise in that player's next search for this sport, **with the reason printed**, so the lift is never mistaken for a match.

**Nobody is notified.** A one-sided yes is silent and stays silent. It becomes visible only when the other person goes looking for a game.

**`search_id` is required.** It says which search surfaced this person — a yes citing a search that is unknown, that is somebody else's or that never showed them is refused, never recorded with an empty link.

**Idempotent.** Tapping again returns the same yes with the same expiry, at `200`.

**It lapses.** Every yes carries its own `expires_at`; when it passes the yes is simply gone, and that person may be dealt to you again. **Never compute the expiry yourself** — the window is ruleset configuration and does not cross the wire as a number.

201.description: The yes stands, and it is new. It lapses at `expires_at`, which was dated the moment it was created.

200.description: You had already said this. **Nothing was created and nothing was extended** — the yes comes back with the expiry it was born with.

409.description:
`origin_search_not_found` — no search of **yours** showed that player for that sport. The origin key is refused rather than linked as null.

`outstanding_interest_cap_reached` — you already have the most yeses in flight this sport allows. **Nothing of yours is shortened to make room**; wait, or one of them comes back. The count and the cap are on `GET /api/v1/interest`.

post.description:
Deals one batch of cards: one judgement at a time, no mode to pick and no setup.

**No mode, in either direction, and no declaration read.** Every deal scores under the same ruler for every viewer — shared tags lead, overlap second, a wide level window — whatever either of you declared, and a player who never declared is dealt without being asked to. On every card `INTENT_ALIGNMENT` is in `degraded_terms` as `NOT_READ_ON_THIS_SURFACE`, which is the surface's doing and says nothing about the person.

**Send `availability_override` if the player edited their week**, and the deal runs on it; omit it and the grid on the profile is used. It writes nothing: the deal comes back with a `KEEP_THESE_TIMES` prompt, and saving is a separate request the player makes. **A cleared week is a legal value** — unticking every cell deals a deck rather than being refused.

**A spent deal deals again.** Post again for a new deal with a new `search_id`; running out of cards is not running out of people, and only a fresh deal that comes back empty means the pool is thin. `pool.remaining` says how many eligible people are beyond this hand, and drops as hands are dealt.

**`pool.want_to_play_you`** says how many people have a live *Let's play* towards you that would be dealt — a count, never a list, and `0` when nobody is waiting. Somebody who said yes to you is dealt **unmarked**: they carry `inclusion_reason: INTEREST_LIFT` and nothing else says so, and they sit where their lift puts them rather than first by rule.

**Somebody you already have a court with is not dealt** — a live challenge or game, and for the cool-off after it is behind you, which is a ruleset window (thirty days at release) and never crosses the wire. Find a game still lists them.

**The order is the deck's variety**: the people Liveness lifted, the ones who said yes among them, then the rest. There is no re-sort — `sorts_available` is empty here, because a deck is one card at a time.

**No widening is offered.** `rung_offers` is `null` on a deal: the relaxation ladder belongs to the shortlist.

**Read it back** through `GET /api/v1/searches/{id}`, in this same shape, minus the two counts — they are true of the moment the hand was dealt.

200.description: One deal: an ordered batch of at most ten cards, sharing one `search_id`. **An empty deal is also a 200** — a fresh deal that came back with nothing is the honest empty state, and the pool it came from is described either way.

403.description: `account_held` — this account is under a live hold.

409.description:
`sport_not_rated` — you hold no rating for this sport.

`player_profile_not_committed` — there is no profile to read a radius, a grid or an area from.

**Never `play_intent_not_declared`**: the deck reads no declaration, so a player who never made one is dealt without being asked to.

503.description: `matchmaking_unavailable`, `gate_data_unavailable`, `index_too_stale`, `search_not_recorded` — four distinct codes at one status, so a client can tell a transient outage from a refusal about *you*.

post.description:
Deals your deck whole again, for one sport.

**Three things lift at once, and only for this sport**: every *Not today* you gave, the people you were dealt today, and the cool-off on anybody you have had a court with. The next `POST /deck` deals all of them. What stays: the people you have a live *Let's play* on are still yours to wait on, another sport's deck is untouched, and the record that you once passed on somebody is kept — a card you see again is still one you have seen.

**Idempotent.** Pressing it twice in a row is one press.

**Nobody is told**, and nothing is returned. The only place a reset shows is your own next deal.

204.description: Cleared. **Nothing is returned** — the next deal is where the difference shows.

403.description: `account_held` — this account is under a live hold.

409.description: `sport_not_rated` — you hold no rating for this sport, so there is no deck of yours to deal again.

post.description:
Every player rated in this sport inside your reach, at their distance and bearing — the population the deck deals from, with the deck's reach and none of its judgement.

**The sport is the whole ask.** No mode (every pairing scores under the deck's ruler), no radius (the reach is your own Search radius — there is no city), no position (the server holds your area), no week.

**Five gates and nothing after them.** Blocked either way, under a hold, disabled, a gender preference either way, and rated in the sport — then everyone inside the circle is drawn, each with a `fit` printed as served. No level band, no quality floor, no cool-off, no pass memory, no dealt memory: somebody you have a court with, somebody you said *not today* to and somebody you are matched with are all on the radar.

**Each row carries `bearing_deg` beside `distance_km`** — north `0`, clockwise, spot to spot, served and never derived — and `ratings[]`, every sport the player is rated in with their Level. Both are on the row and never inside `player_card`. The rows are ordered by distance and then by id, so a position means something.

**`pool.want_to_play_you` is the deck's number.** Computed by the deck's own rule — its gates and its exclusions — so the chip here and the chip on the deck are one number; omitted at zero. Somebody who said yes to you whom the deck would never deal is still drawn, carrying `inclusion_reason: INTEREST_LIFT`, and is not counted.

**A reading is not a deal.** It never enters the dealt memory: browse on Monday and do nothing, and Tuesday's deck deals the same people. Only an answer reaches the deck — `POST /interest` and `POST /passes` take this `search_id` exactly as they take a deal's — and after either the person **stays on the radar**.

**Read it back** through `GET /api/v1/searches/{id}`, in this same shape, minus the chip — it is true of the moment the reading ran.

200.description: One reading: every player the radar may draw for you in this sport, ordered by distance and then id, sharing one `search_id`. **An empty reading is also a 200** — nobody rated in this sport inside your reach is an answer, and the pool it came from is described either way.

403.description: `account_held` — this account is under a live hold.

409.description:
`sport_not_rated` — you hold no rating for this sport.

`player_profile_not_committed` — there is no profile to read a radius or an area from.

**Never `play_intent_not_declared`**: like the deck, the radar reads no declaration.

503.description: `matchmaking_unavailable`, `gate_data_unavailable`, `index_too_stale`, `search_not_recorded` — four distinct codes at one status, so a client can tell a transient outage from a refusal about *you*. A gate that cannot be evaluated refuses the whole reading rather than drawing anybody it could not check.

post.description:
Keeps somebody out of **your deck** for a while, and reaches nothing else.

**It is not a block, and it never becomes one.** You will still find that person in a shortlist tomorrow if you change your mind; it never touches their deck, and passing twice buys exactly the same window as passing once. The control that removes a person from a person is `POST /api/v1/blocks`, and it is meant to be the heavier gesture.

**Nobody is told.** Not them, not you: no count, no list, no *show them again*.

**`search_id` is required** — it says which deal this card came from.

204.description: Recorded. **Nothing is returned, and nothing ever will be** — there is no route through which a pass reaches anybody, including you.

409.description: `origin_search_not_found` — no search of **yours** showed that player for that sport. The origin is refused rather than linked as null.

post.description:
Stops a question being raised at you again for a while, and reaches nothing else.

**It changes no value.** Saying *yes* to one of these is a `PUT` through the route that owns the value — your radius, your week, your play intent — and this is what the other button does.

**It retires nothing**, including itself: the question standing right now still expires on its own, and this is about the next time it would have been asked.

**It is keyed by the question and never by the value quoted at you.** Declining *keep 22 km?* also answers *keep 32 km?* — you answered about a habit, not about a number. Which sport it goes quiet for depends on the question: a play intent is declared per sport, while your radius and your week are one fact each.

**There is no `search_id`** and no window to name.

204.description: Recorded. **Nothing is returned** — there is no route through which a decline reaches anybody, including you.

409.description: `prompt_does_not_suppress` — *Keep these times?* is asked again on the next search, because the week you improvised is a different week next Tuesday. It is the one prompt with no *not now*.

get.description:
**Sent and received in one list.** *Challenge sent* and *Challenge for you* are one standing read from two sides; tell them apart by whether `organiser_id` is yours.

**The standing is derived, never stored.** It is folded from the seats and the clock at the moment you asked, so a seat whose day ran out reads as lapsed whether or not anything has swept it yet.

**Ended challenges are here too**, carrying `DECLINED`, `LAPSED`, `WITHDRAWN` or `CALLED_OFF`. A list that quietly dropped this morning's is a list that lies.

**Except the one you cleared yourself.** A `CALLED_OFF` row whose game you dismissed (`POST /games/{game_id}/dismissal`) is left off this list as it is left off `GET /games`: one court, one act, and both of your lists read the same set. Nobody else's list moves.

**This is also the remedy for `open_challenge_stands`.** A refused send names nobody; read this to find out which of your own open games is in the way.

200.description: Every challenge you hold a seat in, newest first, each with what it is right now.

post.description:
**One act, everybody at once.** A doubles send is one challenge containing four people, answered by each of them separately — never three separate invitations.

**Your own seat is accepted from birth.** You are the one proposing, so nothing asks whether you want to play the game you just built.

**Each invitee gets 48 hours from when *their* seat was invited**, so a seat filled later is not already half expired.

**The arrangement you built is what is recorded**, and it is what they answer — never a better one worked out afterwards.

**Everything is re-checked here**, in one transaction, because your line-up may be an hour old and nothing refetches it in the background. The send either happens whole or writes nothing at all: there is no partial send that quietly drops one person.

**The sport, the kind of evening and the week come from the search**, not from this request. There is no window picker anywhere — you change your window by changing your grid.

201.description: The challenge stands, and everybody on the court has been asked.

403.description: `account_held` — **your** account is under a live hold. The same code a search returns, and refused at the entry point: a hold that stops you searching but lets you send invitations is the same hole with the blast radius pointed at other people.

400.description:
`challenge_with_no_invitee`, `organiser_holds_a_seat`, `one_person_to_a_seat`, `cannot_challenge_yourself` — who is on the court, and every one of them a caller's bug. Checked **first, before anything is read**, because they are true regardless of anybody else's state: telling an organiser their line-up went stale when they invited nobody sends them refreshing a screen that was never wrong.

`court_is_not_the_sports` — the seats are not `2 x seats_per_side`, evenly split, in the court's own order. The one refusal in that family that cannot come first: the shape is the sport's, and the sport is the search's to say.

409.description:
`court_origin_not_found` — no search of yours showed all of those players. One code for four cases, on purpose.

`line_up_no_longer_sendable` — somebody on this court can no longer be invited to it. **Which one is deliberately not said, and neither is why.** Re-read the origin search: its read-back re-evaluates the same gates and marks the seats. **Do not re-run the search** — that mints a new `search_id` the whole line-up must adopt, and its untouched seats are only *probably* in the new answer.

`open_challenge_stands` — two people on this court already have a game between them, **in any sport**. Read your own challenges to find out who; an open game of yours was always yours to read.

503.description: `challenge_gates_unavailable` — a safety gate could not be read, so nothing was minted. Transient and about the platform: retry the same request.

get.description:
**The screen you answer on.** The list tells you what you have been asked; this tells you who is asking and what this platform makes of playing them.

**The pairing is computed when you open this, in your own direction.** Nothing is copied at send and nothing is replayed from the organiser's search — which is why a challenge born of a mutual yes draws the same screen as one built from a shortlist, and why the Fit here is genuinely yours.

**The card block is drawn while the arrangement is being decided and at no other time.** A challenge that ended draws its arrangement and the names alone, and so does the seat of somebody who declined or lapsed inside one that is still open: they have left, and that person is a stranger to you again.

**Answering is never gated on any of it.** If the pairing cannot be computed — you hold no rating in this sport, or something the matcher needs could not be read — `pairing_absence` says which, the arrangement answers as always, and the buttons are drawn from the standing.

**Nothing here is re-checked against who is reading.** The safety gates ran when this challenge was minted, in both directions, and they are not run again.

200.description: The arrangement, the people on it, and what you make of each of them.

404.description: `challenge_not_found` — no challenge of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you are not on its court — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about a stranger's evening.

post.description:
**Your yes matters on its own**, and is not conditional on the other seats: the conversation opens on the *first* acceptance and grows with each one, so there is no waiting room and no single moment where the game becomes real.

**The seat is not in the path** because you hold at most one in any challenge — and nobody may answer for anybody else.

The challenge reads `ON` once **every** seat is accepted, with no special case for the organiser and none for singles.

200.description: Your seat is accepted, and the challenge as it now stands.

404.description: `challenge_not_found` — no challenge of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you are not on its court — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about a stranger's evening.

409.description:
`seat_already_answered` — you have answered this one. **Not idempotent, deliberately**: *yes* after *no* is a different answer and not a repeat of one.

`answer_window_has_passed` — your day ran out. The seat already reads as lapsed and may have been offered to somebody else, so an answer that resurrected it would contradict a card the platform has already drawn.

`game_moment_has_passed` — **on a court somebody left**, the moment the plan agreed has passed, so a yes now would seat you into a game whose moment is gone. `game_is_history` — that game has happened, or never will. Neither is reachable on a court that was never a game.

`challenge_is_over` — the organiser removed this challenge while your day was still running. Your seat has nothing of its own to refuse, and the court is over; the answer is refused rather than recorded on a challenge nobody is arranging any more.

post.description:
**Your no is about you.** It reopens exactly your seat and disturbs nothing else: the people who already agreed did nothing wrong and are still in the game, and the organiser may offer your seat to somebody else.

**Nobody is told you declined**, and no response anywhere names you as having done so.

**Saying nothing is not this.** Silence past your day is a *lapse*, which is a different fact and is counted apart — the platform never files it as a judgement you made.

200.description: Your seat is open again, and the challenge as it now stands.

404.description: `challenge_not_found` — no challenge of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you are not on its court — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about a stranger's evening.

409.description:
`seat_already_answered` — you have answered this one. **Not idempotent, deliberately**: *yes* after *no* is a different answer and not a repeat of one.

`answer_window_has_passed` — your day ran out. The seat already reads as lapsed and may have been offered to somebody else, so an answer that resurrected it would contradict a card the platform has already drawn.

`game_moment_has_passed` — **on a court somebody left**, the moment the plan agreed has passed, so a yes now would seat you into a game whose moment is gone. `game_is_history` — that game has happened, or never will. Neither is reachable on a court that was never a game.

`challenge_is_over` — the organiser removed this challenge while your day was still running. Your seat has nothing of its own to refuse, and the court is over; the answer is refused rather than recorded on a challenge nobody is arranging any more.

post.description:
**Grows a court that is already standing**, from a line-up you just built. The people who accepted keep their places and their answers; the open seats are offered to the people you name.

**Any live member may do this** — growing a court and ending one are different acts: removing a challenge is the organiser's while nobody has joined and nobody's once somebody has, and calling off the game a court became is any player's on it. A challenge born of two mutual yeses has an organiser who is only whoever said yes second, and leaving the other one unable to finish the four would make an arbitrary tiebreak decide whose game it is. Somebody who declined or let their day run out is **not** a live member.

**Post the whole court, not the new seats.** An acceptance is to the game and not to the side, so you may move somebody across the net — and you may never take them out.

**Each newly seated player gets their own 48 hours**, dated from this moment. A seat filled later is not already half expired, and nobody's existing deadline moves.

**The window is not re-stamped.** The week this challenge was proposed for was fixed when it was sent, and a challenge born of a mutual yes has none at all — the plan, not the window, is what says when anybody actually plays.

**Everything is re-checked here**, in one transaction, exactly as a send is: the four fail-closed gates over the whole court, and the open-challenge rule with **this** challenge excepted and no other. The fill either happens whole or writes nothing.

**Somebody who let your invitation run out is out of this court's own pool, and out of nothing else.** Nobody is asked twice on one challenge, so they are not a candidate for this fill for as long as this court stands — and asking them again is a **new** challenge rather than a seat on this one. Every **other** search of yours reaches them immediately, in any sport: their seat reopened and the open-challenge rule released them with it.

200.description: The seats are filled and the court is returned as it now stands. Everybody newly seated has their **own** day from this moment.

404.description: `challenge_not_found` — no challenge of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you are not on its court — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about a stranger's evening.

403.description:
`account_held` — **your** account is under a live hold, and a hold that let you invite people would be the same hole with the blast radius pointed at them.

`fill_is_the_live_members` — you hold a seat on this court and you have left it. **Not a 404**: your own seat is still drawn on the challenge, so pretending it is not there would be the wrong lie.

400.description:
`challenge_with_no_invitee`, `organiser_holds_a_seat`, `one_person_to_a_seat`, `cannot_challenge_yourself` — who is on the court, and every one of them a caller's bug. Checked **first, before anything is read**, because they are true regardless of anybody else's state: telling an organiser their line-up went stale when they invited nobody sends them refreshing a screen that was never wrong.

`court_is_not_the_sports` — the seats are not `2 x seats_per_side`, evenly split, in the court's own order. The one refusal in that family that cannot come first: the shape is the sport's, and the sport is the search's to say.

409.description:
`court_origin_not_found` — no search of yours showed all of the people you are newly asking. One code for four cases, on purpose. **The people already on the court are not looked up in it**, so a court that keeps them is not refused for them.

`line_up_no_longer_sendable` — somebody on this court can no longer be invited to it. **Which one is deliberately not said, and neither is why.** Re-read the challenge and the origin search.

`open_challenge_stands` — two people on this court already have a game between them **in any sport**, and it is not this one: this court's own pairs are excepted, and no other challenge is.

`nobody_new_to_invite` — every seat on the court you posted is already taken by somebody in the game. **The court is not grown, and nothing is written.**

`nobody_is_asked_twice` — somebody on that court has already answered this challenge. Unreachable through the builder, which does not offer them; this is the aggregate's backstop.

`accepted_player_may_not_be_removed` — a court that dropped somebody who is already in.

`challenge_is_over` — this challenge has ended.

`game_moment_has_passed`, `game_is_history` — **on a court somebody left**: the game's agreed moment has passed, or the game has happened or never will, so nobody may be seated into it. Neither is reachable on a court that was never a game.

503.description: `challenge_gates_unavailable` — a safety gate could not be read, so nothing was minted. Transient and about the platform: retry the same request.

post.description:
**Remove the challenge** — the organiser's act on a court that was never a game, and admitted exactly while **nobody besides the organiser holds an accepted seat**: before anybody has answered, and again once everybody who joined has left — whatever seats are still deciding. The moment somebody has joined it is refused: a court somebody has joined is nobody's to end for the others, so from then on the organiser leaves it like anybody else, and it is over by itself when nobody is on it, or one player is and nobody is still deciding. The invitees' challenges read `WITHDRAWN` and offer no answer — a yes or a no on a removed challenge is refused with `challenge_is_over` — and an invitation whose day was still running is neither answered nor unanswered: it leaves the record that prices silence, and the lapse loop writes nothing for it.

**A court that has been a game has no exit anybody presses.** *Call it off* lived on this route and is gone: no player's single decision ends a game for the others. Such a court is called off by the departure that leaves at most one player on it, or by its hour when it is still short of a player — `CALLED_OFF`, with `ended_by` the leaver or nobody — and asking this of it is refused with `court_has_been_a_game`.

**Whole-challenge, and it never removes one person.** A withdraw ends the arrangement for everybody on it, and taking one person out of a court that still stands is refused here as it is everywhere else.

**Irreversible.** There is no route back. Asking the same people again is a **new** challenge, with fresh deadlines and its own record of who has answered — which is what it actually is. That a removal can be followed by a resend to the same person, on a fresh clock, is a named and accepted risk with its falsifier written down.

**What this releases is the people on the court.** A send holds its pairs for as long as an answer is owed; this is that exit. Somebody who let their day run out needed none: their seat reopened and the open-challenge rule released them with it.

**A noun and not a verb**, because what this creates is the ending — the withdrawal, one of the two things in this context that a fold of the seats could never produce. The conversation is destroyed in the act where one exists: there is none before anybody has answered, and there may be one the organiser is alone in again.

200.description: The challenge is over, and it is returned as it now stands — `WITHDRAWN`, `ended_by` naming you — with every seat exactly as it was: a seat still awaiting an answer keeps its question and its deadline, and the standing is read before either.

404.description: `challenge_not_found` — no challenge of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you are not on its court — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about a stranger's evening.

403.description: `withdraw_is_the_organisers` — you hold a seat on this court and the act is not yours: removing the challenge is the organiser's alone, and an organiser who left their own seat holds none. **Not a 404**: you can already see this challenge, so pretending it is not there while your own seat is drawn on it would be the wrong lie.

409.description:
`court_has_been_a_game` — this court became a game, and such a court is nobody's to end for the others, its organiser included. It ends by its players leaving — the departure that leaves at most one player on it calls the game off — or by its hour, when it is still short of a player as its moment passes.

`somebody_has_joined` — somebody besides you holds an accepted seat, so it is no longer yours to remove for the others. Leave it instead (`POST /challenges/{id}/departure`); it ends by itself when nobody is on it, or one is with nobody deciding.

`challenge_is_over` — this challenge has ended, this act included: a second press meets it.

post.description:
**You are out of a court you had agreed to** — a game, or a court that is not whole yet. Your seat reopens on the challenge; where the court had become a game, that game survives with your seat drawn empty, and the people still on it keep what they agreed — the plan, the room, the record. Anyone still on the court may fill your seat the way a half-built court is filled, and the newcomer's yes re-seats the **same** game.

**Any player on the court, the organiser included**, while the court stands — and, on a game, while it is awaiting its entry and its agreed moment is ahead or no moment is agreed yet. Once the moment has passed, leaving means nothing and is refused; a court that is not a game has no moment to guard.

**A court is over when at most one player is on it and no seat is awaiting an answer**, and the organiser is a player in that rule. Before a game the challenge ends by itself — as `DECLINED`, because a departure is a no — and its room with it. On a game, the departure that leaves one player on it **ends the court with its game** in this request: the challenge reads `CALLED_OFF` naming you, `GET /games` reads `CALLED_OFF` naming you, and the room is gone. Singles included: an opponent who leaves calls the game off — for the person they leave, too.

**You are out of this court's own pool for as long as it stands.** Nobody is asked twice on one challenge; being asked again is a **new** challenge. Every other search reaches you at once — the pair rule released you the moment you left.

**The others are told**: the room draws *{name} left — that seat is open again*, and your own list and inbox no longer hold the game or the room.

**Two people may leave**, and two seats may be open. Nothing here prices a departure yet — it is recorded, with its moment, and that is all.

**A noun and not a verb**, like the withdrawal: what this creates is the departure.

200.description: Your seat is open again, and the challenge as it now stands. `LINE_UP_INCOMPLETE` where the others are in — on a game, that game survives with your seat empty; `AWAITING_ANSWERS` where somebody is still deciding; `DECLINED` where the court was never a game and your leaving deserted it — **a court is over when nobody is on it, or one player is and no seat is awaiting an answer** — and a departure is a no; and `CALLED_OFF` where your leaving deserted a court that has been a game: the last but one with nobody deciding, or the last, whoever is still deciding — the court ends with its game, `ended_by` you, and the game is called off in this same request — `GET /games` reads it `CALLED_OFF` with `called_off_by` you, and the room is gone.

404.description: `challenge_not_found` — no challenge of **yours** has that id, or you hold no **accepted** seat on it. One code for three cases: it does not exist, you are not on its court, or your seat is awaiting, declined, lapsed or already left — because a departure is the one act whose refusal must not confirm that you *were* on this court a moment ago.

403.description: `account_held` — **your** account is under a live hold. A departure writes a line into a room other people are in, which is reach.

409.description:
`challenge_is_over` — this challenge has ended.

`game_is_history` — the game has happened, was called off, or its entry window closed on silence. The line-up is the record of an evening, and nothing on it moves.

`game_moment_has_passed` — the moment the plan agreed has passed. Leaving would mean nothing now, and a no-show cannot vacate a seat to block the result. **Only where there is a game**: a half-built court may carry a plan naming a moment, and has no moment to guard.

There is no `not_a_game_yet` any more: a yes can be taken back before the court is whole.

503.description: `challenge_gates_unavailable` — a safety gate could not be read, so nothing was minted. Transient and about the platform: retry the same request.

post.description:
**Clear a called-off court from your own two lists**, met from the Chats row — the same act `POST /games/{game_id}/dismissal` is from the Now card, recorded on the same game, read by both lists (`docs/adr/0173`, `docs/adr/0175` §5). Yours alone: nobody else's lists move, and the game, its record and the challenge are untouched. It is instant and there is no undo — a mis-tap loses the row and the card and nothing else, which is why there is no sheet.

**For everybody the court asked.** The card's trash is admitted for players on the game; the row is drawn for everybody with a seat on the challenge, answered or not — an invitee still deciding on a fill when the court was called off has a row and never had a card — so this door admits anybody holding a seat, and hands the act to the game on the court's word.

**Only on a court that is `CALLED_OFF`**, refused with its own code on every other standing.
