**A noun and not a verb**, like the card's: what this creates is the dismissal, and it answers nothing because the thing a redraw would draw is the thing you removed.

204.description: The court is cleared from your Chats — and its card from your Now, where it had one — on this device and every other, and nothing else moves. A second press answers the same and writes nothing.

404.description: `challenge_not_found` — no challenge of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you are not on its court — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about a stranger's evening.

409.description: `court_is_not_called_off` — only a called-off court's row can be removed. A live court's row is the court, and the other endings' rows are the record for the day they stay.

get.description:
**A room opens on the first acceptance and grows with each one after it.** A doubles court whose line-up is still filling draws the members it has, not the court it will be.

**Ordered by the last entry, newest first.** A room where nothing has happened yet carries `last_entry: null` and orders on the moment it opened — the opening writes no line, so there is genuinely nothing there yet.

**No state pill and no standing.** The last entry is what a pill would have said; a standing beside it would be a second place for one fact to be true. The state-keyed surfaces are the challenge screen and the game screen.

**Only live rooms are here, because there are only live rooms.** A conversation is destroyed rather than delisted once the episode it was opened for is over — deliberately the opposite of `GET /challenges`, which keeps ended challenges and says so. The difference is the difference between a record and a room.

**This is one of two reads for the Chats tab, and they are not merged.** `GET /challenges` is the other. Two sections, two contexts, two queries, two caches.

200.description: Every room you are a member of, the ones that moved last first.

get.description:
**The header and the newest page in one response**, folded against one instant, so the members you are holding and the entries you are drawing can never disagree about who is in the room.

**Open at the newest entry and page backward** from `entries[0].seq` through `/entries`. You have the whole conversation when you hold `seq` 1 — there is no `has_more`, because a gapless sequence makes `seq` 1 the beginning.

**Nothing here is re-evaluated against you.** The safety gates ran when the challenge was minted; a read that re-ran them would tell you something changed about somebody else.

**`people` is everybody this response names and `members` is the roster.** Fill every `{name}` and every author label from `people`: the actor of a `SEAT_LEFT` line is by definition no longer a member, and a client naming off the roster alone drew *? said no*.

200.description: The room's header and its newest page, from one fold.

`conversation_not_found` — **one code for two cases**: there is no room with that id, or there is one and you are not in it. They are not told apart on purpose, because a 403 would answer *is this id real* about a stranger's evening.

Leave the screen. There is no retry that changes this.

get.description:
**A cursor over `seq`, never an offset.** One code path serves history and catch-up: a client that has been away and finds a hole below the newest page walks backward through this route until it reaches its own high-water mark.

**`before_seq` is exclusive**, and omitting it asks for the newest page.

**No header and no `read_at` here.** A page of entries is folded against nothing — every entry carries its own moment — so a second instant would be a second clock to reconcile against the one the detail read gave you.

**But every page carries the faces of whoever it names.** `people` is every author and actor on this page and nothing about the roster; merge it into what you hold, because the people a page names are not the members — the one who said no is on the page and off the court.

post.description:
**`200`, not `201`, and the message comes back.** A repeat carrying the same `client_message_id` answers with the same message and the same `seq`, and records nothing — so a send that paused offline and resumed can never become two bubbles.

**The message is returned rather than refetched**, which is also what keeps your own message off the live channel's round trip.

**It has no id of its own.** `(conversation_id, seq)` identifies it.

200.description: The message as it was recorded — **or, on a repeat, the one that already stands.**

400.description:
`message_is_empty` — nothing but whitespace.

`message_is_too_long` — past the cap. **Refused, never truncated**: a shortened message is one you believe you sent whole, in front of other people.

403.description: `account_held` — your account is under a live hold. **A hold stops you writing anywhere another player sees it, and never stops you reading**: every read on this context stays open to you, because a hold must not erase an arrangement other people are already inside.

404.description:
`conversation_not_found` — **one code for two cases**: there is no room with that id, or there is one and you are not in it. They are not told apart on purpose, because a 403 would answer *is this id real* about a stranger's evening.

Leave the screen. There is no retry that changes this.

post.description:
**A heartbeat, not a state.** Post this while somebody is typing and stop posting when they stop — about every 3 seconds. There is deliberately no *stopped* call, because a *stopped* that never arrives — the app is killed, the phone loses signal, the request is dropped — would leave a room with an indicator nothing could ever clear.

**What clears it is the server's own 5-second expiry**, so the failure mode is the indicator vanishing rather than sticking. Keep the cadence under that expiry or your own indicator flickers on people who are still typing.

**It records nothing durable and moves no sequence.** The room's `last_seq` is exactly what it was, however many of these you post — a typing frame is not an entry, and nothing here appends, locks or commits.

**No rate limit, and none is planned.** Writing the same key repeatedly is idempotent and cheap, and the expiry is what bounds it.

**It carries no body.** What is being typed is nobody's business until it is sent.

204.description: Recorded. Also the answer when you were already recorded as typing — the heartbeat is idempotent and re-posting it is the cheapest thing this route does.

403.description: `account_held` — your account is under a live hold. **A hold stops you writing anywhere another player sees it**, and an indicator in somebody else's room is somewhere another player sees it. Every read on this context stays open to you.

404.description:
`conversation_not_found` — **one code for two cases**: there is no room with that id, or there is one and you are not in it. They are not told apart on purpose, because a 403 would answer *is this id real* about a stranger's evening.

Leave the screen. There is no retry that changes this.

get.description:
**Two named events, and you subscribe per name.** `nudge` says the room moved; `typing` says somebody is typing. The kind is on the SSE `event:` field rather than inside the JSON, so an event name you have never heard of is ignored by construction — which is what makes a third one, one day, additive for a phone that shipped today.

**A `nudge` is `{ v, conversation_id, last_seq }` and nothing else.** On receiving one, fetch from **your own** high-water mark through `GET /conversations/{id}/entries` — never from `last_seq`.

**A `typing` is `{ v, conversation_id, player_ids }`, and it moves no cursor of any kind.** It is not an entry, carries no `seq`, and the room's `last_seq` is unaffected by it. It arrives when the answer changes and not on a timer, **you are never in it**, and an empty `player_ids` is how an indicator goes away. There is no *stopped* signal anywhere: the server reports whoever's heartbeat has not expired, so a killed app clears within 5 seconds by doing nothing at all.

**`v` does not move for the new event.** A client that listens only for `nudge` is entirely unaffected by this addition, which is why the envelope version says `1` on both.

**A dropped frame costs nothing.** Because you fetch from your own cursor and not from the frame's number, the *next* nudge repairs whatever the lost one would have said. There is nothing to detect and nothing to reconcile.

**One `nudge` arrives the moment the stream opens**, carrying the room's current `last_seq`. That is what makes resume correct without `Last-Event-ID` being load-bearing, and it is how a client that has been away catches up in one step.

**The stream closes when your access token expires** — about every fifteen minutes. Reconnect with a fresh one through your ordinary refresh path; the token travels in the `Authorization` header, never a query string.

**A closed stream means the room is not live, and nothing more.** It closes on token expiry, on a deploy, and when this server's own subscriber cannot be reached — deliberately, so that a chat which is not live *looks* not-live instead of looking up to date. Every read on this context keeps working throughout; only the latency changes.

**Close it when the app backgrounds and re-open on foreground.** iOS severs a backgrounded app's connections, and re-opening is the same code path as any other reconnect.

200.description: An open `text/event-stream`. Two named events ride it: `nudge` carries a `LiveNudgeSchema` and `typing` carries a `LiveTypingSchema`. **Subscribe per name**; a name you do not know is not yours to render.

Leave the screen. There is no retry that changes this.

get.description:
**Arranged, played and finished in one list.** A game awaiting an entry, one awaiting an answer and one that never happened are one thing at three moments of its life.

**The standing is derived, never stored.** It is folded from the record and the clock at the moment you asked, so a game whose entry window ran out reads as never played whether or not anything has swept it — nothing sweeps it, because there is nothing for a sweep to correct.

**`read_at` is the instant every standing and deadline here was folded against.** Render your countdowns from it, so they cannot disagree with the standing beside them.

**A called-off game you have dismissed is not here** (`POST /games/{id}/dismissal`), on this device and every other — the dismissal is recorded on the game, once, and subtracted on every read.

200.description: Every game you were on the court of, newest arrangement first, each with what it is right now.

get.description:
**The game screen's forecast, split, stakes and Levels, computed when you ask.** Nothing here is stored on the game, and nothing on `GET /games` changes: a seat there still carries a name and nothing else.

**Read in your direction.** `split.gap` is your side's strength minus theirs, and `at_stake` is what a counted result would do to *your* Level — the rating engine's own rule read forward, side against side, so it is the pair the result will deliver.

**Three blocks, each omitted on its own ground.** `forecast` and `split` are omitted together when the pairing cannot be computed — somebody on the court holds no rating in the sport, or a seat could not be priced — and there is deliberately no reason beside the absence. `at_stake` is omitted on a friendly, where a counted result is meaningless rather than unavailable, and where the rule has nothing to move or nothing to price against — you hold no rating in the sport, or nobody across the net does. `seats` names the Level of everybody the platform holds one for.

**Only while the game is awaiting an entry.** After *we played* — or after the entry window closed on silence — the route refuses, because a pairing is a claim about a game that has not happened.

200.description: What this platform makes of your court, computed for you at `read_at`.

404.description: `game_not_found` — no game of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you were not on its court — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about four strangers' evening.

409.description: `pairing_is_history` — the game has happened, or its entry window closed on silence. The pairing means what a card means *because this game has not happened*; afterwards the values would be a claim about people made from a record that has moved on.

post.description:
**One act, and the record decides what it means.** Send the score you believe was played:

- nothing on the table yet → you are saying *we played, here is the score*, and **that entry is what records that the game happened**. There is no date to send: the moment of the entry is the moment.
- your own side's score on the table, unanswered → a **correction**, free, and not a second turn. Any of your side may make it, not only whoever typed first.
- the other side's score on the table → your side's **one** disagreement, and it carries a score because there is no bare rejection.

**A lone score is confirmed by silence** when its 24 hours run out, and the game counts. **Two scores nobody accepts leave the game unscored** — which still counts as an evening you played and moves nobody's Level.

**Nobody is penalised for any of this.** Not for saying nothing, not for disagreeing, not for a disagreement the other side ignored.

200.description: The game as it stands with your score on the table.

403.description: `you_were_not_on_this_court` — no game of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you did not play in it — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about four strangers' evening.

409.description:
Everything above, plus:

`your_side_has_already_answered` — one score per side. The cap is what bounds an argument to two rounds, and what makes silence safe to read as agreement.

`the_other_side_has_answered` — correcting is free until they respond and not afterwards. `acceptance.agreed_at` is when they did, so the sentence a player reads need not be vague about it.

`the_court_has_an_open_seat` — somebody left and nobody has filled their seat, so there is no court to have played on. Fill it, or let the window close.

`the_game_was_called_off` — somebody ended it while a seat was open, so there is nothing to have played. The ending is on `standing` and `called_off_at`.

`the_game_started_short` — a booked game whose hour came with a seat open: somebody left after the club's cut-off and nobody took the seat. It ends uncounted (`standing` `STARTED_SHORT`), and nothing about it can be recorded.

`a_no_show_is_reported` — somebody was reported as not coming to this booked game and their day to dispute it runs (`no_shows`): the game does not count, so there is no score to enter.

400.description:
`a_result_must_carry_a_score` — an objection with nothing in it. There is no bare rejection here: a rejection carrying no score is free and always optimal for the loser.

`a_score_must_name_a_winner` — a level set, or a match level in sets. None of the four sports produces a draw, and *Last 5* has no third column to put one in.

`a_score_is_not_this_shape` — more sets than any of these sports has, or a number no set reaches.

post.description:
**One opponent suffices.** The person across the net is the whole of the evidence that a score was real.

**It does not settle the result immediately.** The grace runs from the *score*, not from your tap, and inside it a disagreement still wins — so a partner who is quick to their phone cannot close the door on an opponent who has not read it yet. `acceptance.settles_at` is when it becomes final, and it is on the response the **proposing** side reads too — a score that has been agreed is no longer a score waiting on silence.

**Saying nothing does the same thing**, a day later. Accepting is how you make it true sooner, and it is never how you avoid a penalty — there is none.

200.description: The game as it stands with your agreement recorded.

403.description: `you_were_not_on_this_court` — no game of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you did not play in it — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about four strangers' evening.

409.description:
Everything above, plus:

`nobody_has_proposed_a_result` — there is nothing from the other side to accept.

`accepting_your_own_sides_result` — **only the other side can accept**, because a teammate agreeing with a teammate proves nothing.

`the_result_is_already_accepted` — your side has already agreed to this one.

post.description:
***Kuba didn't come*** — on a **booked** game whose hour has come, where you would otherwise enter the result (#547). Said by somebody who came, about somebody else on the court; a second report of the same player answers the same and writes nothing, and each player who did not come is reported on their own.

**The game does not count** from the report on, and nobody's Level moves. The reported player has **24 hours to dispute it** (`no_shows[].dispute_by`); after that it stands — the strongest mark on a record — with nothing written at that moment. **Nobody arbitrates a dispute**: the report falls and is on nobody's record.

A player **the club checked in** cannot be reported.

200.description: The game as it stands with your report on it.

403.description: `you_were_not_on_this_court` — no game of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you did not play in it — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about four strangers' evening.

409.description:
Everything above, plus:

`no_shows_are_for_booked_games` — only a game booked on a court has an hour somebody could fail to come to.

`the_game_has_not_started` — its hour has not come yet.

`a_result_is_entered` — somebody already said you played, with a score; answer the score instead.

`checked_in_at_the_club` — the club checked that player in: they were there, and can never be reported.

`you_were_reported_as_a_no_show` — you were reported yourself; dispute it instead.

`the_game_was_called_off`, `the_game_started_short` — there was no game to come to.

400.description:
`not_on_this_court` — that player was not on this game.

`you_cannot_report_yourself` — you are the one person your report proves came.

post.description: **You were reported as not coming, and you did** (#547). Inside 24 hours of the report. The report falls, nothing goes on your record, and the game still does not count: nobody arbitrates which of you is right. A second dispute answers the same and writes nothing.

200.description: The game as it stands with your dispute recorded.

403.description: `you_were_not_on_this_court` — no game of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you did not play in it — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about four strangers' evening.

409.description:
`nobody_reported_you` — there is nothing of yours to dispute.

`the_dispute_window_has_closed` — your day to say you came has passed: the report stands.

post.description:
**Clear a called-off court from your own two lists** — the game's card from Now and the challenge's row from Chats (`docs/adr/0172` §5, `docs/adr/0173`). Yours alone: nobody else's lists move, and the game, its record and the challenge are untouched. It is instant and there is no undo — a mis-tap loses the card and the row and nothing else, which is why there is no sheet.

**Recorded on the game, once per player**, so the card and the row are gone on your other phone and after a reinstall; `GET /games` and `GET /challenges` each subtract it on every read rather than keeping a list.

**Only on a game that is `CALLED_OFF`**, and only for somebody on its court — the presser, or the players the leaver left; the leaver's seat is open and the card was never on their rail.

**A noun and not a verb**, like the departure: what this creates is the dismissal, and it answers nothing because the thing a redraw would draw is the thing you removed.

204.description: The card is cleared from your rail — on this device and every other — and nothing else moves. A second press answers the same and writes nothing.

403.description: `you_were_not_on_this_court` — no game of **yours** has that id. One code for two cases — it does not exist, or you did not play in it — because separating them would answer *is this id real* about four strangers' evening.

409.description: `game_is_not_called_off` — only a called-off game's card can be cleared. The other endings' cards carry a score or a strand's verdict and are the record for the day they stay; a live game's card is the game.

get.description:
**A plan is one challenge's, and this is the only plan read.** One row for every court you hold an accepted seat on — arranging, whole, or over — keyed by `challenge_id`. The room draws it by its own `challenge_id` from the moment it opens; Now joins it to a game by the game's `challenge_id`. The plan is not a field on either, because a game is a record of an evening and a plan is an agreement about a future, and the contexts do not read each other.

**A court with nothing agreed is a row with three nulls, and it carries the anchor.** Absence means one thing only: you hold no accepted seat on that court. An invitee still deciding gets no row; somebody who left gets no row.

**`anchor` is what the day chips run from** — the challenge's send until the game exists, then the game's `planned_at`, only ever later.

**There is no `read_at` here, deliberately.** A plan folds nothing against the clock — its day and hour are wall-clock facts, drawn literally and never counted down — so there is no instant for it to have been folded against. Fold the card against `GET /games`' `read_at`, which keeps every clock on that screen the same one.

**`agreed_point` is derived and sent**: the agreed instant when the day and the hour are both recorded, the start of the following local day when only the day is, and `null` when no day is.

200.description: One row for every court you may plan, written or not, newest arrangement first.

put.description:
**Any member may fill or change any slot, any number of times.** There is no lock and no rate limit — every change writes a system line naming who and what, and **the line is the friction**.

**Writing the value already there records nothing and answers `200`.** Without that the room fills with *Tomek set the place* three times over.

**This is a note and never a court.** No id, no lookup, no autocomplete, no reuse, no geocode — and nothing anywhere reads it. One club will be spelled four ways and nothing will notice, which is what refusing a venue record costs.

200.description: The plan as it now stands.

400.description:
`the_place_is_empty` — nothing but whitespace. **A slot is never emptied**, so a blank value is not a way of clearing one.

`the_place_is_too_long` — past the cap. **Refused, never truncated.**

403.description: `account_held` — your account is under a live hold. **A hold stops you writing anywhere another player sees it, and never stops you reading**: `GET /plans` stays open to you, because a hold must not erase an arrangement other people are already inside.

404.description: `plan_not_found` — **one code for three cases**: there is no challenge with that id, there is one and you were never on its court, or you were asked and have not said yes. They are not told apart on purpose, because a 403 would answer *is this id real* about four strangers' evening — and an invitee still deciding is not shown the plan at all.

409.description: `plan_is_history` — the court is over, so its slots are frozen: its game left its entry window, or, before any game, the challenge itself ended. **That is the only thing that freezes them, and locking is not it**: a locked plan is still fully editable by any member. Once *we played* can no longer be said, the plan is a note about an evening that is over.

put.summary: Set the day you are playing
put.description:
**A local day in the platform's one zone**, so one arrangement reads the same on every phone in it.

**Clamped to 7 days past the row's `anchor`** — the send until the game exists, then `planned_at` — which is what keeps a plan from naming a day on which *we played* can no longer be said, and what leaves every plannable day at least twenty-four hours to say it once there is a game. The anchor only moves later, so a day set before the court was whole stays valid after.

**Writing the day already there records nothing and answers `200`.**

200.description: The plan as it now stands.

400.description: `the_day_is_past_the_horizon` — past 7 days from the row's `anchor`. The days a client offers are clamped to the same bound and shrink as the week runs out; once there is a game, **inside the entry grace there is no day left to set at all**, and the only act remaining is *We played*.

put.summary: Set the time you are playing
put.description:
**The hour is the agreement, not a guess at a booking.** Nothing on this platform will ever hold a court, so nothing can ever contradict it — there is no un-agreeing to fear, only re-agreeing, and any member may do that at any time.

**Thirty-minute steps between 06:00 and 23:00, validated here.**

**Writing the hour already there records nothing and answers `200`.**

200.description: The plan as it now stands.

400.description: `the_hour_is_not_offered` — outside the grid, between two of its steps, or carrying seconds. **Bounded chips the platform offered, never a free instant**: the grid a client draws is a convention, and this refusal is what makes it true.

put.description:
**We are agreed.** Any member may lock, once the court is whole and all three slots are set — and locking is an **act** rather than a fourth slot: a complete plan is one everybody *could* agree, and this says somebody did. It writes a system line into the room, which is the whole of what it does.

**The lock waits for the court.** Two of four may set where, day and hour; they may not agree them for four. While a seat is open or unanswered the answer is `the_court_is_not_whole`, and the card draws the count line where this button will be.

**It takes no body.** The value is the three slots and they are already recorded; sending one back would be the second place that fact is true.

**A locked plan is not a frozen one.** Any member may still move any slot afterwards, the plan stays locked, and every move writes its own line — there is no un-agreeing to fear, only re-agreeing. **The game leaving its entry window is still the only thing that freezes a slot.**

**There is no unlock**, for the same reason a slot is never emptied: the lock is a thing that happened.

**Locking a plan that is already locked answers `200` and records nothing**, and the first lock's `locked_at` is the one that stands.

200.description: The plan as it now stands.

Once *we played* can no longer be said, the plan is a note about an evening that is over.

`the_court_is_not_whole` — a seat is still open or unanswered. **The lock waits for the court**: where, day and hour may be set by whoever is in, and *we are agreed* is said only once everybody who will have to keep it is in. The card draws the count line where the lock button will be — `2 of 4 in — you can plan now, lock when everyone's here` — and never a greyed button, which is why this is its own code. Asked before the count. A lock already taken survives a later departure and answers `200` again.

`the_plan_is_not_complete` — a slot is still empty. **A refusal and not a silent `200`**, which is deliberately the opposite shape from locking a plan that is already locked: a no-op here would leave you believing you had agreed one. It is a conflict rather than a `400` because the request carried nothing at all — what is wrong is the state of the plan.

get.description:
**A card appears the day after the game and stays for seven days.** Not on the evening itself — an answer given ten minutes after losing badly is not the answer this is for — and not for ever, because a card nobody is obliged to answer can only accumulate.

**A game is on this list only once it is over**: the score is agreed, or both sides put one up and neither gave way. A game nobody ever said was played never appears at all — there is nobody to rate for an evening that did not happen.

**Answering removes it, whatever you put on it.** Submitting closes the card for ever, including the card you answered with everybody left blank.

**Absence is the only reason given.** A game not yet a day old, one whose week has run out and one you have already answered are all simply not here — and none of them is something to draw differently.

**Ids only.** Join `game_id` against `/api/v1/games` for the names, the sport and the date; `players` is everybody else who was on that court, in the line-up's own order.

**Ignoring all of this costs nothing.** There is no strand for rating, no penalty, and nothing is recorded about a card that expired.

200.description: The courts still waiting for your stars, **soonest to expire first**. An empty list is the ordinary answer.

post.description:
**Everybody from one game, answered together.** In doubles that is three people — both opponents *and* your partner, because the person who saw you play closest was on your own side of the net. In singles it is the one opponent.

**Anybody may be left blank**: leave them out of `ratings`. Sending an empty `ratings` answers the card without rating anybody, which is an answer and closes it.

**Submitting closes it for ever.** A second request is refused, a blank stays blank, and there is no correction path — so ask before you send.

**Only your most recent rating of a given person counts.** Rating somebody again after another game replaces what you said last time rather than adding to it, so partners who play every week cannot inflate each other by volume.

**A low rating feeds the average and nothing else.** It does not pass, hide or block, and it will not stop you being matched with that person again. `POST /api/v1/passes` and `POST /api/v1/blocks` are the controls that do those things, and both are meant to be deliberate.

**Nobody is told, and no individual answer is ever shown to anybody.** What reaches every reader — the person you rated included — is an average out of five beside how many different people it rests on, over their fifty most recent raters (ADR-0179 §5).

204.description: Answered, and the card is closed. **Nothing is returned, and nothing ever will be** — there is no route through which an individual rating reaches anybody, including the person who gave it and the person it is about.

400.description:
`they_were_not_on_this_court` — stars for somebody who was not there, **including yourself**. You rate everybody else on the court and nobody else.

`you_rated_the_same_person_twice` — one card carries one answer about each player. Refused rather than collapsed, because collapsing means the platform picking which of your two opinions to keep.

`stars_are_one_to_five` — whole stars, one to five. There is no zero and there are no halves.

403.description: `this_game_is_not_yours_to_rate` — no settled game of **yours** has that id. **One code for three cases** — it does not exist, you did not play in it, or its result has not settled — because they have one remedy and separating them would answer *is this id real* about four strangers' evening.

409.description: `you_have_already_rated_this_game` — the card is closed. It closed when you answered it, whatever you put on it, and there is no way to reopen it.

get.summary: Your own record — how others see you
get.description:
**The same sheet everybody else is shown about you**, which is what makes it worth having: the numbers on it have been deciding who you are offered to since you signed up, and a penalty nobody can look up is a penalty nobody can fix.

**Nothing gates it.** A block is between two people and the gender preference is mutual; neither has anything to say about somebody reading their own record, and a hold does not reach it either — this is the one screen a held player has for finding out how they appear.

`is_self` is `true`. Read it rather than comparing ids.

**What other players said comes back as the figure and its count** — `sportsmanship.average` and `sportsmanship.raters`, exactly what a stranger is served about you. The coarse band that used to stand in for it here is retired by ADR-0179 §5, which names what that costs. It changes nothing about how you are matched: the reliability pill is what the platform acts on.

**`?sport=` works here too**, and picks which of your own Levels the skill card draws — the same resolution a stranger's sheet takes.

parameters.name: sport

schema.description:
Which sport you arrived from. **It selects what the sheet is about and never who may be seen.**

Where the subject holds a rating in it, that is the sport `skill` is drawn for. Where they do not — and where you send nothing — it falls back to the sport they have played most, ties broken by the sport registry's own order. Read `skill.sport` for the answer rather than assuming it is what you sent.

Admission is untouched by this. Whether a record opens at all is decided in the partitions the platform already showed you this person in, which is not something a client sends.

404.description: `record_unavailable` — this account has no record to draw: not yet named, or no profile committed. The recovery is onboarding's second part, which `GET /users/me` already sends a cold launch into.

get.description:
Who this person is, as of the moment you opened it.

**Read through a prior disclosure, never about a person.** It opens for somebody a search of yours returned, somebody you share a live challenge, a game or a group with, somebody in a group you run, and yourself — and for nobody else. Without a rule of that shape this route would be a player-enumeration endpoint, and a UUID being hard to guess is not an authorization model.

**Nothing expires but a group.** A search record is kept for ever, so a sheet you could open this morning opens next year — any shorter window could only refuse a face the app is currently showing. A group opens it while you are both in it, because its Members lists who is in it now — and while you run an official group they are in.

**The gates are live.** A block placed since the search, a hold, an account that may not be shown and the mutual gender preference are re-evaluated on every open, so a disclosure entitles you to *ask* and never to be answered. **The gender preference is the one gate that does not reach whoever runs the group they are in**: it says who a player is willing to be matched with, and running their group is not that.

**Asking about yourself is allowed** and answers `is_self: true` — the client is told rather than left to compare identifiers. It draws the same sheet `/players/me/record` does, figure for figure: `is_self` retitles it and moves nothing on it.

**`?sport=` chooses what the sheet is about, never who may be seen.** Send the sport you arrived from; where they are not rated in it you get their most played, and admission is decided from what the platform already showed you regardless.

404.description:
`record_unavailable` — **one code for four causes, and the body is identical in all four.** You were never shown this person; one of you has blocked the other; the account is held or in a state that may not be shown; or there is no such player.

**The indistinguishability is the feature.** A response that named which would deliver a block to the one person a block is meant to be invisible to, and a response that separated *never disclosed* from *no such player* would answer *is this id real* about a stranger. Draw one line — *This record isn't available.* — and do not branch on anything else here, because there is nothing else here.

get.summary: The groups the caller belongs to, newest joined first

post.summary: Create a player group at a home club
post.description: The caller becomes the group's **Owner and first member**, and the group gets its link, which never changes. Answers the group as its page reads it.

400.description: A field the player has to correct, named by `details.field`, checked in the form's order: `group_name_invalid` (`name`) — 1–40 characters once trimmed; `home_club_unknown` (`home_club_id`) — only a club in Raketa can be a home club. Nothing was recorded.

get.description: Its name, monogram, dots, member count and home club; its link and join policy; whether the caller owns it; for every sport, how many members are rated in it and the first of them to join — the Games tab's *N of M*; and the faces on the Info tab's members row, which **leaves out a blocked pair, either way round**, as the Members list does. No count moves.

404.description: `group_not_found` — **one code for two cases**: no such group, and a group the reader is not a member of. Both have one remedy.

503.description: `block_state_unavailable` — who is blocked could not be read, and faces nobody could check are not served. Nothing was recorded; retry.

delete.summary: Delete a group nobody else is in
delete.description: **The Owner, and only while they are its only member.** Afterwards the group is in no list and no search, its link reads *nothing at that link* (join search answers `read_as` `LINK` and no clubs), and the requests waiting on it are gone.

403.description: `not_the_group_owner` — the caller is in the group and is not its Owner. **Nobody but the Owner** sees or answers its requests, edits it or deletes it.

404.description: `group_not_found` — no such group, or one the caller is not in.

409.description: `group_has_other_members` — somebody besides the Owner is in it. A group is deleted only while its Owner is its only member; an Owner who wants out of one with people in it leaves. Nothing was recorded.

put.summary: Edit a group: its name and who can join
put.description: **The Owner's**, both fields as *Edit group* holds them, recorded together or not at all. Saving what the group already says records nothing. **The link never changes**, and nor does the monogram's colour. **Switching to `ANYONE` admits everybody waiting at once**, and `admitted` says who. Answers the group as its page reads it, under `group`.

403.description: `not_the_group_owner` — the caller is in the group and is not its Owner. **Nobody but the Owner** sees or answers its requests, edits it or deletes it.

404.description: `group_not_found` — no such group, or one the caller is not in.

400.description: `group_name_invalid` (`details.field` `name`) — 1–40 characters once trimmed. Read only once the caller is known to be the Owner. **Nothing was recorded** — the policy neither.

503.description: `block_state_unavailable` — who is blocked could not be read for the answer's members row. **Nothing was recorded**: the answer is drawn before the save commits, so the retry is the whole edit again.

post.summary: Join a group, or ask to
post.description: **One tap, and the group's policy decides what it was.** Under *Anyone* the caller is a member **at once** (`relation` `MEMBER`). Under *People I approve* their Join request waits for the Owner (`relation` `REQUESTED`). Neither is recorded twice: tapping again as a member, or while the request waits, changes nothing and answers the same. Answers the group as a club's card draws it, so the card is patched in place.

404.description: `group_not_found` — there is no such group.

delete.description: The caller is no longer a member, and may join again later under the group's policy. **An Owner leaving a group other people are in passes it to the member who has been in longest** — their current stay, so somebody who left and came back counts from their return — and the requests waiting on it pass with it.

404.description: `group_not_found` — no such group, or one the caller is not in: a second tap on *Leave* meets this, because they are not in it any more.

409.description: `lone_owner_cannot_leave` — the caller owns the group and is its only member, so there is nobody to pass it to. *Delete the group* is what undoes it. Nothing was recorded.

get.summary: Members of a group, for one sport
get.description:
**Only the members rated in `sport`** — who in the group the caller could play it with: the caller first, then the Owner, then everybody else newest joined first. Each with their face, their Level in the sport, their Player Score where they have one, whether they own the group and when they joined. **A blocked pair, either way round, is left out of each other's list**, and the group's member count does not change.

**Read by the group's members, and by whoever runs an official group now** — running one is not membership. That caller reads the same rows in the same order, and is a row only once they have joined as a player. A removed Administrator, and one the group was handed away from, are answered as anyone else who is not in it is.

post.description:
*I'm in — if everybody is, book it and charge my share.* **Silent, free, and it holds nothing** — no money moves, no court is held, nobody is told (the others see the player In on the card) — **unless it is the last**. Yeses are the game's, not a version's: a yes on any version counts toward the one game. A yes already said records nothing and answers the same.

**A member may join a post they were never dealt** (#546) — *I'm in* on a sheet's *Already happening here*: a yes like any other, held to who the post is for (`no_longer_fits` otherwise) and to what dealing it would ask of them now — free for its hour, no game then, within their Games & money (`post_not_open_to_you`, which is not said).

**The last yes books the game** (the client gives its ten seconds of *Undo* before sending it): every seat's share is held on the club's account and then all are taken, or none is — `booked` names the booking and its Game, and everybody is emailed *It's a game! · you paid*. When a share could not be held, **nobody paid**: that player's seat is open again (`open_seats`), and when it is this player's own, `your_payment` names the refused payment to confirm. **At an On request club the last yes puts the game to the club** (#543): `waiting_for_the_club`, `open_seats` nought, nothing booked and nobody charged — the court is held, the club is emailed, and the charge and *It's a game!* follow its yes.

404.description: `proposal_not_found` — no such game **for this player**: it does not exist, it was never dealt to them (a yes on a post is the exception: a member may join one they were never dealt, #546), or (for a yes) they are no longer in its group. One code for all three.

409.description: `proposal_is_over` — the game is no longer filling, named by `details.standing` (`EXPIRED` once its book-by passed, `WITHDRAWN` once its poster took the post back with nobody else In, `COURT_HOUR_LOST` once the last court at its club and hour went, `TURNED_DOWN` once its On request club refused it or did not answer). The card leaves. `payment_to_confirm` — this player's seat reopened because their payment could not be held: confirming it (`details.seat_charge_id`) is their yes again. `proposal_already_answered` — this player said no: the card does not come back. `proposal_is_full` — every seat is In. `payment_method_required` — no saved payment method: save one, then say yes. `live_yeses_exhausted` — `details.cap` live yeses in `details.sport` already. `no_longer_fits` — somebody In now is somebody this player does not fit, or a post is not for them (#546); the card has gone, and who or why is not said. `post_not_open_to_you` — joining a post they were never dealt, they could not be dealt it now (#546). Nothing was recorded — except on `proposal_is_over` with `COURT_HOUR_LOST` from the yes that filled it: no court was left at the club and hour, the card is over, and nobody paid.

503.description: `block_state_unavailable` — whether this player fits the people In could not be read. `payments_unavailable` — the yes filled the game and the payment provider could not be reached to hold the shares. Nothing was recorded; retry.

delete.description:
*Withdraw* on a You're In row: free and silent until the game fills. The seat is open again, and the player may say yes again while it fills. Withdrawing a yes never said records nothing. **A poster withdrawing with nobody else In takes the post with them**; with others In, the game carries on without them.

**While an On request club decides, this is *Leave the game*** (#543): nobody has paid; the request to the club is called off (`CALLED_OFF` · `SEAT_OPENED` on the others' Home), the held court is free, and the game is back in the decks with this seat open — the others still In. Full again, it goes to the club again.

The card leaves.

post.description: *Post — you're In*: **posting is the poster's yes**. The game is made at the court hour picked — its share and book-by read off the club — for the *Who* and Level range the controls hold, both stored on it, and **dealt as up to three versions** to the poster's best fits free then: one per full set of them, the evenest first (in doubles 9 or more fits are three, 6–8 two, 3–5 one; fewer, one version with seats open). They see it as a *Challenge* (`CHALLENGE`), and until its book-by it keeps being dealt to anybody who becomes a fit. It is in the poster's *You're In* (`GET /players/me/live-yeses`), withdrawn there (`DELETE /proposals/{id}/yes`): with others In the game carries on without them; with nobody, the post is gone. Not full by its book-by, it disappears and nobody paid.

post.summary: I confirmed my payment — my yes again
post.description:
*Confirm your payment to keep your seat.* The player confirmed, in the app, the payment that could not be held when the game filled. It is **asked of the provider**, never taken on the phone's word; held now, it is the player's yes again — and if theirs was the seat still open, the game books on it and everybody else is charged then. Answers as a yes does. Somebody else took the seat first: the payment is let go.

**A rescue's payment** (#545) — refused when the player went for an open seat on a booked game — confirmed is **the join again**: the seat that opened first is theirs, as `POST /bookings/{id}/seats` takes one, and the answer is the join's.

404.description: `seat_charge_not_found` — no such charge **for this player**. `proposal_not_found` — they are no longer in the game's group; `booking_not_found` on a rescue's payment (#545), which is let go.

409.description: `payment_not_confirmed` — the provider still waits for the player (`details.status`), or the charge was never a payment to confirm (`NOTHING_TO_CONFIRM`): confirm it in the app, or accept the terms or save a method and say yes. `proposal_is_over` — the game is no longer filling, named by `details.standing` (`EXPIRED` once its book-by passed, `WITHDRAWN` once its poster took the post back with nobody else In, `COURT_HOUR_LOST` once the last court at its club and hour went, `TURNED_DOWN` once its On request club refused it or did not answer). The card leaves. `proposal_is_full` — somebody else took the seat. On both, the payment the player confirmed is let go and nobody pays it. `live_yeses_exhausted` and `no_longer_fits` as a yes meets them. **On a rescue's payment** (#545), as `POST /bookings/{id}/seats` meets them: `seat_just_taken`, `booking_is_called_off`, `game_has_started`, `rescue_not_offered` — and the payment is let go.

503.description: `payments_unavailable` — `block_state_unavailable` — whether this player fits the people In could not be read. `payments_unavailable` — the yes filled the game and the payment provider could not be reached to hold the shares. Nothing was recorded; retry.

get.description: You › Payments' *RECEIPTS*: every share the reader paid, the latest first, **the club named as the seller**. A hold let go — a game that did not book — is not here: nobody paid it.

**The reader's games from the moment they fill**, soonest first, each with its status and money line, and **how many need them** — Home's badge. The status is folded at `read_at` from the booking, its Game's result and the clock: *Booked* until the hour, then the result states as today's cards name them. A game a Classic play challenge opened is not here — it is `GET /games`'. Nothing is recorded.

The game details of a booked game, for a player in it: the sides with each seat's face, Level and *paid* tag, the status, WHERE (the club, the court and how far it is), the hour, the money line, whether the balance forecast is drawn (`GET /games/{game_id}/pairing` draws it), and **on the game's day, the reader's check-in code** — a QR payload and a short code, theirs alone. **The chat is the reader's room whose `game_id` is this game's**, in `GET /conversations`.

**A rescue seen from outside** (#545): a member its open seat is offered to reads the same game standing in the seat that opened first (their tile unpaid — *You?*), with `rescue` — no check-in code, no `leaving`. Nothing is recorded.

404.description: `booking_not_found` — no such booked game **for this player**: it does not exist, or they have no seat on it and its open seat is not offered to them. One code for all three.

503.description: `block_state_unavailable` — for a reader with no seat on it, whether they fit the people on it could not be read. Retry.

post.description: *Leave the game* (the client shows the sheet first: the booking's `leaving` says what it costs). **Before the club's cut-off** the leaver is refunded at once, less the card fee, and the seat is offered to others — on their record only if the game is then called off because of it. **After the cut-off** the seat stays paid and is offered to others until the start; the leaver is refunded, less the fee, when somebody takes it, and it is on their record if nobody does. **While the club decides** nobody has paid: the yes and the request to the club are withdrawn, as `DELETE /proposals/{id}/yes` does. The leaver leaves the game's chat with their seat; everybody else's Home reads `SEAT_OPEN`. Refused once the hour has begun.

404.description: `booking_not_found` — no such game **for this player**: it does not exist, or they have no seat on it — including one they already left. One code for all three.

409.description: `game_has_started` — its hour has begun; there is nothing to leave. `booking_is_called_off` — the game is off (refused, unanswered, or short at its cut-off) and everybody still in is refunded, or nobody paid. Nothing was recorded.

post.description: *I'm in · 27 zł* on a rescue — a Seat open card, a Seats to fill row, a rescue's details (the client gives its ten seconds of *Undo* first). **Pays at once**: the share is held on the club's account and taken, and the player takes **the seat that opened first**, on its side — `booked` names the booking and its Game, now on their Home, and they are emailed *It's a game! · you paid*; they join the game's chat. **The leaver who left after the cut-off is refunded, less the card fee, the moment this payment succeeds** (emailed *You've been refunded · your seat was taken*); one who left before it was refunded when they left. `open_seats` is what is still open. When the share could not be held, nothing was taken: `your_payment` names the refused payment, and confirming it (`POST /seat-charges/{id}/confirmation`) is the join again. A player already on the game is answered the same `booked`, and nothing is recorded.

404.description: `booking_not_found` — no such booked game, or the reader is not in its group. One code for both.

409.description: `seat_just_taken` — **the first join wins**: somebody took the seat a moment before, or none is open — *Someone just took it*. `booking_is_called_off` — the game is off (short at its cut-off). `game_has_started` — its hour has begun. `rescue_not_offered` — the seat is not one this player is offered (fit, free, Games & money, a seat they left); which is not said. `payment_to_confirm` — their earlier *I'm in* here waits on their bank: confirming it (`details.seat_charge_id`) is the join again. `payment_method_required` — no saved method. Nothing was recorded and nobody charged.

503.description: `block_state_unavailable` — whether the player fits the people on the game could not be read. `payments_unavailable` — the provider could not be reached to hold the share. Nothing was recorded; retry.

post.summary: Not this time, on a Seat open card
post.description: A swipe left on a **Seat open** card: **silent, and never on the player's record.** The card does not come back to their deck; the seat stays on their *Seats to fill*, which lists every rescue they fit. A second no records nothing.

404.description: `booking_not_found` — no such open seat **offered to this player**: it does not exist, they are not in its group, or it is taken, off or not theirs to be offered.

503.description: `block_state_unavailable` — whether the player fits the people on the game could not be read. Retry.

post.summary: I was told the club handed me these groups
post.description: The sheet that says *[club] made you the administrator of [group]* was closed or followed: each named group this administratorship runs and has not been told about leaves `/users/me`'s `profiles.handovers`, for every phone. **Anything else is stepped over, never refused** — a group handed on meanwhile, told about already, or not theirs.

403.description: `not_an_administrator` — this account holds no active administratorship at that club: removed since the last request, or never. **Every administrator operation answers this the same way.**

of_side.description: Whose score was agreed with. **Always the accepter's opposite** — a teammate agreeing with a teammate proves nothing — so this names the score and, with it, which of the two people this is news for.

agreed_at.title: Agreed At
agreed_at.description: When they agreed. On the wire because *a second ago* and *five hours ago* are the same refusal to a client that cannot see it, and the sentence a player reads has to be able to say which.

settles_at.title: Settles At
settles_at.description: When this agreement becomes final. Measured from the **score**, not from the tap: the person the grace protects is the opponent who has not read the score yet, and their clock started when it was put in front of them.

AcceptanceSchema.title: AcceptanceSchema
AcceptanceSchema.description:
Somebody agreed with the other side's score, and it has not settled yet.

**Present only while the grace runs.** Once it has passed the game is
confirmed and the agreed score is on `score`; inside it nothing has settled,
a disagreement still wins, and the proposing side is no longer waiting on
silence — which is a different sentence on their screen and a correction the
aggregate will now refuse.

acts_as_player.title: Acts As Player
acts_as_player.description: Whether this account acts as a player: it has given the Adult attestation — every sign-up did, and *Start playing* asks it first — or it holds a Player profile. `false` only for an account an invitation opened that has not started playing.

administers.title: Administers
administers.description: One entry per club whose groups this account runs, by name.

pending_invitations.title: Pending Invitations
pending_invitations.description: Invitations addressed to this account's email that are still open, soonest to expire first. One disappears once accepted, removed or past its 72 hours.

handovers.title: Handovers
handovers.description: Every official group a club handed this account's active administratorship there **that it has not been told about**, oldest first (`docs/adr/0192`). One disappears once `POST /administrator/clubs/{club_id}/handovers/seen` names it, or when the club hands the group on. Empty for an account that runs nothing, and for groups an administrator created.

AccountProfilesSchema.title: AccountProfilesSchema
AccountProfilesSchema.description:
Which profiles this account holds (``docs/adr/0185`` §2) — what the
entry gate reads first. *Profile* is the switcher's word.

kind.description: `PLAYER` — a player's own group, with an Owner. `OFFICIAL` — a club's, one per WhatsApp group, run by one of its Administrators: **no Owner**, and its sports are the ones it declares.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sport dots, in the registry's order. **A player group's**: each sport **at least two** members hold a Skill rating in, read when the group is read — a rating earned or a member leaving moves them on the next read. **An official group's**: the sports it declares.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: Every Group member — a player group's Owner, and the Administrator who joined an official group as a player, included. The same for every reader.

waiting_count.title: Waiting Count
waiting_count.description: How many Join requests are waiting — the amber *N waiting*. `0` when nobody is.

AdministeredGroupCardSchema.title: AdministeredGroupCardSchema
AdministeredGroupCardSchema.description:
A card on the administrator's Groups tab. `sports` are the declared
dots; `member_count` is *N members*.

kind.description: `PLAYER` — a player's own group, with an Owner. `OFFICIAL` — a club's, one per WhatsApp group, run by one of its Administrators: **no Owner**, and its sports are the ones it declares.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sport dots, in the registry's order. **A player group's**: each sport **at least two** members hold a Skill rating in, read when the group is read — a rating earned or a member leaving moves them on the next read. **An official group's**: the sports it declares.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: Every Group member — a player group's Owner, and the Administrator who joined an official group as a player, included. The same for every reader.

link.title: Link
link.description: The Group link to post into the WhatsApp group: the public site's address, `/join/` and the group's code. **It never changes** — not on a rename, a policy change or a handover.

whatsapp_size.title: Whatsapp Size
whatsapp_size.description: How many people the WhatsApp group has.

players.title: Players
players.description: Every player, **newest joined first** — the Administrator too, if they joined as a player. A blocked pair, either way round, is left out, as every Members list leaves them out; `member_count` is the group's.

requests.title: Requests
requests.description: *Want to join · N*: everybody waiting, in the order they asked, each with every sport they are rated in and its Level. Empty when nobody is.

AdministeredGroupResponse.title: AdministeredGroupResponse
AdministeredGroupResponse.description:
An official group as the administrator running it opens it — and what
its settings hold. `member_count` is *N players*.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: **The official groups this administrator runs** at this club, newest created first — never a colleague's. Empty before the first: *No official groups yet*.

AdministratorProfileResponse.title: AdministratorProfileResponse
AdministratorProfileResponse.description: *My administrator profile at club X* — the guarded read.

adult_attested.title: Adult Attested
adult_attested.description: Required to be `true`, exactly as at sign-up: `false` is refused with `adult_attestation_required`. **Not a date of birth and not age verification.**

AdultAttestationRequest.title: AdultAttestationRequest
AdultAttestationRequest.description:
The Adult attestation, given by an account that already exists — what
*Start playing* asks first (``docs/adr/0185`` §5).

copy_version.title: Copy Version
copy_version.description: Identifier of the exact copy the player was shown. Not the copy itself — the words are the client's and are never stored here.

AnswerProposalsOptInRequest.title: AnswerProposalsOptInRequest
AnswerProposalsOptInRequest.description:
The proposals question, answered again from the profile screen.

``accepted`` is a required ``bool`` and **not** nullable, which is the one
place this differs from the commit's `ProposalsOptInRequest`: there,
*unanswered* is a state a client can legitimately be in and is refused with
a code that says *ask the question*; here the screen **is** the question
and pressing is the answer, so ``null`` is a 422 rather than a fact.

**The surface is not a field.** It is the route's — ``PROFILE`` — and a
body naming one is ignored, because a client that could assert where a
consent was gathered could assert one it never gathered.

ratings.title: Ratings
ratings.description: The players you are rating. **Leave somebody out to leave them blank**, and send an empty list to answer the card without rating anybody — both are answers, and both close the card for ever.

AnswerTheCardRequest.title: AnswerTheCardRequest
AnswerTheCardRequest.description:
A whole card, answered once.

Everybody from one game is answered together, which is what keeps a busy
month from becoming a chore list.

pairing_id.title: Pairing Id
pairing_id.description: Which of the arrangements, stable within one answer

is_current.title: Is Current
is_current.description:
The one being drawn: **the evenest on a line-up**, and the seat order you sent on a forecast.

A line-up opens on the closest game of the three, in both modes — the same re-seating *Even it out* performs by hand. **Who is on the court is still the group objective's choice** and `group_reason` still says why; what this decides is only which way round they sit. `lineup.seats` follows it.

is_best.title: Is Best
is_best.description:
Best by the group objective. **The objective itself is never returned** — a second score you would have to trust is worse than none — so `group_reason` names what decided it instead.

**Omitted on every arrangement when no objective was computed**, rather than pointed at something else: a line-up with a seat still open, a singles line-up, and every forecast. There is nothing to be best *by* in any of them — no cross pairs, no seat delta, no mean over three Fits — and *Even it out* is then the only selection there is. Draw `is_evenest`.

is_evenest.title: Is Evenest
is_evenest.description: The closest game of the three — what *Even it out* selects. **A separate boolean from `is_best` because the two can differ**, which happens precisely when the four's levels are near-equal and balance has nothing left to say.

split.description:
The two side strengths the forecast was computed from, and the signed difference between them. **The same computation `pct` is** — an arrangement whose sides are equal reads `gap` 0 and the evenest `pct` of the three.

**A provisional arrangement carries one like any other**, under the same assumption `pct` is carried under: the empty seat is read as if the missing player matched the one already there, and `provisional` carries that caveat for all four numbers at once.

ArrangementSchema.title: ArrangementSchema
ArrangementSchema.description:
One way round, with its own forecast. **All of them cross.**

There are exactly three pairings of four people and the engine walks all
three to choose. Returning what it already knows costs nothing and makes
*Even it out* a **selection** rather than a calculation — every swap the
builder permits is one of these, so there is no arithmetic left for a client
to be tempted by.

seat_index.title: Seat Index
seat_index.description: Which seat, stable across all three arrangements: 0 is you, 1 is beside you, 2 and 3 are across the net.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who is in this seat. **Omitted on an open seat** — the top-level `seats` list says why that one is open.

ArrangementSeatSchema.title: ArrangementSeatSchema
ArrangementSeatSchema.description:
One seat within one arrangement: where it is, and who is in it.

`relationship` is **stated and never inferred from the side** — the whole
partner/opponent asymmetry hangs on it, and a client deriving it would be a
second implementation of a domain rule.

status.title: Status
status.description:
`in_progress`, `completed` or `abandoned` — and the field that says which of two things *neither a question nor a result* means.

- `in_progress` **with** a `question`: the questionnaire, awaiting that answer.
- `in_progress` with **neither**: the questionnaire has **stopped**. No remaining question would meaningfully tighten the estimate, and nothing has been rated — every answer is still revisable, and `POST /assessments/{assessment_id}/completion` is what creates the Skill rating.
- `completed`: the `result` is here and the answers are settled.
- `abandoned`: neither, and the run ended without a rating.

questions_asked.title: Questions Asked
questions_asked.description: How many of this run's questions have been answered. The outstanding `question` is **not** counted — it has been put to the player but not answered — so a question counter reads this plus one, and a fresh run reports 0. Replayed from the transcript on every read, which is what lets a resumed run report the position it is really at rather than restarting at 1. Once the run is over this is the same number `result.questions_asked` carries.

transcript.title: Transcript
transcript.description: Every answer given in this run so far, in the order they were given, each with the question it answered **as that question was asked** — so an answered question can be rendered from the response alone, by a client that was never shown it. Empty, never absent, on a run with no answers yet: a fresh run and a run whose answers are being withheld are not two readings of one payload. Grows by one entry per answer and is replayed from the stream on every read, so it survives a reinstall and a second device with nothing cached locally. Length is `questions_asked`; the outstanding `question` is not in it, because it has not been answered.

AssessmentStepResponse.title: AssessmentStepResponse
AssessmentStepResponse.description:
The server-driven step: at most one of `question` / `result` is set, and
`transcript` is everything already answered behind it. Neither means the run
is not asking and has not been rated — see `status`.

AtStakeSchema.title: AtStakeSchema
AtStakeSchema.description:
What a **counted** game against this opponent would do to your Level.

Filled by the backend, never by the matcher and never by the client — it is
the rating engine's own update rule read forward (``docs/adr/0139``), so the
pair printed here is the pair the game will deliver if it is played. Omitted
in for-fun, where a counted result is meaningless rather than unavailable.

**Neither figure is ever zero**, and it is priced head-to-head: in a doubles
sport the game will be a four and the other two seats are unknown when the
card is drawn, so the magnitude carries that sport's weighting while the
pairing is the one you are looking at.

shared_count.title: Shared Count
shared_count.description: Hours of the week both of them ticked

next_slot.description: The soonest hour both ticked, or null when there is none

AvailabilityOverlapEvidence.title: AvailabilityOverlapEvidence
AvailabilityOverlapEvidence.description:
How much of the searcher's week the candidate is free in.

The term is ``|shared| / |mine|`` and has **no constants at all** — the
denominator is the searcher's own ticked cells, which is what makes the
reading asymmetric and what makes it a fact about the pair.

Overlap is evidence a game can be *arranged*, never a proposed time, which is
why a candidate sharing no slot at all is still shown: the times rung exists
for exactly that pairing.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: The player to block. The blocker is the authenticated caller and is never sent.

surface.description: Which screen the block was made from. Recorded as context; no rule reads it.

BlockPlayerRequest.title: BlockPlayerRequest
BlockPlayerRequest.description:
*Do not show me this person again.*

``surface`` is a closed set the client already holds — the four screens that
show one player to another — and it is validated here rather than by the
domain because there is no served vocabulary for a client to hold a stale
version of. Nothing branches on it.

**There is no reason field and there never will be.** A reason for a block
belongs to a Report, and a request shape is where one would be added first.

BlockSurface.title: BlockSurface
BlockSurface.description: The four surfaces of `search-telemetry.md` §2, as a block records them.

name.title: Name
name.description: The club's name; `null` for a club that no longer exists.

paid.title: Paid
paid.description: Every seat's share was taken — `false` for a reader not on the game, who has paid nothing (#545).

free_to_leave_until.title: Free To Leave Until
free_to_leave_until.description: The club's cut-off while it is still ahead at `read_at` — leaving before it is refunded. `null` from the cut-off on, and for a game that filled after it. The line switches by itself at this instant.

refunded_grosze.title: Refunded Grosze
refunded_grosze.description: What everybody still in is given back — the whole share, on a game called off at its cut-off or cancelled by its club (*refunded 30 zł*). `null` where nothing is.

BookedMoneySchema.title: BookedMoneySchema
BookedMoneySchema.description: The money line: *Paid · 30 zł · free to leave until Sat 17:00*.

booking_id.title: Booking Id
booking_id.description: The booking — the same id the game had while it filled.

BookedSchema.title: BookedSchema
BookedSchema.description: The game a yes booked — *It's a game!*

BookedSidesSchema.title: BookedSidesSchema
BookedSidesSchema.description:
The sides the game was booked with, **the reader's first, with them first
on it** — *You + Piotr vs Inés + Bartek*.

name.title: Name
name.description: Their Name, whole — the tile may cut it short, never invent a first name. `null` for an account that can no longer be named.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived link to their first photograph; `null` with `photo_id` draws a poster.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their published Level in the game's sport; `null` if unrated.

paid.title: Paid
paid.description: Their share was taken — the *paid* tag. `false` while the game waits for its club, on a request that was never booked, and on the reader's own tile when they are not on the game but offered its open seat — the dashed *You?* (#545).

checked_in.title: Checked In
checked_in.description: The club's desk checked them in on the day (#547): they were there, so *didn't come* is never offered for them.

BookedTileSchema.title: BookedTileSchema
BookedTileSchema.description: One seat on a booked game.

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The ordinary Game it opened: its result acts, its balance forecast (`GET /games/{id}/pairing`) and its room in `GET /conversations` are all reached by this id. `null` while it waits for its On request club, and on a request the club never booked.

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant the status and money line were folded against.

status.description: `WAITING_FOR_THE_CLUB` — an On request club has the full game and has not answered: nobody has paid, there is no Game yet (`game_id` is `null`) and no court given. `BOOKED` — full and booked, its hour still ahead. `NEEDS_RESULT` — its hour has come and nobody has said it happened. `CONFIRM_THE_RESULT` — a score is on the table. `COUNTED` — a score is agreed. `UNCOUNTED` — they played and no score is agreed. `NEVER_PLAYED` — nobody said it happened in time. `CALLED_OFF` — it will not be played; `called_off_reason` says why. `SEAT_OPEN` — somebody left and the seat is offered (`open_seats`); before the cut-off (`money.free_to_leave_until`) *fills by then or the game is off and everyone is refunded*, after it *the game goes ahead*. A game whose hour comes with a seat still open is `UNCOUNTED` with `uncounted_reason` `SEAT_EMPTY`.

called_off_reason.description: Why a `CALLED_OFF` game will not be played — `null` on every other status. `REFUSED` — the On request club refused it. `NO_ANSWER` — the club did not answer in time. In both nobody paid. (A seat opening while it waited takes the request back instead: it leaves Home, and the people still In find the game filling again in their live yeses.) `SHORT_AT_THE_CUT_OFF` — a seat that opened before the club's cut-off was still empty at it: everybody still in is refunded in full (`money.refunded_grosze`); read off the clock from the cut-off on. `CANCELLED_BY_THE_CLUB` — the club cancelled it, with its reason (`club_cancel_reason`): everybody still in is refunded in full (`money.refunded_grosze`), it is on nobody's record, and they are dealt a new card first (#547).

club_cancel_reason.description: Why the club cancelled a `CANCELLED_BY_THE_CLUB` game — `WEATHER`, `REPAIR`, `DOUBLE_BOOKING` or `OTHER` (no reason given). `null` on every other game.

uncounted_reason.description: Why an `UNCOUNTED` game is uncounted with nobody disagreeing about a score — `null` otherwise. `SEAT_EMPTY` — its hour came with a seat open: somebody left after the cut-off and nobody took the seat. No Level moved, and nothing is on the record of those who stayed. `NO_SHOW` — somebody who came reported a player who did not (#547): the reported player has a day to dispute it (`GET /games` — `no_shows`), after which it stands; the game does not count either way. A report every reported player disputed is an ordinary `UNCOUNTED`, with no reason: nobody arbitrated.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: Seats a leaver left open — the dashed tiles; nought unless `SEAT_OPEN`. The sides list the seats still held.

court_name.title: Court Name
court_name.description: The court the game was given — *Court 2*. `null` until the club gives it: an On request club gives it with its yes.

shows_forecast.title: Shows Forecast
shows_forecast.description: Draw the balance forecast — `GET /games/{game_id}/pairing`, the card today's game screen draws — while the full game awaits its entry. `false` while a seat is open and once a result is told.

check_in.description: On the game's day — the club's calendar day — the reader's code to show at the desk. `null` on every other day, and for a game that will not be played.

leaving.description: What *Leave the game* would cost now — the line under the button and its sheet (`POST /bookings/{id}/departure`). `null` where there is no button: once the hour has come, on a game that is over, and for a reader not on the game.

rescue.description: Present for a reader **not on the game** whom its open seat is offered to — a Seat open card, a Seats to fill row (#545): they stand in the seat that opened first, unpaid (*You?*), and **I'm in · `money.share_grosze`** is `POST /bookings/{id}/seats`. No Chat and no Leave. `null` for a player in it.

BookingDetailsResponse.title: BookingDetailsResponse
BookingDetailsResponse.description:
A booked game's details, for a player in it — or for a member its open
seat is offered to (#545).

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole name, and **nothing may derive a familiar form from it** (``docs/adr/0107``, ``docs/adr/0171``). ``null`` where ``users`` no longer has the account — never for an unnamed player, whom the entry gate holds at the naming step.

CalledOffBySchema.title: CalledOffBySchema
CalledOffBySchema.description:
Who called the game off, and what they are called (``docs/adr/0172`` §4).

**The name is carried because the court cannot supply it**: the leaver whose
departure called the game off has been **vacated** — their seat is drawn
`player_id: null` — so the seats alone could not name them. It is the same
name a seat carries, read in the same set read, and it is `null` for the
same reason a seat's is: an account `users` no longer answers for.

**A departure is told from a press by whether this player still holds a
seat on the game.** The presser does; the leaver's seat is open. No second
field says which — the record already does.

CalledOffReason.title: CalledOffReason
CalledOffReason.description: Why a game will not be played (the mechanics §14.1).

withheld.title: Withheld
withheld.description: Present only on a read-back, where it is always `false`: the fail-closed gates were re-evaluated and this row still stands. A row they no longer admit arrives as the withheld shape instead.

fit.title: Fit
fit.description: The printed number, out of a hundred, and the only one a player is asked to trust. It contains no Liveness.

distance_km.title: Distance Km
distance_km.description: Kilometres to one decimal, measured between the two **drawn spots** — one fixed point inside each player's coarse area, the same for every viewer — and never below `0.1`. The Fit does not read it: the distance term and the radius gate measure cell to cell, so a player at the very edge may print `10.3` inside a 10 km reach. **Promoted out of the distance evidence** so the *Closest* sort reads a field rather than reaching into a variant, and **omitted** rather than sent as zero when the distance term stood down — which is what lets a stood-down row sort last instead of first.

bearing_deg.title: Bearing Deg
bearing_deg.description: **On a reading only.** The compass bearing from your drawn spot to theirs — north `0`, east `90`, clockwise, a whole degree — measured spot to spot beside `distance_km`, so the two place one point on the radar. **Served, never derived**: the client computes no geometry beyond scaling. On the row and never inside `player_card`, because its value depends on who is looking. Omitted on every other surface.

ratings.title: Ratings
ratings.description: **On a reading only.** Every sport this player is rated in, with the Level held there, in the sport registry's order — the card's sport chips. `player_card.level` is the same number for the reading's own sport. Omitted on every other surface.

terms.title: Terms
terms.description: Every term that fired, **ranked by contribution** — the reasons, in the order the arithmetic puts them in. The cap is the client's.

degraded_terms.title: Degraded Terms
degraded_terms.description: The terms that stood down, each with **whose gap it is**: the renormalisation basis. Without it a Fit is uninterpretable — a 78 built on four terms and a 78 built on seven are different readings of the same number — and without the reason beside it, *reliability is not a thing here yet* and *they have not said what kind of evening they want* arrive as one flat list.

liveness_reasons.title: Liveness Reasons
liveness_reasons.description: Why this person moved, ranked by how far. **Codes only** — there is no field here a Liveness number could be written to.

inclusion_reason.description: Why this person is in the list at all, when the reason is one the searcher is owed. **A union of one**: only an interest lift *admits* anybody, and the two reasons that merely reorder stay in the store — one reaches you as a liveness reason instead, and the other is a third party's unpopularity you are owed no version of. Omitted otherwise.

at_stake.description:
What a counted game against this person would do to your Level — the rating engine's own update rule read forward, so the pair printed here is the pair the game will deliver if it is played.

**Omitted in for fun**, where a counted result is meaningless rather than unavailable, and **omitted in competitive when either of you holds no rating in this sport** — never drawn as a pair of zeros.
