would_be_forecast.description: What this candidate would leave on court. Precomputed only when a line-up has exactly one seat open, so **omitted on every shortlist**.

CandidateSchema.title: CandidateSchema
CandidateSchema.description:
One row of the shortlist: the pairing, and the person.

Three field families have a **different author** from the rest and are
attached by the backend after the scorer returns — the card, the at-stake
block and the distance. None of them is a fact the scorer may see, and none
may be computed by the client. **On a reading two more join them**, the
bearing and the sport chips, on the same argument.

On a read-back this row means *the live gates still admit this person*, and
it says so: ``withheld`` is ``false``, positively, rather than absent. A row
the gates no longer admit is a :class:`WithheldRowSchema` instead, and the
two are a union precisely so that **rendering a person the product has agreed
not to show is not a shape this contract can hold** (``docs/adr/0109``).

starts_on.title: Starts On
starts_on.description: Its Monday, on the club's clock.

CappedWeekSchema.title: CappedWeekSchema
CappedWeekSchema.description:
A week the player has as many games booked in as they allow: nothing is
dealt for it.

CardType.title: CardType
CardType.description: The three cards a deck deals (the mechanics §8.1).

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant this whole answer was folded against — the standing, every deadline on it, and which seats are still in.

mode.description: The kind of evening it was sent for. ``null`` when the surface it came from has none; on a challenge born of a mutual yes, `FOR_FUN` when either of the pair declared *for fun* for the sport and `null` otherwise (ADR-0169 §8).

window.description: How soon the week this was proposed for comes round. ``null`` on a mutual-born challenge: no grid was proposed from.

organiser_id.title: Organiser Id
organiser_id.description: Whose proposal this is. Their seat is **accepted from birth** — they are the one asking.

standing.description: What this challenge is at ``read_at``. **Derived from the seats and the clock, never stored.**

seats.title: Seats
seats.description: The court in its fixed order — every **A** seat, then every **B**. Empty seats are in the list, because which side is short is part of what a court is.

pairing_absence.description:
Why no seat carries a card, when the arrangement is still being decided and none was drawn. **Omitted when there is no absence to report** — either the cards are on the seats, or this standing draws no card block at all and the standing already says so.

`NOTHING_TO_COMPUTE` — you hold no rating, have declared no Play intent, or have committed no player profile in the sport you were challenged in. Being asked to play a sport you never declared for is how this works rather than a corner of it, and the screen does not apologise for it.

`COULD_NOT_BE_READ` — somebody else's outage. **Three answers and not two**, because an outage drawing the identical absence as an unrated sport is indistinguishable from four erased accounts.

**Answering is never gated on any of this.** The arrangement always answers and the buttons are drawn from the standing, so a matchmaking outage never becomes *you cannot answer your challenge*.

ChallengeDetailResponse.title: ChallengeDetailResponse
ChallengeDetailResponse.description:
One challenge, richly — the arrangement, the people and the pairing.

**Its own ``read_at``**, because it is its own fold against its own instant:
the standing, every seat's deadline and which seats are still in were all
read against this one moment.

**The card block is drawn while the arrangement is being decided and at no
other time** (``docs/adr/0143`` §8) — one rule stated on the two standings
that draw one, so a standing added later is silent by default. `DECLINED` and
`LAPSED` draw the arrangement and the names alone; `ON` draws neither,
because the game's own screen owns it the moment a game exists.

**Nothing here is re-gated against who is reading** (§2). The four
fail-closed gates ran over every pair of this court when it was minted, and a
card that vanished from behind two buttons that still work would be the one
disclosure a safety gate may never make.

**A reader who has left is a different question and is not that** (§8's
amendment, on [#394](https://github.com/Raketa02/Raketa/issues/394)). The card
block is a **decision aid**, so a reader with no answer left to give is drawn
none — which settles what the block is *for* rather than who may read a
challenge. They still get the arrangement, every seat and every name, and
the buttons are drawn from the standing as they always were.

ChallengeListResponse.title: ChallengeListResponse
ChallengeListResponse.description:
Your challenges, newest first.

**One list and not two.** *Challenge sent* and *Challenge for you* are one
standing read from two sides, so nothing here splits them: the client tells
them apart by whether ``organiser_id`` is yours.

**Ended challenges are in it, and their standing says so.** A list that
quietly dropped this morning's lapse would be the same class of lie as a
read-back that got shorter.

``read_at`` is the instant every standing and deadline here was folded
against. It travels so a client's countdowns and the standings beside them
cannot come from two different readings of the clock — ``GameListResponse``'s
field verbatim, for its written reason (``docs/adr/0143`` §7). The detail
read carries **its own**, because it is its own fold against its own instant.

mode.description: The kind of evening it was sent for. ``null`` when the surface it came from has none — the deck asks nobody to pick one. **A challenge born of a mutual yes is `FOR_FUN` when either of the pair declared *for fun* for the sport, and `null` otherwise** (ADR-0169 §8) — never `COMPETITIVE`, because two competitive declarers get a counted game by the absence and not by a stamp.

window.description: How soon the week this was proposed for comes round. **Derived at send from the grid the search ran on** and never asked for. ``null`` on a mutual-born challenge: no grid was proposed from.

organiser_id.title: Organiser Id
organiser_id.description: Whose proposal this is. Their seat is **accepted from birth** — they are the one asking.

standing.description: What this challenge is at the instant it was read. **Derived from the seats and the clock, never stored**, so it is right for the whole gap between a deadline and anything noticing.

ended_at.title: Ended At
ended_at.description:
When this challenge ended. ``null`` on the three standings that are not endings, and that is the whole of what the absence means: *this challenge has not ended*.

**It is what a shelf life is subtracted from** — an ended row keeps its place for a day and then goes, which is `read_at` minus this and nothing else. **Not `read_at`**, which means the opposite: the instant every standing and deadline here was folded against.

**The ending is the last departure, not the ending's own name.** A refusal outranks silence whatever order the two arrived in, so a `DECLINED` court may have gone on standing for days after the no — until the last seat still deciding ran out. This is when that happened.

**A departure is dated exactly unless it was a decline**, and that is the whole of the precision here:

- **A lapse is exact.** It *is* a deadline passing, so the instant is on the seat already and no sweep needs to have run.
- **A withdrawal is exact.** A decision somebody took, carrying its own moment.
- **A decline is an upper bound**, at or before which that person left. Nothing records when somebody said no, so it is bounded by the tighter of the two facts that are recorded: that seat's own deadline, and the last thing that happened to the challenge.

So `LAPSED`, `WITHDRAWN` and `CALLED_OFF` are always exact, and `DECLINED` is exact whenever the seat that left **last** was one that ran out — which a mixed court often is — and a bound otherwise. The bound is late rather than early, which is the safe direction for a shelf life: a row that outstays it is news gone stale, and one retired early is somebody never learning a seat reopened.

**`CALLED_OFF` is exact too**: the act's own instant, a departure's or a press's (`docs/adr/0172` §2).

ended_by.title: Ended By
ended_by.description:
The player whose act ended this challenge (`docs/adr/0172` §3). ``null`` on the three standings that are not endings, and that is the whole of what the absence means.

**Always the occupant of one of the court's seats**, never a second copy of a name — the face and the name a row draws are that seat's. Which seat, by standing:

- `CALLED_OFF` — the last leaver, or whoever pressed *Call it off*; told apart by their seat, which reads `LEFT` for a leaver and `ACCEPTED` for a presser.
- `WITHDRAWN` — the organiser.
- `DECLINED` — the seat whose *no* or departure completed the desertion: a seat that `LEFT` or `DECLINED`, never one that ran out, because a no outranks silence. Between two nos dated alike, court order.
- `LAPSED` — the seat whose window was the last to run out.

Read from the same per-seat instants `ended_at` is made from, so the name and the date cannot come from two clocks.

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The game this court became, and ``null`` until its line-up first completed — the same id ever after, through a re-seat and through the ending (`docs/adr/0172` §4). What lets a row and the leaver's sheet tell a court that has been a game from one that has not: leaving the last other player on one *calls the game off*, and on one that has not it *closes the court*. Read from `games` and never recorded on the challenge.

seats.title: Seats
seats.description: The court in its fixed order — every **A** seat, then every **B**. Empty seats are in the list, because which side is short is part of what a court is: an A-side full with a B-side short is a different court from the reverse.

ChallengeSchema.title: ChallengeSchema
ChallengeSchema.description: One challenge, with its whole court and what it is right now.

gender_preference.description:
Who this player is willing to be matched with.

**It is mutual and durable.** Narrowing it makes them invisible to the excluded side entirely — including to searchers who asked for anybody — and the client must say so at the moment of setting; learning it from silence is not acceptable. Seats already accepted are facts, not candidates: nothing already agreed is undone.

ChangeGenderPreferenceRequest.title: ChangeGenderPreferenceRequest
ChangeGenderPreferenceRequest.description: A new durable answer to *who am I willing to play with*.

gender.description: The player's own answer. `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY` is a first-class answer; it matches only unconstrained searches, which costs its holder reach, and the client is what says so at the moment of asking (`docs/adr/0096`).

ChangeGenderRequest.title: ChangeGenderRequest
ChangeGenderRequest.description: A new answer to the gender question — *self-declared, freely changed*.

intro.title: Intro
intro.description: The new line, or `null` to withdraw it. Trimmed, then held to **at most 100 characters** and **one line** — the commit's fence exactly, with the commit's codes: `intro_not_admitted` and one coarse `details.reason`, `too_long`, `multiline`, or `contains_contact` for a phone number, an email, a URL or bare domain, or an `@handle`. Whitespace is `null`: a line with nothing in it is withdrawn, never stored empty.

ChangeIntroRequest.title: ChangeIntroRequest
ChangeIntroRequest.description:
The line, replaced — or withdrawn (``docs/adr/0179`` §6).

**The field is required and nullable**, which is the shape of a value whose
absence is a real act: ``null`` withdraws the line, and ``{}`` is a 422 so
that a client which forgot the field cannot be clearing lines. No
``max_length``, for the commit's reason: the cap is the domain's, and the
domain refuses with `intro_not_admitted` and `reason: too_long`, which is
the code a client branches on.

**Nothing comes back.** The intro reaches the card, the record and its
author's own profile read and nowhere else — a sweep in ``tests/unit/
test_intro.py`` holds the contract to those three shapes — and a response
that echoed the trimmed line would be a fourth. The author reads it back
from the profile read, as the two gender writes are read back.

ChangeLocationRequest.title: ChangeLocationRequest
ChangeLocationRequest.description:
The phone's fix, on a cold start.

**What is sent is never what is kept.** The client sends the fix its device
gave it, with the accuracy onboarding used; the platform rounds it to the
cell about a kilometre across before anything is recorded, exactly as the
commit does, and a fix that rounds to the cell already stored records
nothing (``docs/adr/0174`` §6). Nothing comes back: no route on this
surface serves the area yet — the profile read grows the field when *You*
is built — and a silent write on every launch is not the one to start.

The bounds are the world's, as they are on the commit's ``location`` —
read from the value object rather than spelled again. A fix outside them
is a broken reading and not a place, refused at the boundary rather than
rounded into a cell at the pole.

photo_ids.title: Photo Ids
photo_ids.description: Ids returned by `POST /photos`, in the order the player arranged them — the first is the one a player card shows. At most 3; **an empty list is valid and clears**. Every id is checked to exist and to belong to this player, exactly as the commit checks it, and the same id twice is refused with `duplicate_photo`.

ChangePhotosRequest.title: ChangePhotosRequest
ChangePhotosRequest.description:
The photographs, replaced whole and **in order** (``docs/adr/0179`` §8).

An empty list is a legal value and clears: a profile may hold none, and the
poster returns. There is no *clear my photos* flag for the week's reason —
the list is the answer.

search_radius_km.title: Search Radius Km
search_radius_km.description: Whole kilometres, re-checked against the range and step served by `GET /player-profile/options`. Refused with `search_radius_out_of_bounds` — a disabled slider is not a validation.

social_tags.title: Social Tags
social_tags.description: Every tag this player now holds, as ids served by `GET /player-profile/options`. **The list is the selection** — what is absent is dropped. Re-checked against the served vocabulary and the served floor and ceiling exactly as the commit re-checks them; the same id twice is refused with `duplicate_social_tag`.

ChangeSocialTagsRequest.title: ChangeSocialTagsRequest
ChangeSocialTagsRequest.description:
The Social tags, replaced whole (``docs/adr/0179`` §8).

Strings rather than an enum, as the commit carries them: an id outside the
served vocabulary is refused by the domain with ``unknown_social_tag``, a
count outside the served bounds with ``social_tag_selection_out_of_bounds``,
and the client gets a code it can act on rather than a 422.

short_code.title: Short Code
short_code.description: Six characters to type when the camera will not read — upper case, no look-alikes.

qr_payload.title: Qr Payload
qr_payload.description: What the QR code encodes: the booking, the player and the code.

CheckInSchema.title: CheckInSchema
CheckInSchema.description: *Show at the desk*: the reader's own code for this game.

ClaimCodeRequest.title: ClaimCodeRequest
ClaimCodeRequest.description:
The address and the 8-character code from the email. The code is read
forgivingly — case, spaces and dashes are ignored — and its length is not
checked here: a code of the wrong length is simply not the right code, and
is told ``code_incorrect`` as every other one is. The bound is a cap on
what a request may carry, not a rule about codes.

ClaimInvitationRequest.title: ClaimInvitationRequest
ClaimInvitationRequest.description:
*Have an invitation code?*: the address and the 8-character code. The
code is read forgivingly — case, spaces and dashes are ignored — and its
length is not checked here: a code of the wrong length is simply not the
right code.

ticket.title: Ticket
ticket.description: Present it as `ticket` when setting the new password. Good for `expires_in` seconds, and never past the code's own hour; claiming the code again replaces it.

ClaimTicketResponse.title: ClaimTicketResponse
ClaimTicketResponse.description: A correct code, exchanged for a ticket the new password is set with.

ClubCancelReason.title: ClubCancelReason
ClubCancelReason.description:
Why the club cancelled a booked game (the mechanics §16.9) — the players
are told it with their refund.

distance_km.title: Distance Km
distance_km.description: From the reader's Location area to the club, one decimal and never below `0.1`. **`null` for a reader with no Location area**, whose clubs come A–Z.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: What the club offers, in the registry's order.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: The biggest crowd first. **Home-club search**: every group at the club — and a club with some is the one the New group form tints and tags *group already here*. **Join search**: every group when the club itself matched, only the groups whose name matched when it did not, and exactly the linked group for a link. Empty for a club with none: *no groups here yet*.

ClubCardSchema.title: ClubCardSchema
ClubCardSchema.description:
One club as a search draws it: its header — which is context, not a
choice — and the groups inside it.

ClubNameSchema.title: ClubNameSchema
ClubNameSchema.description: The group's home club, as a line under its name.

social_tag_ids.title: Social Tag Ids
social_tag_ids.description: The tag ids this player picked, as served by `GET /player-profile/options`. The count is re-checked against the served floor and ceiling, and an id this platform does not serve is refused with `unknown_social_tag`.

photo_ids.title: Photo Ids
photo_ids.description: Ids returned by `POST /photos`, in the order the player arranged them — the first is the one a player card shows. At most 3; an empty list is valid. Every id is checked to exist and to belong to this player.

weekly_hours.title: Weekly Hours
weekly_hours.description: The hours of the week this player ticked. **At least one of the 112** — an empty list is refused with `weekly_hours_empty`. The minimum is exactly one and is not served: it is fixed, so a client holds it as a constant. Repeated hours are collapsed, and the floor is counted after that.

search_radius_km.title: Search Radius Km
search_radius_km.description: Whole kilometres, re-checked against the range and step served by `GET /player-profile/options`.

gender.description: The player's own answer, asked once. Required — `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY` is a first-class answer and is what a player who does not want to say sends; there is no way to send nothing. It matches only unconstrained searches, which costs its holder reach, and the client is what says so at the moment of asking.

gender_preference.description:
Who this player is willing to be matched with. Optional, and `ANY` when it is not sent.

**It is mutual and durable.** It governs what reaches this player as well as what this player sees, so narrowing it makes them invisible to the excluded side entirely — including to searchers who asked for anybody. The client must say so at the moment of setting; learning it from silence is not acceptable. A single search may narrow this further and nothing may widen past it.

intro.title: Intro
intro.description:
One line about yourself — your **intro** — or nothing. Optional: a player who skips the step sends nothing (or `null`, or whitespace, which is the same), and has no intro rather than an empty one.

Trimmed, then held to **at most 100 characters** and **one line**, in any language. Refused with `intro_not_admitted` and one coarse `details.reason` — `too_long`, `multiline`, or `contains_contact` for a phone number, an email, a URL or bare domain, or an `@handle` — so the client can say what to change without the server explaining what it matched. Nothing else is read.

Edited later from the You tab through `PUT /players/me/intro`, with the tags and the photos it sits between (ADR-0179 §6). It crosses on the player card and on the record, and this response does not echo it.

CommitPlayerProfileRequest.title: CommitPlayerProfileRequest
CommitPlayerProfileRequest.description:
Every answer from onboarding's second part, in one body.

**Photos and the intro are the fields with a default**, because holding no
photograph is a legitimate answer to *add some photos* and writing nothing
is a legitimate answer to *say it in your own words* (``docs/adr/0170``).
Everything else is something this request must actually carry — a
location, a radius, a tag selection, an answer to the proposals question,
and **a week with something ticked in it** (``docs/adr/0102``).

The week's *floor* is not spelled here, and that is the same decision the tag
selection's is: an empty list passes this schema and is refused by the domain
with ``weekly_hours_empty``, so the client gets a code it can branch on
and a recovery it can offer, rather than a 422 that can only say some field
somewhere was wrong.

ConcernSchema.title: ConcernSchema
ConcernSchema.description:
The engine's own statement that a term is genuinely weak.

Judged where the weights and the curves are, over **points forgone** rather
than over a raw value — a social vibe of 0.20 costs under four points of a
competitive match and nearly twenty of a friendly, and only one of those is
worth warning anybody about. A client thresholding a value would be that
judgement in TypeScript, written differently in every client.

**Ranked by the engine, capped by the client**: a card shows one, *Why 78?*
shows all of them.

ConfidenceReasonResponse.title: ConfidenceReasonResponse
ConfidenceReasonResponse.description: Why confidence landed where it did: a stable key and the sentence shown.

ConsentSurface.title: ConsentSurface
ConsentSurface.description:
Where a player was standing when they answered.

Two values, and both are reachable. ``ONBOARDING`` is the only one the commit
can record — the commit *is* the end of onboarding's second part. ``PROFILE``
is the You tab's ``PUT /players/me/proposals-opt-in`` (``docs/adr/0179`` §8),
where the same question is answered again and every press records: the
surface is the **route's** and never the body's, because a client that could
assert where a consent was gathered could assert one it never gathered.

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant this list was folded. It earns one because **its very membership is a fold**: a room is destroyed rather than delisted, so whether a row appears at all was decided against this instant.

ConversationListResponse.title: ConversationListResponse
ConversationListResponse.description: Every room you are a member of, the ones that moved last first.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who they are, and what a line's `actor_id` and a message's `author_id` match

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole name, and **`null` for an account `users` can no longer name** — never for an unnamed player, whom the entry gate holds at the naming step. The person keeps their place either way: a member dropped would draw a three-person doubles court, and an actor dropped would leave a line naming nobody. Draw the unknown player's mark for `null` and nothing else. Nothing may derive a familiar form from it, and it is never the nickname: a handle is drawn on a record and said nowhere (``docs/adr/0171``).

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Their current photograph. Omitted when they have none, and omitted together with `photo_url` — the two travel as a pair or not at all.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived signed link to that photograph, minted for **this response**. It expires within minutes and is not a stored value.

ConversationMemberSchema.title: ConversationMemberSchema
ConversationMemberSchema.description:
One person who has agreed to be on this court right now.

**Derived from whichever record is arranging, never stored**
(``docs/adr/0146`` §7), and it **grows one acceptance at a time**: a doubles
room whose line-up is still filling draws the members it has, because a row
with four faces for a two-member room would be drawing the court rather than
the room.

**The same four fields as a person, and a narrower claim.** Being on the
list is the fact; the face is `ConversationPersonSchema`'s. A member is
always among the response's `people` too, resolved in the same read, so the
two lists cannot disagree about a current member.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who they are, and what a line's `actor_id` and a message's `author_id` match

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole name, and **`null` for an account `users` can no longer name** — never for an unnamed player, whom the entry gate holds at the naming step. The person keeps their place either way: a member dropped would draw a three-person doubles court, and an actor dropped would leave a line naming nobody. Draw the unknown player's mark for `null` and nothing else. Nothing may derive a familiar form from it, and it is never the nickname: a handle is drawn on a record and said nowhere (``docs/adr/0171``).

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Their current photograph. Omitted when they have none, and omitted together with `photo_url` — the two travel as a pair or not at all.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived signed link to that photograph, minted for **this response**. It expires within minutes and is not a stored value.

ConversationPersonSchema.title: ConversationPersonSchema
ConversationPersonSchema.description:
One person this response names — **a name and a face, and nothing else.**

No Level, no band, no area, no score — those are a *card*'s, and a card is
what a searcher reads to decide about a game that might happen. Everybody
here was on this court or spoke in this room.

**The shape `people` is a list of, and the shape a member has.** A member is
a person who is on the court *right now*; the person a `SEAT_LEFT` line is
about is not, and is still somebody the page has to name. One shape for
both, so a client resolves every `actor_id` and `author_id` the same way.

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant the header and the page were folded — **one instant for both**, so members and entries can never disagree.

people.title: People
people.description: Everybody this response names, resolved once against `read_at` and ordered by id: the members, and every author and actor in `entries`. **A superset of `members`**, so a current member is the same face in both. Fill every `{name}` and every author label from here, and merge each page's `people` into it as you page back.

entries.title: Entries
entries.description: The newest page, **oldest first inside it**. Page backward from `entries[0].seq` through `GET /conversations/{id}/entries`; you have the beginning when you hold `seq` 1.

ConversationResponse.title: ConversationResponse
ConversationResponse.description: One room's header **and** its newest page, from one fold.

challenge_id.title: Challenge Id
challenge_id.description: The challenge whose first acceptance opened it

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The game its line-up completed into, and **`null` until it does**. A room whose line-up is still filling has no game and no plan, so there is nothing for a *Details* door to open — draw no door rather than a dead one.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who has agreed to be on this court right now

people.title: People
people.description: Everybody this row names, resolved once and ordered by id: the members, and whoever `last_entry` is about. **A superset of `members`** — fill `{name}` and the author label from here.

last_entry.title: Last Entry
last_entry.description:
The newest thing in the room, rendered by the same two components the stream uses — never a preview string.

**`null` in a room where nothing has happened yet**, which is a real state rather than an edge case: the opening writes no line, so a room whose first acceptance is its whole history has no entry at all.

ConversationRowSchema.title: ConversationRowSchema
ConversationRowSchema.description:
One room, as a row in the Chats tab.

**No state pill, and no standing anywhere on it** (``docs/adr/0148`` §6).
Reading one would make the conversation ask `challenges` and `games` what
they are, which it never does — and it does not need to, because **the last
entry is what a pill would have said.**

CourtAtStakeSchema.title: CourtAtStakeSchema
CourtAtStakeSchema.description: What a **counted** game against this person would do to your Level.

shared_count.title: Shared Count
shared_count.description: Hours of the week both of them ticked

next_slot.description: The soonest hour both ticked, or null when there is none

CourtAvailabilityOverlapEvidence.title: CourtAvailabilityOverlapEvidence
CourtAvailabilityOverlapEvidence.description:
How much of the searcher's week the candidate is free in.

The term is ``|shared| / |mine|`` and has **no constants at all** — the
denominator is the searcher's own ticked cells, which is what makes the
reading asymmetric and what makes it a fact about the pair.

Overlap is evidence a game can be *arranged*, never a proposed time, which is
why a candidate sharing no slot at all is still shown: the times rung exists
for exactly that pairing.

CourtConcernSchema.title: CourtConcernSchema
CourtConcernSchema.description: One term the platform is not comfortable about on this pairing.

reason.description: Whose gap this is: nobody's (`NOT_YET_ON_THIS_PLATFORM` — the term has no provider on this platform at all), yours (`NOTHING_FROM_YOU`), or theirs (`NOTHING_FROM_THEM`). The last deliberately covers every reason a record could not be read, because separating them would publish activity recency.

CourtDegradedTermSchema.title: CourtDegradedTermSchema
CourtDegradedTermSchema.description:
One term that stood down, and **whose gap that is**.

A pair rather than a bare ``Term``, because a flat list holds two different
sentences as one fact: *reliability is not a thing on this platform yet* and
*they have not said what kind of evening they want*.

**It ships even though no *Why?* sheet is drawn over it**, and its own
contract is the reason: without the renormalisation basis a Fit is
uninterpretable — a 78 built on four terms and a 78 built on seven are
different readings of one number. Printing a Fit without it is the exact
failure this field exists to prevent, and the alternative — printing no Fit —
throws away the number the screen exists to give.

km.title: Km
km.description: Whole kilometres between the two areas

area_code.title: Area Code
area_code.description: The candidate's coarse area, as a machine code

outside_their_radius.title: Outside Their Radius
outside_their_radius.description: Whether the searcher sits outside the candidate's own ring

CourtDistanceEvidence.title: CourtDistanceEvidence
CourtDistanceEvidence.description:
How far away they are, and whether the searcher is outside *their* ring.

A candidate's own radius is a Liveness dock and **never a gate**: somebody
who set a small radius is not refusing to be found, and the searcher is
shown the fact rather than having the person removed. The standalone flat
dock for it is struck — the reciprocal reading already prices it, and
proportionately.

sigma_group.title: Sigma Group
sigma_group.description: The confidence is part of the claim, so it crosses with it

assumption.title: Assumption
assumption.description: What the provisional figure assumed, as a code the client renders in its own words. Null when nothing was assumed.

CourtForecastSchema.title: CourtForecastSchema
CourtForecastSchema.description:
How even a game against this person is forecast to be.

``provisional`` travels **inside** the forecast rather than beside it: the
failure being guarded against is a screen showing the number without its
caveat, and a sibling boolean is exactly how the two get separated in a
refactor.

**One seat a side, whatever the sport's court seats.** The block is drawn per
person, and *how would a game against **you** go* is the question somebody
answering an invitation is asking; a four-way figure would be one answer
printed once per seat.

their_intent.description: The candidate's declaration for this sport

aligned.title: Aligned
aligned.description: Whether the two read the same evening

CourtIntentAlignmentEvidence.title: CourtIntentAlignmentEvidence
CourtIntentAlignmentEvidence.description:
What kind of evening each of them is after.

**Intent is a weight and not a gate.** A candidate who declared the opposite
loses the term's entire weight and takes no further charge — the zero is the
whole answer, and a second dock would be a gate wearing a modifier's clothes.
A candidate who has *not* declared has the term dropped and renormalised away
instead, so declaring against the searcher already costs strictly more than
saying nothing.

CourtLevelFitEvidence.title: CourtLevelFitEvidence
CourtLevelFitEvidence.description:
How far apart the two levels are, and which way.

The tolerance behind the curve is absolute on μ and never reads a band: the
shipped bands are deliberately uneven because *evidence* is unevenly
available down the scale, not because a tenth of a point means less at the
top.

CourtLikelyRangeSchema.title: CourtLikelyRangeSchema
CourtLikelyRangeSchema.description:
The **likely range** — μ ± σ, clamped to the scale — as `rating` published it.

Nested rather than two flat fields, because a range is one value with two
edges. **The client computes nothing here**: the rounding lives in the
engine, and a range derived anywhere else is a second set of drawing
constants.

fit.title: Fit
fit.description: The Fit, in your own direction. **The only number here you are asked to trust**, and it contains no Liveness offset.

distance_km.title: Distance Km
distance_km.description: Kilometres to one decimal, measured between your two **drawn spots** — the same number every other candidate prints, never below `0.1`. **Omitted and never zero** when the distance term stood down: somebody whose distance could not be read is not next door.

terms.title: Terms
terms.description: Every term that fired, **ranked by contribution**, each with the evidence behind it. The contributions sum to the Fit **before the modifiers** — see `contribution`, which is where that gap is explained rather than being two sentences that disagree.

degraded_terms.title: Degraded Terms
degraded_terms.description: Every term that stood down, and whose gap each one is. **The Fit's renormalisation basis**, without which the number above cannot be read.

concerns.title: Concerns
concerns.description: Terms the platform is not comfortable about on this pairing.

forecast.description:
What the court **as it stands** would leave on court, read in your direction — everybody still in, placed where they actually sit.

**The same figure rides on every card**, because a forecast is a fact about the game rather than about one person. A seat still open reads as if whoever fills it matched the player already on that side, which is what `provisional` says.

**Omitted where no game can be arranged out of what is left.** A side with nobody on it is not a side, so a court whose far side has all declined leaves nothing to forecast against — and an invented number would be worse than the absence.

at_stake.description:
What a counted game against this person would do to your Level — the rating engine's own update rule read forward.

**Omitted in for fun**, where a counted result is meaningless rather than unavailable, and **omitted when either of you holds no rating in this sport** — never drawn as a pair of zeros.

CourtPairingSchema.title: CourtPairingSchema
CourtPairingSchema.description:
What this platform makes of you **against** this person.

**Recomputed when the screen is opened, in your own direction** — never
copied at send and never replayed from the organiser's search
(``docs/adr/0143`` §3). That is the only shape under which *Match score for
you* is true: neither stored Fit is publishable, because one is the
organiser's reading of the invitee and the other was scored with the
searcher's own reliability deliberately set to null.

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole name, and **nothing may derive a familiar form from it** — every sentence naming somebody uses the whole name or names nobody (``docs/adr/0171``). Never the nickname: a handle is drawn on a record and said nowhere.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Their current photograph. Omitted when they have none, and omitted together with `photo_url` — the two travel as a pair or not at all.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived signed link to that photograph, minted for **this response**. It expires within minutes and is not a stored value: a client that keeps one keeps a dead link.

area_code.title: Area Code
area_code.description: Their coarse area, as a machine code

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level, as RacketSkill published it

range.description: Where their Level most likely sits

player_score.title: Player Score
player_score.description:
Their **published** Player Score, and never a re-derivation of one (`docs/adr/0140`).

**Omitted where the platform has watched nothing**, which is most people today — the segment disappears rather than reading `Score 0`, because a nought printed for somebody nothing was watched of is a claim where there is a gap.

CourtPersonSchema.title: CourtPersonSchema
CourtPersonSchema.description:
Who one person on this court is. **A closed list with two permanent gaps.**

No bio and no free text of any kind, ever; and **no activity recency at any
granularity** — not a timestamp, not *active today*, not a green dot.

**``photo_id`` and ``photo_url`` are present exactly together.** An id with
no link beside it is a photograph nothing can draw; neither means the client
draws the generated court poster, which chooses by hash and needs nothing
from the wire (``docs/adr/0134``). Refusing the photograph outright would
make the person who asked you to play more anonymous than a stranger in your
deck, which is the wrong way round.

matched.title: Matched
matched.description: Tag ids they both hold, in this column

CourtPlayingStyleEvidence.title: CourtPlayingStyleEvidence
CourtPlayingStyleEvidence.description:
What the two of them are like during the hour on court.

The split from social vibe is **by relationship, not by tag group**: every
matrix row carries its own column, so a tag can be read for the hour on court
in one row and for the evening around it in another.

A pair with nothing firing is *different, not incompatible* — the term's zero
is a real clash, never an absence of relationship.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: The platform's confidence transform over the combined σ, as a whole percent. Never 100: the platform cannot tell a player it is certain.

CourtPredictedBalanceEvidence.title: CourtPredictedBalanceEvidence
CourtPredictedBalanceEvidence.description:
How even the game is forecast to be, and how sure of that the platform is.

``pct`` is the forecast the player is shown; ``confidence`` is the platform's
existing σ transform and never a second spelling of certainty.

strands.title: Strands
strands.description: The strands that produced a reading, over the closed six

floor_breached.title: Floor Breached
floor_breached.description: Whether the published score sits under the reliability bar

CourtReliabilityEvidence.title: CourtReliabilityEvidence
CourtReliabilityEvidence.description:
What the candidate's record says about turning up and following through.

``score`` is the **published Player Score** — the number on the player's own
profile — and never the matcher's private per-mode blend of the same six
strands. A penalty justified by a figure that exists nowhere a human can look
is unexplainable, and a player who works their visible score back up must be
able to see the penalty lift.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: The **renormalised** weight — this term's share of a hundred over the terms that actually fired.

contribution.title: Contribution
contribution.description:
The weight times the value.

**The contributions sum to the Fit before the modifiers**, and `fit` above is the figure after them — the same number every other surface prints for this pairing. Those are the reliability dock and its neighbours, engine internals this screen does not draw, so the breakdown explains the pairing rather than reconstructing the total to the decimal.

CourtScoredTermSchema.title: CourtScoredTermSchema
CourtScoredTermSchema.description: One term that produced a reading, and what it was worth here.

day.title: Day
day.description: ISO weekday — 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday. The grid is Monday-first.

hour.title: Hour
hour.description: The hour that cell starts at, wall clock — 19 is 19:00 to 20:00

CourtSharedSlot.title: CourtSharedSlot
CourtSharedSlot.description:
The next hour of the week both players ticked.

**The grid is never rendered to anybody as a calendar.** Only the count of
shared hours and the name of the next shared one are ever shown, because
overlap is a fact about a pair where a calendar is a fact about a person.

matched.title: Matched
matched.description: Tag ids they both hold, in this column

CourtSocialVibeEvidence.title: CourtSocialVibeEvidence
CourtSocialVibeEvidence.description:
What the two of them are like around the game.

The same shape as playing style and deliberately a **separate variant**: the
two terms carry different weights, invert between the modes, and a client
renders them under different headings. One variant with a column field would
make *which term is this* a value the client has to branch on rather than a
type it can dispatch over.

CourtState.title: CourtState
CourtState.description: What a yes on the card does (the screens A2.3).

CourtStrandReading.title: CourtStrandReading
CourtStrandReading.description:
One reliability strand that produced a reading.

A strand with too few observations **stands down and is absent from the
list** rather than present at zero: *we have not seen enough* and *they are
bad at this* are different facts, and a term may never be honestly neutral.

CourtTagPair.title: CourtTagPair
CourtTagPair.description:
Two tag ids one relationship row fired on.

Ids only. The row's kind is the field it sits under, its column is the term
it sits under, and its strength or severity is a ruleset number the player is
not shown — what is owed here is *which two things about you two this reads*.

name.title: Name
name.description: *Same name as the WhatsApp group*: trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 1–40 characters. Refused with `group_name_invalid`, `details.field` `name`.

join_policy.description: `ANYONE` or `PEOPLE_I_APPROVE`. **Switching to `ANYONE` admits everybody waiting at once.**

whatsapp_size.title: Whatsapp Size
whatsapp_size.description: How many people the WhatsApp group has — **required**, a whole number from 2 to 1024. It limits nothing: more players than this is allowed and honest. Refused with `whatsapp_size_invalid`, `details.field` `whatsapp_size`.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: What the group plays — **required**, and **only the club's**. Ticking one twice is ticking it. Refused with `group_sports_required` for none, or `sport_not_offered_by_club` with the sport in `details.sport` — `details.field` `sports` either way.

CreateOfficialGroupRequest.title: CreateOfficialGroupRequest
CreateOfficialGroupRequest.description:
*New official group*. **The home club is not asked**: it is the club in
the path, fixed.

name.title: Name
name.description: Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 1–40 characters. Never unique. Refused with `group_name_invalid`, `details.field` `name`.

home_club_id.title: Home Club Id
home_club_id.description: A club from home-club search — **required**. A club Raketa does not have is `home_club_unknown`, `details.field` `home_club_id`.

CreatePlayerGroupRequest.title: CreatePlayerGroupRequest
CreatePlayerGroupRequest.description:
A player creates a group. **No sport is asked for**: the group plays
whatever its members are rated in (``docs/adr/0183`` §6).

DayRange.title: DayRange
DayRange.description: A third of a day, as a card and the posting grid group hours.

sport.description: Which sport this deal is for

availability_override.title: Availability Override
availability_override.description:
The week to run **this one deal** against, when the player edited it on the Play screen. Omit to use the grid on your profile — **omit it, never send `null`**.

**It is an ask and never a correction.** Nothing here writes your profile; the app offers to save it afterwards.

DealDeckRequest.title: DealDeckRequest
DealDeckRequest.description:
What a deal is asked for. **The sport, and the week you are asking about.**

This said *one field, and that is the whole contract* until the week was
added, and the three refusals it was written to protect are untouched by
that: **a mode, a widening and a pass window** may not arrive here, and a
grid is none of the three.

**There is no `mode` here and there never will be.** The deck reads your own
declared Play intent for this sport, resolved backend-side, and *no
preference* is a working deck rather than a blocked one — indecision is not a
state this product refuses. A mode on this body would be the field the
telemetry constraint refuses: `mode` is null exactly when the surface is the
deck.

**There is no widening here either.** The relaxation ladder does not reach
the deck, so a deal carries no rung offers and there is no offer for one to
cite.

**There is nothing about a pass.** The suppression window crosses the wire in
no shape at all — no field, no code, no timestamp — which is what makes a
pass unable to become something stronger by way of a request.

**The week is an ask and never a correction**, exactly as it is on a search.
It is here because the alternative was a deck that silently ranks on a week
the player has just replaced, and because a client cannot compute the
difference itself: a search that took a times rung ran on a grid with a slot
the player never ticked, and only this backend knows that.

proposal_id.title: Proposal Id
proposal_id.description: The game. On a `SEAT_OPEN` card it is the **booking's** id — the same id the game had while it filled: `POST /bookings/{id}/seats` takes the seat, `POST /bookings/{id}/no` is *not this time*, and `GET /bookings/{id}` its details.

type.description: `PICKED_FOR_YOU`, `CHALLENGE` (a member's post) or `SEAT_OPEN` (a rescue: a booked game that lost a player, dealt to its best fits — #545).

challenger.description: The poster of a challenge; `null` on a pick, and on a challenge once its poster withdrew — *the group challenged you*.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start; games are 1 h.

share_grosze.title: Share Grosze
share_grosze.description: What this player pays if it fills — at once, on a `SEAT_OPEN` card.

deadline.title: Deadline
deadline.description: When the card leaves unfilled — its book-by; on a `SEAT_OPEN` card the club's cut-off, then the start. The client counts down only under 24 h.

in_count.title: In Count
in_count.description: People In on the whole game, every version counted — nought on a `SEAT_OPEN` card, whose players have paid (`paid` on their tiles).

version_count.title: Version Count
version_count.description: Versions the game was dealt in; above one, the card says how many people are In on the whole game.

court.description: `COURT_AVAILABLE` — a yes is a free vote; `BOOK_IT_NOW` — a yes fills the game and books it; `BOOKED` — a rescue: the court is booked, and a yes takes the seat and pays at once.

court_name.title: Court Name
court_name.description: What the club calls the court — *Court 6* — on a `SEAT_OPEN` card; `null` on a game still filling, which is given one at booking.

no_free_cancellation.title: No Free Cancellation
no_free_cancellation.description: The club's cut-off has already passed for this game.

club_confirms.title: Club Confirms
club_confirms.description: An On request club: a full game waits for the club's yes before anybody pays, so *Book it now* charges nobody at once and its stamp carries no price.

forecast.description: `null` where it cannot be read: somebody on the card holds no rating in the sport, or nobody faces the reader yet.

DeckCardSchema.title: DeckCardSchema
DeckCardSchema.description: One card, as the reader is dealt it: **their own version** of the game.

DeckChallengerSchema.title: DeckChallengerSchema
DeckChallengerSchema.description: Who a challenge names — *Kuba challenged you*.

name.title: Name
name.description: The club's name; `null` for a club that no longer exists.

provisional.title: Provisional
provisional.description: A seat is empty and was read as matching its partner.

DeckForecastSchema.title: DeckForecastSchema
DeckForecastSchema.description: How even the game on **this** card is forecast to be, with these sides.

grade.description: *High / Good / Slim overlap*: the hours everybody on the card shares, over the week of whoever has least to give.

cells.title: Cells
cells.description: Twenty-one: day by day from Monday, morning first.

count.title: Count
count.description: Cards of this kind the reader is dealt here.

DeckSegmentSchema.title: DeckSegmentSchema
DeckSegmentSchema.description: One side of the *Competitive · N / For fun · N* switch.

DeckSidesSchema.title: DeckSidesSchema
DeckSidesSchema.description:
The rows are the sides (Q70): the reader's, and the other. A side may be
short of a seat, which the client draws empty.

name.title: Name
name.description: Their Name, whole — the tile may cut it short, never invent a first name. `null` for an account that can no longer be named.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived link to their first photograph; `null` with `photo_id` draws a poster.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their published Level in the card's sport; `null` if unrated.

is_in.title: Is In
is_in.description: They said yes: the **IN** tag. Nobody else carries a tag — a player still deciding is a plain tile.

paid.title: Paid
paid.description: On a `SEAT_OPEN` card, a player on the booked game — *2,75 · paid* (#545). `false` on a game still filling, and on the reader's own tile, which is the open seat.

intent.description: The declaration. `NO_PREFERENCE` is an **explicit answer** and not an absence — the matcher must be able to tell *either suits me* from *I never opened that screen*, and nobody is ever backfilled to it. There is no null.

surface.description: Which screen this was declared on. Required, because the client is the only party that knows — and safe to take its word for, because nothing branches on it: it is context recorded beside the fact, never a thing a decision reads.

DeclarePlayIntentRequest.title: DeclarePlayIntentRequest
DeclarePlayIntentRequest.description:
What kind of game this player wants in one sport, and where they said so.

The sport is the path, because it is half the resource's identity: the
resource is *one player's intent in one sport* (``docs/adr/0094``).

DegradedReason.title: DegradedReason
DegradedReason.description:
Whose gap a stood-down term is. **Four values, and one line drawn twice.**

``floor.py`` draws that line to decide a number — *the gate counts
person-specific gaps and never platform-wide absence* — and until now it was
drawn nowhere else, so the one list that crosses the wire held *reliability
is not a thing here yet* and *they have not said what kind of evening they
want* as the same fact, twenty times a search.

The fourth value is the line drawn a second time, from the other side: a
term the **search** declined to read is nobody's gap either — not the
platform's, which has the provider, and not the person's, who may well have
declared — and the deck is the surface that does it (``docs/adr/0169`` §2).
Filing that under either existing code would print a sentence about a person
that is false of them.

**It is a code and not a sentence**, on ``docs/adr/0106``'s rule: a client
writing *"they haven't declared"* off a bare ``Term`` would be an engine rule
in TypeScript, and *"nobody has a record yet"* becomes silently false the day
``matches`` ships, with no gate that catches it.

**``NOTHING_FROM_THEM`` deliberately swallows reliability's three causes** —
no record, the last observation past the horizon, no strand clearing the
observation bar. Separating them would publish activity recency, which
``docs/adr/0106`` §5 refuses by name, so the refusal is held by the shape of
this vocabulary rather than by a reviewer noticing it in a later ticket.

**``NOTHING_FROM_YOU`` wins a tie** — both grids blank, neither side tagged —
because it is the only one of the two a reader can act on.

reason.description: Whose gap this is: nobody's (`NOT_YET_ON_THIS_PLATFORM` — the term has no provider on this platform at all), yours (`NOTHING_FROM_YOU`), theirs (`NOTHING_FROM_THEM`), or the surface's (`NOT_READ_ON_THIS_SURFACE` — the deck reads no intent for anybody, so the term stood down for every card and says nothing about either of you). `NOTHING_FROM_THEM` deliberately covers every reason a record could not be read, because separating them would publish activity recency.

DegradedTermSchema.title: DegradedTermSchema
DegradedTermSchema.description:
One term that stood down, and **whose gap that is**.

A pair rather than a bare ``Term``, because the flat list held two different
sentences as one fact: *reliability is not a thing on this platform yet* and
*they have not said what kind of evening they want*. The engine draws that
line to decide a number — the evidence gate counts person-specific gaps and
never platform-wide absence — and it now survives the wire.

**The reason is a code and the client writes the sentence** (``docs/adr/0106``).
A client deriving *"they haven't declared"* from ``INTENT_ALIGNMENT`` alone
would be an engine rule in TypeScript, and *"nobody has a record yet"* is a
sentence that goes silently false the day ``matches`` ships. The term supplies
the other half: ``INTENT_ALIGNMENT`` and ``SOCIAL_VIBE`` under one code are two
different sentences.

**The platform tier repeats on every row and is drawn once.** It is here
because it is this candidate's renormalisation basis — a 78 built on four
terms and a 78 built on seven are different readings of the same number, and
dropping it would make the row's own arithmetic unreadable — and
``NOT_YET_ON_THIS_PLATFORM`` is a fact about the platform rather than about
twenty people, so the sheet states it once beside the version stamps
(``the-play-screens.md`` §8). Suppressing it on the wire instead was refused:
the basis is not decoration.

left.description: `BEFORE_THE_CUT_OFF` — refunded at once, less the card fee (the receipt follows within moments); the seat is offered to others. `AFTER_THE_CUT_OFF` — the seat stays paid and is offered to others until the start; refunded, less the card fee, when somebody takes it. `WHILE_WAITING_FOR_THE_CLUB` — nobody had paid: the yes and the request to the club are withdrawn, and the game is filling again.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who holds this seat. ``null`` on a seat nobody was put in.

answer.description: What they did about being asked. ``null`` while they have not answered, and on a seat nobody was put in. **A lapse is not a refusal** — they are different facts and the platform counts them apart.

answer_by.title: Answer By
answer_by.description: When this seat's answer stops being wanted. Past it the seat reads as lapsed whether or not anything has swept it, and a late answer is refused rather than accepted late. ``null`` exactly when nobody was asked: an empty seat, the organiser's, and both seats of a challenge born from a mutual yes.

name.title: Name
name.description:
The whole name, and **nothing may derive a familiar form from it** — every sentence naming somebody uses all of it or names nobody (``docs/adr/0107``, ``docs/adr/0171``). Never the nickname, which is a handle drawn on a record and said nowhere.

``null`` on a seat nobody was put in, and ``null`` where ``users`` no longer has the account — never for an unnamed player, whom the entry gate holds at the naming step. The seat stays either way: a seat with no name is still a position on the court, and the screen has a side to name instead.

**A name is the whole of what a challenge borrows about a person here.** A Level, a band, an area and a photograph are a card's, and a card is drawn on the detail read alone.

card.description:
Who this person is and what you make of them, drawn only while the arrangement is still being decided and only for somebody still in it. Omitted on your own seat, on an empty one, on a seat that declined or lapsed, on **every** seat when you yourself have declined or lapsed, and on every seat when `pairing_absence` says there is no pairing to draw.

**Having answered is not having left.** A reader who **accepted** keeps their cards: they have no answer left to give either, and they are still on the court.

DetailSeatSchema.title: DetailSeatSchema
DetailSeatSchema.description:
One seat on the detail read — the list's seat, and a card where one is drawn.

**The card is per seat as well as per challenge** (``docs/adr/0143`` §8).
Somebody who declined or lapsed inside a still-open court gets none: the pair
releases the moment a seat leaves, and *that person is a stranger to you once
more.* Their seat stays and keeps its name, because the standing sentences
name them.

**Your own seat never carries one either.** A pairing with yourself is not a
question.

**And a reader who has left is drawn none at all**
([#394](https://github.com/Raketa02/Raketa/issues/394)). The rule above is
asked about the reader as well as about the court: their seat has left, so
everybody still arranging is a stranger to them once more. It is the whole
card block that goes rather than one seat's card, and it goes without a
`pairing_absence` — the same absence an ended standing produces.

km.title: Km
km.description: Whole kilometres between the two areas

area_code.title: Area Code
area_code.description: The candidate's coarse area, as a machine code

outside_their_radius.title: Outside Their Radius
outside_their_radius.description: Whether the searcher sits outside the candidate's own ring

DistanceEvidence.title: DistanceEvidence
DistanceEvidence.description:
How far away they are, and whether the searcher is outside *their* ring.

A candidate's own radius is a Liveness dock and **never a gate**: somebody
who set a small radius is not refusing to be found, and the searcher is
shown the fact rather than having the person removed. The standalone flat
dock for it is struck — the reciprocal reading already prices it, and
proportionately.

name.title: Name
name.description: Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 1–40 characters. Refused with `group_name_invalid`, `details.field` `name`.

join_policy.description: `ANYONE` or `PEOPLE_I_APPROVE`. **Switching to `ANYONE` admits everybody waiting at once.**

EditGroupRequest.title: EditGroupRequest
EditGroupRequest.description:
The Owner saves *Edit group* — the New group form's Name and Who can join
cards, **both as the form holds them**. The home club is not here: it never
changes (``docs/adr/0183`` §2).

group.description: The group as its page reads it, after the save.

admitted.title: Admitted
admitted.description: Everybody the switch to `ANYONE` admitted, **in the order they asked** — the Edit screen shows them. Empty for every other save.

EditedGroupResponse.title: EditedGroupResponse
EditedGroupResponse.description: The group as *Edit group* left it, and who the save let in.

entries.title: Entries
entries.description: The page, **oldest first inside it**. Empty when `before_seq` was 1 — there is nothing before the beginning.

people.title: People
people.description: Every author and every actor on this page, resolved once and ordered by id. **Not the roster and not a superset of it** — a page names only what is on it, so merge these into the `people` you already hold rather than replacing them. Empty when `entries` is.

EntryPageResponse.title: EntryPageResponse
EntryPageResponse.description:
One page backward. **No header, and no instant** — but the page's own faces.

`people` is not a header: it says nothing about the room and nothing about
who is in it. It is the one thing the detail read could not have given a
client for this page, because the people a page names are not the members.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every error response, on both API surfaces.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable identifier for this exact failure. The only half of the envelope a client may branch on.
code.title: Code

message.description: Human-readable diagnostic. Never the copy shown to a user — that is the client's, chosen from the code.
message.title: Message

trace_id.description: This request's identifier, also returned on the X-Request-ID header. Ties a client-side failure to a server log without logging a payload.
trace_id.title: Trace Id

details.description: Structured context for this code, when the code defines any.
details.title: Details

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

sport.description: Which sport this yes is for

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who you would like to play

search_id.title: Search Id
search_id.description: The search this person was shown to you in. **Required** — a yes with no origin is refused rather than recorded with a null link.

ExpressInterestRequest.title: ExpressInterestRequest
ExpressInterestRequest.description:
One tap. **Three fields, and the third is not optional.**

``search_id`` is the **origin key**: it says which search surfaced this
person, and an interest citing a search that is unknown, that belongs to
somebody else or that never showed them is **refused, never linked as null**.
A silently dropped link is a denominator that lies, and *interests per search*
is how this engine is judged.

**The position is not sent.** The backend reads it off the cited search's own
returned rows, so the origin key is true by construction rather than by a
client being honest about where it was scrolled to.

mutual.title: Mutual
mutual.description: `true` when they had already said *Let's play* to you for this sport. **A mutual is told to both sides.** A one-sided yes is told to nobody, ever.

challenge_id.title: Challenge Id
challenge_id.description:
**The game the two of you have**, when there is one — the challenge this tap opened, or the one an earlier mutual between you opened that is not finished with.

**`null` is one answer covering two causes, and it does not say which.** You may already have a game *being arranged* together, or the platform may have declined to open one. That distinction does not cross this wire and will not — so a client that reported the absence as a state of its own would be reporting the second, which is a fact about the other person no refusal here is allowed to disclose.

`mutual` is unaffected either way: it is what the two yeses say.

outstanding.description: Where this sport now stands against its cap, after this tap.

ExpressedInterestResponse.title: ExpressedInterestResponse
ExpressedInterestResponse.description:
What one tap answers with.

``mutual`` is the one thing this tells you about the other person, and you
have earned it by them having said yes to you first. Nobody is notified of a
one-sided yes, in either direction.

FactorResponse.title: FactorResponse
FactorResponse.description:
One evidence category's row: what it says, and which way it pulled.

``direction`` is one of ``up`` / ``down`` / ``neutral``, computed by the
engine from that category's own evidence against the final estimate. The
client never derives it — a client-side arrow is a second opinion about the
arithmetic, and two clients would eventually hold two of them.

FailureReason.title: FailureReason
FailureReason.description: Why a share could not be held (the mechanics §12.2, §19).

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant every row and deadline here was read against.

badge.title: Badge
badge.description: The tab's badge: the Seats to fill rows.

seats_to_fill.title: Seats To Fill
seats_to_fill.description: Every rescue in the group the reader fits — the pair rule, the kind their intent wants, free for the hour in their week, no game of theirs then, within their Games & money — **soonest first**, before or after the cut-off. Never a game still filling: that is the deck's. *You're In* is `GET /players/me/live-yeses`.

FillInResponse.title: FillInResponse
FillInResponse.description: A group's **Fill in** tab for one sport: *Seats to fill* (#545).

search_id.title: Search Id
search_id.description: The search this fill was built from — **yours, and run just now**. Everybody being newly asked must have appeared in it, and each new seat cites where they sat. The people already on the court are not looked up in it: they came from somewhere else, possibly weeks ago.

court.title: Court
court.description: The whole court as it will stand, in the court's own order: every **A** seat, then every **B**. It must be the sport's shape, you must be in it, and **everybody already on the court must still be in it** — they may change sides and they may not lose their place.

FillSeatsRequest.title: FillSeatsRequest
FillSeatsRequest.description:
**The send's shape minus the mint**: the court, and the search behind it.

The challenge is in the path, so what is left is the two things a fill has to
say — and the two the send says. Everything else about the game is already on
the challenge: the sport, the kind of evening, and the **window**, which is
stamped when a challenge is sent and never again. A challenge born of two
mutual yeses has no window at all and keeps none.

``court`` is the **whole** arrangement and not the seats being filled. An
acceptance is to the game and not to the side, so the people already in may
be moved across the net — and may not be taken out. A court that omitted one
of them is refused.

sport.description: Which sport this four would play

mode.description: Competitive or for fun — the vector this reads under

search_id.title: Search Id
search_id.description: The search these people came off. **Required** — a forecast about somebody no search of yours showed is refused, not computed.

players.title: Players
players.description:
The people beside you, **in seat order**: the first is your partner in the arrangement the response marks `is_current`. One, two or three — a seat may be empty, and the forecast comes back **provisional** when one is.

Nobody twice, and never more than the sport seats. An empty seat is read *as if the missing player matched the one already there*, which is a claim about somebody who is not there — sending the same person twice would make that assumption look like a fact.

ForecastRequest.title: ForecastRequest
ForecastRequest.description:
What a four you composed yourself would leave on court.

**This route creates no search and records nothing.** Re-posting `/lineups`
per swap would enter a six-edit builder session into *searches run* as six
searches, which is a lie in the one table the product uses to judge itself.

`search_id` is **required**, and every player named must have appeared in
that search's returned rows. Unbounded, this would be a level lookup for any
player in the city reachable by id; bounded, it tells you nothing the
shortlist did not already show you.

ForecastResponse.title: ForecastResponse
ForecastResponse.description:
Three arrangements of a four you composed. **And no `search_id`.**

Nothing was searched and nothing was recorded, so there is no id to read this
back by and no breakdown to open. The two version stamps cross because a
forecast nobody can reproduce is a number nobody should trust.

sigma_group.title: Sigma Group
sigma_group.description: The confidence is part of the claim, so it crosses with it

assumption.title: Assumption
assumption.description: What the provisional figure assumed, as a code the client renders in its own words. Null when nothing was assumed.

ForecastSchema.title: ForecastSchema
ForecastSchema.description:
How even a game is forecast to be. One type, everywhere it appears.

``provisional`` travels **inside** the forecast rather than beside it: the
failure being guarded against is a screen showing the number without its
caveat, and a sibling boolean is exactly how the two get separated in a
refactor.

ForgotPasswordRequest.title: ForgotPasswordRequest
ForgotPasswordRequest.description: *Forgot password?*: the address to send a link and a code to.

home_club.title: Home Club
home_club.description: The group's home club, listed first.

distance_km.title: Distance Km
distance_km.description: How far it is from the poster; `null` with no Location area.

book_by.title: Book By
book_by.description: The latest the post can fill.

courts.title: Courts
courts.description: How many courts of the sport are free then.

fits_free.title: Fits Free
fits_free.description: Its own *n free*: the poster's best fits free at this hour.

FreeCourtSchema.title: FreeCourtSchema
FreeCourtSchema.description: One *Free courts* row: a club and hour the post could be made at.

GameKind.title: GameKind
GameKind.description:
Whether this game is evidence about how well anybody plays.

**Stamped at the plan and never derived at the end.** ADR-0049's fourth
rejected option is the reason: *a friendly is a thing people choose*, and
reclassifying a counted game because nobody typed a score hands a player the
exact evening they said they did not want, and gives one word two meanings —
what you chose, and what you failed to record.

GameListResponse.title: GameListResponse
GameListResponse.description:
Your games, newest arrangement first.

**One list and not several.** A game awaiting an entry, one awaiting an
answer and one that never happened are one thing at three moments of its
life, and splitting them would make the client's shelves the platform's
opinion about which of them matters.

``read_at`` is the instant every standing and deadline here was folded
against. It travels so a client's countdowns and the standings beside them
cannot come from two different readings of the clock.

GameOutcome.title: GameOutcome
GameOutcome.description:
How one counted game went for the person the record is about. **Two.**

*Unscored* is not a third value: a game nobody agreed a score for produced no
outcome for anybody, and the absence is spelled by not being in the run at
all (``docs/adr/0137``).

**A second spelling of ``games``' own ``Outcome``**, mapped at the adapter
that reads it — which is the shape ``matchmaking``'s ``GameResult`` already
takes for the same two words, and this context's standing rule about
borrowing another context's domain types (``docs/adr/0159``). The risk is the
same one ``OnCourtVerdict`` carries and it is answered the same way:
``tests/unit/test_player_record_skill.py`` fails the build if the two
vocabularies stop agreeing.

GamePairingAtStakeSchema.title: GamePairingAtStakeSchema
GamePairingAtStakeSchema.description:
What a **counted** game on this court would do to your Level.

The rating engine's own update rule read forward, **side against side** —
the pair the result will deliver if the game is played, and the same pair
for everybody on your side.

sigma_group.title: Sigma Group
sigma_group.description: The confidence is part of the claim, so it crosses with it.

assumption.title: Assumption
assumption.description: What the provisional figure assumed, as a code the client renders in its own words. Null when nothing was assumed — which, on a game, is always.

GamePairingForecastSchema.title: GamePairingForecastSchema
GamePairingForecastSchema.description:
How even this court's game is forecast to be, **read in your direction**.

``provisional`` travels inside the forecast rather than beside it, on the
engine's own rule: the failure guarded against is a screen showing the
number without its caveat. **It is never `true` on a game today** — a
line-up is frozen at the plan, so no side is short — and the field is kept
because the shape is the court's. When a seat can be open, the answer is
*omitted*, never provisional.

GamePairingRangeSchema.title: GamePairingRangeSchema
GamePairingRangeSchema.description:
The likely range a seat's Level sits in — μ ± σ as RacketSkill published it.

Named for its surface rather than reusing the card's ``LikelyRangeSchema``:
a second class of that name would not shadow the card's in the contract, it
would rename it (``docs/adr/0159``'s rule, one context over).

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant the game's standing was folded at and the pairing computed against.

forecast.description: How even the game is forecast to be, in your direction. **Omitted when the pairing cannot be computed**, and always together with `split`.

split.description: The evidence behind `pct`: between what and what, on the scale you already read Levels on. **Omitted together with `forecast`.**

at_stake.description: What a counted result would do to your Level. **Omitted on a friendly** — meaningless rather than unavailable — and omitted where you hold no rating in this sport, or nobody on the other side does. A side with one unrated seat is priced over the people on it who are rated, because that is what the result will do. Never a pair of zeros.

seats.title: Seats
seats.description: One row per seat whose person holds a rating in this sport, in the court's own order. Somebody unrated is simply not here.

GamePairingResponse.title: GamePairingResponse
GamePairingResponse.description:
What this platform makes of your court, computed when you asked.

**Read beside the game and stored nowhere.** Everything here is as-of-now
and means what a card means *because this game has not happened*; the route
refuses once it has. Nothing on `GET /games` changes: a seat there still
carries a name and nothing else.

**Three blocks, and each is omitted on its own ground.** `forecast` and
`split` go together — one computation — and are omitted when the pairing
cannot be computed: somebody on the court holds no rating in the sport, or
a seat could not be priced. There is no reason beside the absence; draw
nothing and say nothing. `at_stake` is omitted on a friendly, where a
counted result is *meaningless rather than unavailable*, and where the rule
has nothing to move or nothing to price against — you hold no rating in
the sport, or nobody across the net does. `seats` names the Level of
everybody the platform holds one for, and a court with an unrated member
still names the rated ones.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level, as RacketSkill published it.

band.title: Band
band.description: The Level band's published name, as a key — RacketSkill's own vocabulary, exactly as the player card and the record print it. The band's numeric edges are **not** here: they are not a second range to compare `range` against.

range.description: The likely range their Level sits in, as the play card ships it. **The client computes nothing** — not this from `confidence`, and not a band from `level`.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: How sure the platform is, as a whole percentage — `rating`'s own figure and never re-derived here.

GamePairingSeatSchema.title: GamePairingSeatSchema
GamePairingSeatSchema.description:
One seat on the court and the Level of the person in it.

**This is not a card**, and it is not the seat on `GET /games` either — that
one carries a name and nothing else (``docs/adr/0141``), and it is
untouched. What is here is the four figures a record's skill panel and a
player card already publish, read beside the game for as long as the game
has not happened.

GamePairingSplitSchema.title: GamePairingSplitSchema
GamePairingSplitSchema.description:
The two side strengths the forecast was read from, **in your direction**.

`your_side` is yours wherever you sit, and `gap` is `your_side − their_side`
— **signed and served**, so two readers on opposite sides see the sign flip
and neither subtracts two rounded figures the engine subtracted unrounded.
A side's strength is not the mean of the people on it, which is why these
are numbers only the engine has.

GameResult.title: GameResult
GameResult.description:
How one counted game went for one of the people who played it.

**The matcher's own word for it**, as ``PairwiseOutcome`` is for the
familiarity term's tallies, and mapped from ``games``' own ``Outcome`` at the
adapter that reads it. Two values and never a third: a game with no agreed
result produces no result for anybody, and absence is spelled by not being in
the run at all (``docs/adr/0137``).

It is here rather than beside the port that answers it because a run of form
is **recorded**, and every other word a row is written in is declared in this
file.

challenge_id.title: Challenge Id
challenge_id.description: The ask whose line-up completed into this game

kind.description: Whether this evening is evidence. **Chosen when the game was arranged and never derived at the end** — a game nobody scored stays counted, because a friendly is a thing people choose.

window.description: How soon the week this was arranged for came round. ``null`` on a game born of a mutual yes: no grid was proposed from.

standing.description: What this game is at the instant it was read. **Derived from the record and the clock, never stored**, so it is right for the whole gap between a deadline and anything noticing.

planned_at.title: Planned At
planned_at.description: When the last seat accepted and this became a game

played_at.title: Played At
played_at.description: When somebody said it happened. **The entry carries the moment** — there is no booking and no calendar, so this is the moment of the entry itself. ``null`` while nobody has said so.

entry_closes_at.title: Entry Closes At
entry_closes_at.description: When *we played* stops being sayable and the game becomes a game that never happened. ``null`` once somebody has said it happened, and ``null`` on a game that was called off — the window no longer matters, and a card that shelved itself by it would stay for eight days.

called_off_at.title: Called Off At
called_off_at.description: When somebody called it off, while a seat was open (``docs/adr/0163``). ``null`` unless the standing is `CALLED_OFF`; then the act's own instant, which is what the ending card is shelved from — a day later, as `played_at` and `entry_closes_at` already shelve the other endings. Who is `called_off_by`.

called_off_by.description: The player who called it off, and their name (``docs/adr/0172`` §4). ``null`` on every standing but `CALLED_OFF`. The last leaver, whose seat is drawn open — or whoever pressed *Call it off*, who still holds one; which of the two is read off the seats, and the game screen's heading is keyed on it.

seats.title: Seats
seats.description: The court, in the order the challenge handed it over

score.description: The agreed score. ``null`` until something settles on one — including while a lone score is still waiting, because a score nobody has answered yet is not the result.
