outcome.description: Win or loss **for you**. ``null`` for every standing but a confirmed one: a game nobody scored moves nobody's Level and has no outcome to give anybody.

proposals.title: Proposals
proposals.description: The scores on the table, **side A's first and never in the order they arrived**. Empty unless the game is awaiting an answer: before that nobody has entered one, and after it the ending is on `standing` — a confirmed score is `score` and an unscored game is an evening, not a transcript of the argument. Two entries **is** the disagreement, and either side may agree with the other's.

acceptance.description: The agreement that is waiting out its grace, and `null` when none is. **A counter voids one**, so this is what still stands rather than what was once recorded.

no_shows.title: No Shows
no_shows.description: Everybody reported as not coming to this **booked** game, in the court's order (#547). Empty on every other game. A report is the game's entry: no score is on the table beside one, and **the game does not count** whatever it comes to.

GameSchema.title: GameSchema
GameSchema.description: One game, its court, and what it is right now.

GameSide.title: GameSide
GameSide.description: Which side of the net. **Two, and the game names one of them.**

GameStanding.title: GameStanding
GameStanding.description: The nine standings, as codes. A client's words are the client's own.

games_per_week.title: Games Per Week
games_per_week.description: Games a week, Monday to Sunday, from 1 to 7.

most_ill_pay_grosze.title: Most Ill Pay Grosze
most_ill_pay_grosze.description: The most one game's share may cost, in grosze — one of `most_ill_pay_choices_grosze` — or `null` for *off*.

GamesAndMoneyRequest.title: GamesAndMoneyRequest
GamesAndMoneyRequest.description:
Both values, as the screen saves them on every tap. **Types only**: a
value the form does not offer is refused by the domain, with a code naming
what it offers.

games_per_week.title: Games Per Week
games_per_week.description: Once this many games are booked in a week (Monday to Sunday), the deck deals nothing more for it.

most_ill_pay_grosze.title: Most Ill Pay Grosze
most_ill_pay_grosze.description: Cards whose share is above this, in grosze, are never dealt; `null` is *off* — every card is shown.

most_ill_pay_choices_grosze.title: Most Ill Pay Choices Grosze
most_ill_pay_choices_grosze.description: The ceilings offered beside *Off*, in grosze.

GamesAndMoneyResponse.title: GamesAndMoneyResponse
GamesAndMoneyResponse.description:
You › Account › **Games & money**: the player's two limits, and what the
form offers so the client holds neither range.

Gender.title: Gender
Gender.description:
What a player says about themselves — self-declared, freely changed.

Per person and never per sport, which is what keeps it on ``PlayerProfile``
rather than beside a rating (ADR-0089's cardinality, unchanged).

This is **a statement about which searches a player wishes to appear in**,
not a ruling by the platform on who anybody is. A player whose identity is
not on this list picks the answer that puts them where they want to be seen,
or takes ``PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY`` and appears in unconstrained searches only.
The platform adjudicates nothing.

GenderPreference.title: GenderPreference
GenderPreference.description:
Who a player is willing to be matched with — durable, not per search.

**Durable rather than per-search because the gate is mutual.** It has to be
evaluated against a player when somebody *else* searches and they are not
present, and a per-search setting cannot bind that direction at all. A
per-search override may **narrow** this, never widen past it.

kind.description: `PLAYER` — a player's own group, with an Owner. `OFFICIAL` — a club's, one per WhatsApp group, run by one of its Administrators: **no Owner**, and its sports are the ones it declares.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sport dots, in the registry's order. **A player group's**: each sport **at least two** members hold a Skill rating in, read when the group is read — a rating earned or a member leaving moves them on the next read. **An official group's**: the sports it declares.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: Every Group member — a player group's Owner, and the Administrator who joined an official group as a player, included. The same for every reader.

join_policy.description: `ANYONE` — *Join* admits at once (*anyone can join*); `PEOPLE_I_APPROVE` — *Ask to join* leaves a request for the Owner (*Karol approves joins*).

owner_name.title: Owner Name
owner_name.description: The Owner's **whole Name**, never the nickname — who answers a request, for the *approves joins* line. **No first name is cut from it, here or by a client**: a sentence naming somebody uses the whole Name (`docs/adr/0171` §4), so the line reads *Karol Nowak approves joins* and the row truncates it as it truncates any line. `null` for an account that can no longer be named — and **always `null` on an official group**, which has no Owner: its line names `administrator_name`.

administrator_name.title: Administrator Name
administrator_name.description: **An official group's** *approves joins* line: the whole name the club gave the Administrator running it now — *Administrator Marta Wójcik approves joins* — cut by nobody, as `owner_name` is. `null` while nobody runs it, and **always `null` on a player group**, whose line names `owner_name`.

is_administrator.title: Is Administrator
is_administrator.description: Whether **the reader** runs this official group. Their tap is **Join**, never *Ask to join*: they are admitted at once whatever `join_policy` says — they would otherwise be asking themselves. Always `false` on a player group.

relation.description: `MEMBER` — the reader is in it (*you're in*); `REQUESTED` — they asked and their request is waiting (*requested · waiting*); `NONE` — neither, and *Join* or *Ask to join* is the tap. **A declined request reads `NONE`**: nothing tells them it was declined, and they may ask again.

GroupAtClubSchema.title: GroupAtClubSchema
GroupAtClubSchema.description: A group inside a club's card, with what it is to the reader.

segments.title: Segments
segments.description: The segments the reader's Play intent shows, Competitive first — **empty while they have declared no intent for the sport**, which is the one question that replaces the deck.

games_badge.title: Games Badge
games_badge.description: The tab's badge: cards where somebody is already In with the reader, across the segments.

capped_weeks.title: Capped Weeks
capped_weeks.description: Weeks within the deck's fortnight at the reader's games per week — *your 2 games this week are booked*. None of their games is dealt.

cards.title: Cards
cards.description: This segment's cards in the order dealt: seats open after the reader's yes (fewest first), then seat open › challenge › pick, then the soonest deadline, then the best forecast; the same people only at their best hour.

GroupDeckResponse.title: GroupDeckResponse
GroupDeckResponse.description: A group's **Games** tab for one sport and segment.

GroupKind.title: GroupKind
GroupKind.description:
The two kinds of Group (``docs/adr/0183`` §1), and every rule that differs
between them says which it binds rather than reading a null.

A **player group** has an Owner who created it and plays whatever its
members are rated in. An **official group** belongs to a club, has **no
Owner** — one Administrator runs it — and **declares** its sports and the
size of the WhatsApp group it mirrors (§3).

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole Name, never the nickname. `null` for an account that can no longer be named — the member keeps their seat.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Their current photograph. Omitted when they have none, and omitted together with `photo_url` — draw their initials.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived signed link to that photograph, minted for **this response**.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level in the sport asked for, as RacketSkill published it. Always present: somebody not rated in it is not listed.

player_score.title: Player Score
player_score.description: Their published Player Score, 0–100 — the figure their record and a player card print. **Omitted for somebody the platform has watched nothing of**, never `0`: no record is not a bad one.

is_owner.title: Is Owner
is_owner.description: Whether they own the group — the row the **admin** tag is drawn on in a player group.

is_administrator.title: Is Administrator
is_administrator.description: Whether they run this **official** group as its Administrator, and joined it as a player — the row the **admin** tag is drawn on in an official group, second after the reader as an Owner is. Always `false` on a player group.

joined_at.title: Joined At
joined_at.description: When they joined — this stay: somebody who left and came back counts from their return.

GroupMemberSchema.title: GroupMemberSchema
GroupMemberSchema.description: One row of Members, for one sport — *Padel 2,71 · score 92*.

sport.description: The sport the list was asked for.

members.title: Members
members.description: **Only the members rated in `sport`**: the reader first, then the Owner — or the Administrator running an official group, once they joined it as a player — then everybody else **newest joined first**. **A blocked pair, either way round, is left out of each other's list** — and nothing says so: the group's `member_count` is the same for every reader, so it may be more than the rows here. Empty when nobody in the group the reader may see is rated in it.

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole Name, never the nickname. `null` for an account that can no longer be named — the member keeps their seat.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Their current photograph. Omitted when they have none, and omitted together with `photo_url` — draw their initials.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived signed link to that photograph, minted for **this response**.

GroupPersonSchema.title: GroupPersonSchema
GroupPersonSchema.description: A member's face — **a name and a photograph, and nothing else**.

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole Name, never the nickname. `null` for an account that can no longer be named — the member keeps their seat.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Their current photograph. Omitted when they have none, and omitted together with `photo_url` — draw their initials.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived signed link to that photograph, minted for **this response**.

joined_at.title: Joined At
joined_at.description: When they joined — this stay. The app prints *this week* within seven days, and the date after.

GroupPlayerSchema.title: GroupPlayerSchema
GroupPlayerSchema.description:
One player on an official group's page — rows are not tappable, and
nobody can be removed.

GroupReason.title: GroupReason
GroupReason.description:
Why this four beat the runner-up. **One closed code, never a number.**

``G`` chose these four over the other combinations and the third refusal —
*never a number it cannot explain in one sentence with the evidence named* —
applies. A second score the player must trust is worse than none: it competes
with Fit and nobody can act on it. So the evidence half is paid here, by the
term with the largest margin between the winning combination and the
runner-up — the group analogue of the card's top three reasons
(``docs/adr/0117``).

Closed vocabulary and ``docs/adr/0106``-shaped: **the client writes the
sentence, the engine names which.**

GroupRelation.title: GroupRelation
GroupRelation.description:
What a group is to the person reading it (``docs/adr/0183`` §9): they
are in it, they have asked and their Join request is waiting, or neither.

**A declined request reads as ``NONE``** — the request is gone, and nothing
tells them it was declined (``docs/adr/0183`` §7).

kind.description: `PLAYER` — a player's own group, with an Owner. `OFFICIAL` — a club's, one per WhatsApp group, run by one of its Administrators: **no Owner**, and its sports are the ones it declares.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sport dots, in the registry's order. **A player group's**: each sport **at least two** members hold a Skill rating in, read when the group is read — a rating earned or a member leaving moves them on the next read. **An official group's**: the sports it declares.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: Every Group member — a player group's Owner, and the Administrator who joined an official group as a player, included. The same for every reader.

link.title: Link
link.description: The Group link: the public site's address, `/join/` and the group's code. **It never changes** — not on a rename, a policy change or a handover.

is_owner.title: Is Owner
is_owner.description: Whether the reader is the group's Owner. Always `false` on an official group, which has none.

declared_sports.title: Declared Sports
declared_sports.description: **An official group's** declared sports, in the registry's order — what it plays, so the sport filter narrows to the ones the reader is rated in among these, and a reader rated in none of them is shown what to add. **Omitted on a player group**, which plays whatever its members are rated in.

rated_by_sport.title: Rated By Sport
rated_by_sport.description: **Every sport**, in the registry's order — one the group has no dot for too, because the reader may be rated in it and open it.

member_faces.title: Member Faces
member_faces.description: The Info tab's members row: **up to five** faces of everybody but the reader, in the Members list's order — the Owner, then newest joined first — with a blocked pair, either way round, left out, as the list it opens leaves them out. Empty for a reader alone (`member_count` 1), whose row draws their own face — and empty too, with `member_count` above 1, when a block hides everybody else. `member_count` is the group's, so its *+N* counts everybody.

administrator_name.title: Administrator Name
administrator_name.description: **An official group's** *approves joins* line, as a club's card says it: the whole Name of the Administrator running it now. **`null` while it needs an administrator** — the line then names the home club, *Ogrody 33 approves joins*, and requests wait for a handover — and **always `null` on a player group**, whose line names its Owner.

is_administrator.title: Is Administrator
is_administrator.description: Whether **the reader** runs this official group — who joined it as a player: *you approve joins*, answered from the administrator profile. Always `false` on a player group.

GroupResponse.title: GroupResponse
GroupResponse.description: A group, as one of its members opens it.

rated_count.title: Rated Count
rated_count.description: How many members hold a Skill rating in it.

first_rated.title: First Rated
first_rated.description: The first members to join who are rated in it, in joining order — **at most as many as the sport seats**, the faces that fill its seats.

GroupSportSchema.title: GroupSportSchema
GroupSportSchema.description: One sport's *N of M* for the Games tab.

waiting_count.title: Waiting Count
waiting_count.description: How many Join requests wait on it — the queue the handover gave.

HandoverSchema.title: HandoverSchema
HandoverSchema.description:
A group the club handed this account that it has not been told about —
*Ogrody 33 made you the administrator of Ogrody 33 Club*.

group_ids.title: Group Ids
group_ids.description: The `group_id` of each handover the sheet named, from `/users/me`'s `profiles.handovers`. A group handed on meanwhile, told about already or not theirs is stepped over.

HandoversSeenRequest.title: HandoversSeenRequest
HandoversSeenRequest.description: The groups the sheet told the Administrator about (``docs/adr/0192``).

clubs.title: Clubs
clubs.description: Nearest first, then by name — or A–Z for a reader with no Location area.

next_page.title: Next Page
next_page.description: The page to ask for next, or `null` when this was the last.

booking_id.title: Booking Id
booking_id.description: The booking — the same id the game had while it filled. `GET /bookings/{id}` for its details.

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The ordinary Game it opened: the result is told and agreed on `/games/{id}/result`, and its room in `GET /conversations` carries this id. `null` while it waits for its On request club, and on a request the club never booked — there is no Game, and no room.

pool_id.title: Pool Id
pool_id.description: The pool it filled in — a group's id.

status.description: `WAITING_FOR_THE_CLUB` — an On request club has the full game and has not answered: nobody has paid, there is no Game yet (`game_id` is `null`) and no court given. `BOOKED` — full and booked, its hour still ahead. `NEEDS_RESULT` — its hour has come and nobody has said it happened. `CONFIRM_THE_RESULT` — a score is on the table. `COUNTED` — a score is agreed. `UNCOUNTED` — they played and no score is agreed. `NEVER_PLAYED` — nobody said it happened in time. `CALLED_OFF` — it will not be played; `called_off_reason` says why. `SEAT_OPEN` — somebody left and the seat is offered (`open_seats`); before the cut-off (`money.free_to_leave_until`) *fills by then or the game is off and everyone is refunded*, after it *the game goes ahead*. A game whose hour comes with a seat still open is `UNCOUNTED` with `uncounted_reason` `SEAT_EMPTY`.

called_off_reason.description: Why a `CALLED_OFF` game will not be played — `null` on every other status. `REFUSED` — the On request club refused it. `NO_ANSWER` — the club did not answer in time. In both nobody paid. (A seat opening while it waited takes the request back instead: it leaves Home, and the people still In find the game filling again in their live yeses.) `SHORT_AT_THE_CUT_OFF` — a seat that opened before the club's cut-off was still empty at it: everybody still in is refunded in full (`money.refunded_grosze`); read off the clock from the cut-off on. `CANCELLED_BY_THE_CLUB` — the club cancelled it, with its reason (`club_cancel_reason`): everybody still in is refunded in full (`money.refunded_grosze`), it is on nobody's record, and they are dealt a new card first (#547).

club_cancel_reason.description: Why the club cancelled a `CANCELLED_BY_THE_CLUB` game — `WEATHER`, `REPAIR`, `DOUBLE_BOOKING` or `OTHER` (no reason given). `null` on every other game.

uncounted_reason.description: Why an `UNCOUNTED` game is uncounted with nobody disagreeing about a score — `null` otherwise. `SEAT_EMPTY` — its hour came with a seat open: somebody left after the cut-off and nobody took the seat. No Level moved, and nothing is on the record of those who stayed. `NO_SHOW` — somebody who came reported a player who did not (#547): the reported player has a day to dispute it (`GET /games` — `no_shows`), after which it stands; the game does not count either way. A report every reported player disputed is an ordinary `UNCOUNTED`, with no reason: nobody arbitrated.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: Seats a leaver left open — the dashed tiles; nought unless `SEAT_OPEN`. The sides list the seats still held.

needs_you.title: Needs You
needs_you.description: One of the games that need the reader: a result to enter, the other side's score waiting on their agreement, or a seat open in their game.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start; games are 1 h.

court_name.title: Court Name
court_name.description: What the club calls the court — *Court 2*. `null` until the club gives it: an On request club gives it with its yes.

HomeGameSchema.title: HomeGameSchema
HomeGameSchema.description: One card on Home: a game the reader booked.

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant every status and money line here was folded against. Switch a card's line at `free_to_leave_until` from this clock.

needing_you.title: Needing You
needing_you.description: Home's badge — the games that need the reader: the cards with `needs_you`, and every payment they have to confirm (`GET /players/me/payments-to-confirm`), a game still filling whose seat is theirs until somebody else takes it.

games.title: Games
games.description: Every game the reader booked — and every game of theirs an On request club has, or had, to answer — **soonest first**, the ones that are over too; a client shelves an ended card as it chooses. A game a Classic play challenge opened is not here.

HomeResponse.title: HomeResponse
HomeResponse.description: **Home**: the reader's games from the moment they fill.

HomeStatus.title: HomeStatus
HomeStatus.description: What a game on Home is, right now (the mechanics §14.1).

InProgressAssessmentResponse.title: InProgressAssessmentResponse
InProgressAssessmentResponse.description:
One unfinished run: which assessment, and which sport it is for.

Carries no question, no result and no progress. A caller reading this is
deciding *where to send the player*; it re-reads the run it routes to, and
that read is the one that reproduces the outstanding question.

InProgressAssessmentsResponse.title: InProgressAssessmentsResponse
InProgressAssessmentsResponse.description:
Every unfinished run this player holds — empty when they hold none.

Empty is the ordinary answer for a new account and for a player who has
finished everything they started, so it is a 200 with an empty list rather
than a 404 or the singular form's 204.

Ordered by the sport registry, so a caller that wants one run can take the
first entry.

their_intent.description: The candidate's declaration for this sport

aligned.title: Aligned
aligned.description: Whether the two read the same evening

IntentAlignmentEvidence.title: IntentAlignmentEvidence
IntentAlignmentEvidence.description:
What kind of evening each of them is after.

**Intent is a weight and not a gate.** A candidate who declared the opposite
loses the term's entire weight and takes no further charge — the zero is the
whole answer, and a second dock would be a gate wearing a modifier's clothes.
A candidate who has *not* declared has the term dropped and renormalised away
instead, so declaring against the searcher already costs strictly more than
saying nothing.

outgoing.title: Outgoing
outgoing.description: Yeses you sent that are still in flight, newest first. Every one carries its own `expires_at`.

mutual.title: Mutual
mutual.description: Yeses you sent that came back. **Both of you said it**, which is the only way somebody else's yes reaches you at all.

outstanding.title: Outstanding
outstanding.description: One entry per sport, always — the count and the cap in force. Sent before you are near the limit, on purpose.

InterestListResponse.title: InterestListResponse
InterestListResponse.description:
Your own *Let's play* screen. **Outgoing and mutuals only.**

There is no incoming list and there will not be one: a yes nobody has
answered stays silent, which is what makes saying yes low-stakes. The two
lists are disjoint — a yes that came back is in `mutual` and not in
`outgoing` — so a client renders both without deriving either.

InvitationByTokenRequest.title: InvitationByTokenRequest
InvitationByTokenRequest.description:
The token off an invitation's link. In a body rather than a path, so it
is in no access log.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name the club typed.

state.description: `valid`, `expired` (ask the club to send a new one), `used`, or `locked` — five wrong codes.

InvitationByTokenResponse.title: InvitationByTokenResponse
InvitationByTokenResponse.description:
What a link opens, before anything is set: the email *Set your
password* locks its field to, whom it greets, and whether it still
works.

InvitationLinkState.title: InvitationLinkState
InvitationLinkState.description:
Whether an invitation's link still works — the credential's standing,
under a name of its own on the wire (``Standing`` is a challenge's).

InvitationPasswordRequest.title: InvitationPasswordRequest
InvitationPasswordRequest.description:
*Set your password*, and **exactly one** of what opens the way to it:
the `token` from the email's link, or the `ticket` a claimed code returned.

The password carries no bound here: the rule every account shares — 8 to
128 characters with a letter and a digit — is refused as
`password_too_weak` naming the field. Sending both or neither of `token`
and `ticket` is the one refusal here that is a `422`.

JoinPolicy.title: JoinPolicy
JoinPolicy.description:
Who gets in (``docs/adr/0183`` §7).

**Anyone** admits a player the moment they join, and is the default the New
group form opens on. **People I approve** turns a join into a Join request
its Owner answers.

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole Name, never the nickname. `null` for an account that can no longer be named — the member keeps their seat.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Their current photograph. Omitted when they have none, and omitted together with `photo_url` — draw their initials.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A short-lived signed link to that photograph, minted for **this response**.

levels.title: Levels
levels.description: **Every sport they are rated in**, in the registry's order, each with its Level — *Padel 2,44 · Tennis 2,60*. Empty for somebody rated in nothing.

JoinRequestSchema.title: JoinRequestSchema
JoinRequestSchema.description:
A Join request as the Owner sees it: who is asking — ``player_id`` is the
id to approve or decline — and what they play. **No Player Score**: the
request card is club 20's everywhere.

requests.title: Requests
requests.description: Everybody waiting to be let in, **in the order they asked** — *Want to join · N*. Empty when nobody is waiting.

clubs.title: Clubs
clubs.description: Nearest first, then by name — or A–Z for a reader with no Location area. Empty when nothing matched.

next_page.title: Next Page
next_page.description: The page to ask for next, or `null` when this was the last.

read_as.description: What the text was read as. `LINK` — it held `/join/` and a code, and the answer is exactly that group; **`LINK` with no clubs is *nothing at that link***, a link that leads nowhere. `TEXT` — matched against clubs, districts and group names; `TEXT` with no clubs is *no match*.

Leaving.title: Leaving
Leaving.description:
What *Leave the game* does, by when it is pressed (the mechanics §13) —
said on the details before, and answered by the act after.

kind.description: `BEFORE_THE_CUT_OFF` — *You'll be refunded 38,40 zł now (the 1,60 zł card fee isn't returned). Your seat is offered to others. On your record only if the game is then called off.* `AFTER_THE_CUT_OFF` — *Your seat is offered to others. You'll be refunded 38,40 zł when someone takes it; if nobody does, you won't be. On your record if nobody takes it.* `WHILE_WAITING_FOR_THE_CLUB` — *Nobody has paid yet. Leaving withdraws your yes.* The same words the departure answers with.

refund_grosze.title: Refund Grosze
refund_grosze.description: What comes back — the share less the card fee; nought when nobody paid.

card_fee_grosze.title: Card Fee Grosze
card_fee_grosze.description: The card fee that isn't returned — the provider's standard price, an estimate; what it kept is on the receipt.

LeavingSchema.title: LeavingSchema
LeavingSchema.description: What *Leave the game* would cost now (the mechanics §13).

LevelDirection.title: LevelDirection
LevelDirection.description:
Which side of the searcher a candidate's Level sits on.

A code and not a sign on ``delta``, because the client's sentence differs in
all three cases and a renderer deriving *"above"* from a sign is the display
logic the presentation boundary exists to keep out.

It lives here rather than beside the wire shape for the reason
``EvidenceKind`` does: the engine computes it and the schema publishes it, so
a second spelling on the schema's side would be two answers to *which way is
up*. A module may import an engine; the reverse is the fence.

LevelFitEvidence.title: LevelFitEvidence
LevelFitEvidence.description:
How far apart the two levels are, and which way.

The tolerance behind the curve is absolute on μ and never reads a band: the
shipped bands are deliberately uneven because *evidence* is unevenly
available down the scale, not because a tenth of a point means less at the
top.

LevelRangeSchema.title: LevelRangeSchema
LevelRangeSchema.description: A range of Levels, both bounds included.

LikelyRangeSchema.title: LikelyRangeSchema
LikelyRangeSchema.description:
The **likely range** — μ ± σ, clamped to the scale — as `rating` published it.

Nested rather than two flat fields, because a range is one value with two
edges and the rating routes already spell it this way; a card that carried
``range_low`` and ``range_high`` loose beside ``level`` would be the same
fact in a second shape.

**The client computes nothing here.** It is projected onto the index row
from ``rating.rating_initialised`` and copied onto the card, because
``likely_range()`` returns unrounded values and the rounding lives in the
engine — a range derived anywhere else is a second set of drawing constants.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description:
Ranked. **An empty list is a `200`** — the honest empty state is an answer, not a failure.

A read-back may carry withheld rows: the record is immutable and the gates are live, so a row the product has since agreed not to show keeps its place and states that it is withheld. Branch on `withheld` — a fresh search never carries one.

LineupResponse.title: LineupResponse
LineupResponse.description:
The shortlist's envelope, the pool, and the court seated out of it.

One envelope and one row shape across every surface, so the read-back has one
renderer to reproduce: what a line-up adds is the seating, not a second way
of describing a person. `candidates` is the **pool** ⚡ seated from — in Fit
order, up to the ruleset's own candidate cap, the seated among them — and
not the seated alone, so *Pick players myself* on this answer has the rest
of the ranking to offer ([#407](https://github.com/Raketa02/Raketa/issues/407)).

seats.title: Seats
seats.description: The court as it currently stands, seat by seat, in the arrangement marked `is_current`.

arrangements.title: Arrangements
arrangements.description: Every way round, each with its own forecast. Empty only when nobody could be seated at all.

group_reason.description: Why this four beat the runner-up, as one closed code the client writes the sentence for. **Omitted when there was no runner-up** — one admissible four is not a four that won an argument.

dock.description: `NO_SHARED_SLOTS` when the four of you have no hour in common. **A dock, never a refusal**: nobody is removed from the court for it, and the honest line is that you would all have to bend.

LineupSchema.title: LineupSchema
LineupSchema.description:
The court, every way round it can sit, and one reason it won.

**A partial line-up is this shape with fewer people in it** — never a
different one, and never an error. *Nobody* is this shape with every seat
carrying a reason, so a client renders one thing.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who is in this seat, to look up in `candidates[]`. **Omitted on an open seat**, and on your own — you are not a row of your own search.

unfilled_reason.description:
Why this seat is empty. **A seat is never filled below the quality floor to complete a four**, a newcomer least of all — *three of four* is an honest answer, and so is nobody.

`NO_ADMISSIBLE_COMBINATION` is the one worth reading twice: there were people, and no four of you could share a court. Omitted on a seat that is taken.

LineupSeatSchema.title: LineupSeatSchema
LineupSeatSchema.description:
One place on the court, with the person in it or the reason it is empty.

**The person is named by id and their breakdown rides once**, in
`candidates[]` — the same list every other surface returns, carrying **the
same number the shortlist showed**, because nothing is re-scored behind your
back when somebody sits down. Four breakdowns repeated across a court and
three arrangements is four chances for two copies to disagree, on a payload
that is already tens of kilobytes.

v.title: V
v.description: The envelope version, **carried from the first frame**. `1` today. A client parses the shape it shipped with until that build is gone from phones, so this is what a later shape is told apart by.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: The room that moved. It is the room this stream is for — a stream carries one room and there is deliberately no second stream for the Chats list.

last_seq.title: Last Seq
last_seq.description: How long the room is now. **News, not a cursor.** Fetch from your own high-water mark, never from this number: a client that paged from here would reintroduce exactly the hole the nudge exists to close. `0` is a room where nothing has landed yet, which a stream opened on a freshly-opened room genuinely reports.

LiveNudgeSchema.title: LiveNudgeSchema
LiveNudgeSchema.description:
**The whole live contract: a nudge, and nothing else on the wire.**

``docs/adr/0147`` §3. One of these is written into
``GET /conversations/{id}/stream`` whenever the room moves, and one is
written the moment the stream opens carrying the room's current `last_seq`.

**It carries no content, ever.** Not a message, not a system line, not a plan
slot. On receiving one, fetch from **your own** high-water mark through the
ordinary read path — never from `last_seq`. That is what makes a dropped
frame free: the next nudge repairs it, because your cursor is yours.

**Which also means there is nothing here to render.** Whether the UI may draw
something it did not read from the authenticated read path stops being a rule
anybody keeps and becomes a thing this shape cannot express.

**The declaration is generated and the emission is not, and that hole is
named** (``docs/adr/0147`` §7). `make openapi` publishes this model into
`components.schemas`, the client generates **this type** from it, and the
drift and freshness checks cover the declaration. The *operation's* 200 comes
out of `openapi-typescript` as `unknown`, because a stream body is an
`itemSchema` that generator has no shape for — so the client's live port
parses each frame as this type by name, which is still generated and still
never hand-written. **What no check covers is the emission** — a stream body is
not a response model, and nothing type-checks the route against its own
annotation. The mitigation is structural rather than hoped for: the route
declares this model as its stream item, so the framework validates and
serialises every frame **through this model** before it reaches the wire. The
hole is narrowed, not closed, and the residual risk is that of a shape three
fields wide.

v.title: V
v.description: The envelope version, **the same `1` a nudge carries and unbumped by this frame's arrival**. A named event an installed client does not listen for never reaches it, so nothing about the shape it parses has changed.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: The room this is about — the room this stream is for

player_ids.title: Player Ids
player_ids.description: Who is typing **right now**, never including you. A list because a group chat has more than one possible typist; draw one indicator either way. **Empty means nobody is**, which is how an indicator goes away.

LiveTypingSchema.title: LiveTypingSchema
LiveTypingSchema.description:
**Somebody is typing**, and it is the second frame on the wire.

``docs/adr/0156``. It arrives when the answer changes and not on a tick, so a
room where nobody is typing produces nothing at all.

**It carries no `last_seq` and moves no sequence.** A typing frame is not an
entry: nothing was appended, nothing was locked, and the gapless allocator
behind `seq` was never asked for a number. A client must not advance any
cursor on one, and there is nothing here it could advance it to.

**It carries no name.** Fill names from the membership you are already
holding, exactly as every system line does — which is why a corrected
name fixes the indicator without a frame being re-sent.

**An empty list is the clear**, and it is the only clear there is: nobody
sends *stopped*, and the server reports whoever's heartbeat has not expired.
A room whose last typist's app was killed reports nobody within seconds,
through the same field and with nothing special about it.

name.title: Name
name.description: The club's name; `null` for a club that no longer exists.

pool_id.title: Pool Id
pool_id.description: The pool the game was dealt in — a group's id.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start. Every game is one hour.

share_grosze.title: Share Grosze
share_grosze.description: What this player is charged if the game fills, in grosze.

book_by.title: Book By
book_by.description: The latest moment the game can fill; past it the yes lapses.

LiveYesSchema.title: LiveYesSchema
LiveYesSchema.description: One yes on a game that has not filled.

cap_per_sport.title: Cap Per Sport
cap_per_sport.description: How many live yeses a player may have in one sport.

LiveYesesResponse.title: LiveYesesResponse
LiveYesesResponse.description:
You › Payments' **LIVE YESES**: every yes of the reader's on a game that
has not filled, across groups, soonest game first.

LivenessReason.title: LivenessReason
LivenessReason.description:
Why somebody moved, as a code. **Never as a number.**

Ten values: the eight printable signals, with the full inbox spelled as its
three coarse rungs instead of its own name. Their inbox depth is theirs — the
rung crosses and the count does not — and each rung names its own code, so a
threshold moving does not silently re-point a code at a different depth.

The two **silent** signals are absent by construction rather than by
omission: a silent move carries points and no code, so there is no name on
the value to print. ``tests/unit/test_matchmaking_shortlist_contract.py``
holds this enum to exactly the printable roster.

LocationAreaResource.title: LocationAreaResource
LocationAreaResource.description:
Where a player plays.

**What is sent and what is kept are not the same number.** A client sends the
fix its device gave it; the platform rounds to roughly a kilometre before
anything is recorded, and it is the rounded pair that comes back here. The
precise fix is never stored and never shareable
(``../../../../CONTEXT.md`` — *Location area*).

name.title: Name
name.description: What this player is called — what every screen says. `null` until the naming — except on an account an invitation opened, which carries the name the club typed. The entry gate's first destination is **not named in full**: no name, or no nickname — and the naming step asks only for what is missing.

nickname.title: Nickname
nickname.description: The handle, unique across the platform, drawn as `@nickname` under the name on the You tab and nowhere else. `null` until the naming.

is_tester.title: Is Tester
is_tester.description: Whether this account carries the **tester mark**: a real player who may be given a feature before anyone else. Set and cleared by an admin command, never by the player, and `false` for every account until then. **Not a role** — `authority` does not move with it. The player app passes it to flag evaluation as `isTester`, so no published datafile ever has to name a tester.

has_player_profile.title: Has Player Profile
has_player_profile.description: Whether this player has committed a Player profile — the fourth branch of the entry gate. Read from the profile's own event stream rather than from a projection, so it is correct immediately after the commit that creates one. False on a response that is not about the authenticated player, such as the one registration returns.

adult_attested.title: Adult Attested
adult_attested.description: Whether this account has given the Adult attestation. Every sign-up has; an account an invitation opened has not, and *Start playing* asks it first — `POST /users/me/adult-attestation`.

MeResponse.title: MeResponse
MeResponse.description:
``/me``: the account, and **which profiles it holds**
(``docs/adr/0185`` §2) — what the entry gate reads ahead of every
onboarding destination.

Its own shape rather than more fields on :class:`UserResponse`, because the
registration's answer is about an account one line old and has no honest
value for either: it holds no profile yet, and ``/me`` is where the gate
reads them.

type.title: Type
type.description: The discriminator. Two genuinely different shapes ride one ordered stream; this is not a `kind` on one shape (`docs/adr/0148` §4).

seq.title: Seq
seq.description: This entry's place in the conversation. **Gapless and starting at 1**, so `seq` 1 is the beginning of the room — which is why there is no `has_more`. Ordering, paging, de-duplication and reconnect all key on it, and **no reader may infer loss from a gap**: the promise is the server's and nothing may depend on it.

author_id.title: Author Id
author_id.description: Who typed it — a member, since only a member may send. **Name them from the `people` on the response that carried this page**, the one list every face on it is in, so a message and a line are named the same way.

text.title: Text
text.description: Their own words, unrendered and unchanged

client_message_id.title: Client Message Id
client_message_id.description: The id the sending client generated, echoed back. It does **two jobs**: the idempotency key for a resumed send, and the key an optimistic bubble is replaced on.

MessageSchema.title: MessageSchema
MessageSchema.description: What a player typed. **Content, crossing as-is.**

ModifierCode.title: ModifierCode
ModifierCode.description:
The three modifiers inside the budget, and the dock outside it.

Every one of them **prints**: a modifier that could move a score without
owing a sentence would be Liveness wearing stage 4's clothes, and Liveness
has a budget for exactly that.

ModifierSchema.title: ModifierSchema
ModifierSchema.description: One modifier that fired, and what it was worth on this pairing.

letters.title: Letters
letters.description: The first character of each of the first two words, as typed, or the first two characters of a one-word name: *my raketa group* is `mr`, *Ogrody 33 Club* is `O3`. Draw it as it comes — never change its case.

colour.title: Colour
colour.description: A colour **key** from 0 to 7, fixed for the group for ever — derived from its id, so a rename keeps it. Map it to your own palette; the backend never names a colour.

MonogramSchema.title: MonogramSchema
MonogramSchema.description:
The group's tile, **cut by the backend** so every client draws the same
one (``docs/adr/0183`` §5).

kind.description: `PLAYER` — a player's own group, with an Owner. `OFFICIAL` — a club's, one per WhatsApp group, run by one of its Administrators: **no Owner**, and its sports are the ones it declares.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: The sport dots, in the registry's order. **A player group's**: each sport **at least two** members hold a Skill rating in, read when the group is read — a rating earned or a member leaving moves them on the next read. **An official group's**: the sports it declares.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: Every Group member — a player group's Owner, and the Administrator who joined an official group as a player, included. The same for every reader.

MyGroupSchema.title: MyGroupSchema
MyGroupSchema.description: A card on the reader's Groups list.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Every group the reader belongs to, **newest joined first**. Empty for a player in none.

name.title: Name
name.description: What you are called — free text, spaces allowed, **never unique**: two players may share one. Trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed to one space, 2–64 characters after that. This is what every screen says about you.

nickname.title: Nickname
nickname.description: A handle: letters, digits and `. _ -`, no spaces, 2–64 characters, **unique across the platform** — refused with `nickname_already_taken` when another player holds it, admitted when it is already yours. Shown as `@nickname` under your name on your own You tab and on your record, and said nowhere else.

NameRequest.title: NameRequest
NameRequest.description:
The naming — *How should people see you?* (``docs/adr/0171`` §1–2).

Both fields, always: the naming is one act carrying both, and there is no
event for one without the other. The shape rules here are the value
objects' own, restated so the generated client type carries them — and
**the name is normalised before its bounds are checked**, exactly as
:class:`Name` normalises it, so ``"  Ania   Kowalska "`` is admitted and
recorded as ``Ania Kowalska`` and ``"   A   "`` is refused here as too
short. A bound checked on the raw string would admit the second and hand
it to the value object, which refuses it — a typed value meeting an
invariant, which is a 500 for a player's typo (``CONTEXT.md``, *Invariant
vs Unavailability*).

name.title: Name
name.description: The name as recorded: trimmed, collapsed.

NamingResponse.title: NamingResponse
NamingResponse.description:
What the naming recorded: the name as it now stands and the nickname.

Not a ``UserResponse``, deliberately — that shape carries
``has_player_profile``, a fact of another context's this write never asks
about, and ``false`` there would be a claim. The client re-reads ``/me``
before moving on (``docs/adr/0171`` §3); this is what lets it show the
normalised name back at once.

NewPasswordRequest.title: NewPasswordRequest
NewPasswordRequest.description:
The new password, and **exactly one** of what opens the way to it: the
`token` from the email's link, or the `ticket` a claimed code returned.

The password carries no bound here, deliberately: the rule every account
shares — 8 to 128 characters with a letter and a digit — is refused as
`password_too_weak` naming the field, not as a validation error naming none.
Sending both or neither of `token` and `ticket` is a malformed request rather
than a person's mistake, and is the one refusal here that is a `422`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Their whole name, as a seat carries it. ``null`` where ``users`` no longer has the account.

dispute_by.title: Dispute By
dispute_by.description: The end of their day to say they came — 24 hours from the report. **Nothing happens at this moment**: an undisputed report simply stands from here on, and the game reads `NO_SHOW` once every report has had its day.

disputed_at.title: Disputed At
disputed_at.description: When they disputed it. **Nobody arbitrates**: a disputed report falls and is on nobody's record; a game whose every report was disputed is `UNSCORED`.

NoShowSchema.title: NoShowSchema
NoShowSchema.description:
A player reported as not coming to this booked game (#547; the
mechanics §15.3) — and what became of it. **Who reported them is not
here**: the report is the game's, said by the people who came, and a name
on it would be the platform pointing at one of them.

NoticeKind.title: NoticeKind
NoticeKind.description: Every notice a player can be told (the mechanics §17.2).

given_at.title: Given At
given_at.description: When it was given — or when the day last bundled a notice into it, which is what moves it up the list.

opens.description: `BOOKING` — the booked game's details (`GET /bookings/{game_id}`); `PROPOSAL` — a game still filling, or one that did not (`GET /proposals/{game_id}`); `DECK` — the pool's deck in the sport and kind, with this card on top.

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The game it is about: its proposal's id, which its booking takes.

gathered.title: Gathered
gathered.description: How many more notices of its kind the day bundled into this one — told in its words, and pushed to nobody.

NoticeSchema.title: NoticeSchema
NoticeSchema.description: One notice, in the words the phone was pushed — and where a tap opens.

you_complete_it.title: You Complete It
you_complete_it.description: *You complete it* — a card needs only you. On until switched off; at most one a day, the rest bundled into it.

challenges_for_you.title: Challenges For You
challenges_for_you.description: *Challenges for you* — a member's post names you. On until switched off; at most three a day, the rest bundled into the third.

fill_in_alerts.title: Fill In Alerts
fill_in_alerts.description: *Fill in alerts* — a booked game you fit needs one more. Off until switched on; at most three a day.

NotificationChoicesSchema.title: NotificationChoicesSchema
NotificationChoicesSchema.description:
The three notices a player chooses. The seven that are always on are
no choice, and are not here.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: What the club offers, in the registry's order — **the sports an official group may declare**, so the form offers exactly these.

OfficialGroupClubSchema.title: OfficialGroupClubSchema
OfficialGroupClubSchema.description: The club an administrator acts for.

name.title: Name
name.description: *Same name as the WhatsApp group*: trimmed, runs of whitespace collapsed, then 1–40 characters. Refused with `group_name_invalid`, `details.field` `name`.

join_policy.description: `ANYONE` or `PEOPLE_I_APPROVE`. **Switching to `ANYONE` admits everybody waiting at once.**

whatsapp_size.title: Whatsapp Size
whatsapp_size.description: How many people the WhatsApp group has — **required**, a whole number from 2 to 1024. It limits nothing: more players than this is allowed and honest. Refused with `whatsapp_size_invalid`, `details.field` `whatsapp_size`.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description: What the group plays — **required**, and **only the club's**. Ticking one twice is ticking it. Refused with `group_sports_required` for none, or `sport_not_offered_by_club` with the sport in `details.sport` — `details.field` `sports` either way.

OfficialGroupSettingsRequest.title: OfficialGroupSettingsRequest
OfficialGroupSettingsRequest.description:
An official group's settings, **all four as the settings screen holds
them**, recorded together or not at all.

OnCourtVerdict.title: OnCourtVerdict
OnCourtVerdict.description:
What the on-court check concluded about a photograph. **Two values.**

The third state — *nobody looked* — is the **absence** of one of these and
never a third value, which is ``docs/adr/0138``'s rule: a shield saying
*checked and passed* cannot be drawn on a photograph nothing examined, and a
value meaning *unknown* is a value somebody eventually draws a tick for.

**The words are the ones a card already carries, and they are checked
against it.** This is a second spelling of ``player_profile``'s
``PhotoReviewDecision`` on purpose — this context imports no other context's
domain types — and a second spelling that drifts is worse than an import: a
client reading a search card and a record would get two words for one fact.
``tests/unit/test_player_record_identity.py`` fails the build if the two
vocabularies stop agreeing.

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The game this card is about. Post the answer to `/api/v1/sportsmanship/{game_id}`, and join it against `/api/v1/games` for the names, the sport and the date.

players.title: Players
players.description: Everybody else who was on that court, in the line-up's own order — in doubles both opponents **and** your partner, in singles the one opponent. Any of them may be left blank when you answer.

OpenCardSchema.title: OpenCardSchema
OpenCardSchema.description:
One court still waiting for this player's stars.

**Ids and nothing else.** What the people are called, which sport it was and
when it happened all come from the games list this card is drawn beside —
joined on ``game_id``, which is the same join the client already makes to
draw the game. Repeating them here would be a second copy of an evening's
description, and the day the two disagreed the card would name somebody the
game did not.

cards.title: Cards
cards.description: The courts still waiting for your stars. A card appears the day after the game and stays for seven days; ignoring one costs nothing.

OpenCardsResponse.title: OpenCardsResponse
OpenCardsResponse.description:
Every card waiting for you, **soonest to expire first**.

An empty list is the ordinary answer and means nothing is waiting. It does
not distinguish *no games*, *not yet a day* and *already answered*: all three
are simply not on the list, and none of them is something a client would draw
differently.

``cards`` is **required and never absent**, empty though it usually is: a
default would emit it as optional and hand every client a list it has to
check for existence before checking for length.

Opens.title: Opens
Opens.description: The screen a notice opens on when tapped (the screens A9).

distinct_opponents.title: Distinct Opponents
distinct_opponents.description:
How many **different people** those games were against.

**A doubles partner is one of them.** *A pair is anybody you were on a court with* is the rule this platform already counts familiarity by, and a figure counting opponents alone would say that somebody who partners the same person every week spreads their games as widely as somebody who does not.

times_on_court.title: Times On Court
times_on_court.description:
How many **times they were on a court with somebody** across their counted games — the denominator of the pair, and never a count of games.

**A doubles evening contributes three.** Games were the denominator first and are only divisible in singles: one doubles game put three people on the court, so the pair read `3 of 1` and the share went over a hundred. Counting the seats opposite makes both halves the same kind of thing — *five different people across ten times on a court* — and `distinct_opponents` can never exceed it.

**It is not `skill.counted_games`, and the two will differ on this same response.** That one is *what this Level rests on*: confirmed results, in one sport, that the rating actually folded. This one is *how much have they played*: every sport, and an evening nobody agreed a score for is in it. Two honest numbers about the same person, answering two questions — do not reconcile them.

**Counted rather than every game**: a friendly was never evidence about anybody by the choice of the people who arranged it, and it is out of both halves of this pair rather than only the bottom one.

OpponentVarietySchema.title: OpponentVarietySchema
OpponentVarietySchema.description:
How widely this person spreads their games, over their **whole** record.

**Two counts and no percentage, deliberately.** The card this sits on argues
two rows above that a perfect record over nine games and one over forty are
different claims and that a bar alone hides which — so publishing a bare
share here would break the rule the card had just made about itself. Draw
both: `70 % · 14 of 20`.

**The share is yours to compute and it is one division.** Nothing is rounded
on this side and there is no banding, no floor and no tone attached — unlike
a Level's band, which is a key precisely because a client deriving it would
be a second set of drawing constants.

**This is a career statistic, not a window.** It is every counted game the
platform has recorded for them, which is what the number means: *how widely
do they spread their games*, rather than *how widely this season*. There is
no decay behind it and no horizon.

**It prices no promise.** It is not a reliability strand, it is in no
weighted score, and it neither raises nor lowers anybody's standing. It is
context for a Level — a low figure is somebody playing the same few faces
every week, whose rating may be narrow but untested.

OptimisedFor.title: OptimisedFor
OptimisedFor.description:
Whom this search was run for.

``GROUP`` exists because a line-up with seats locked is no longer optimising
for the searcher, who may end up with a worse individual match than an empty
builder would have given them — and the screen has to say so. A shortlist is
always ``SEARCHER``, and the field is on the envelope rather than implied by
the surface so that one renderer reads one fact.

Outcome.title: Outcome
Outcome.description:
What a confirmed result says about one of the people who played.

Two values. *Unscored* is not a third: a game with no agreed result produces
**no outcome for anybody**, which is ADR-0049's *an evening, not evidence*
stated as a type — the absence has one spelling, and it is not being in the
answer.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: When this yes lapses. **Dated when it was created** and never extended by tapping again — a second tap changes nothing. On expiry the row is simply gone: there is no *expired* state and no archive.

OutgoingInterestSchema.title: OutgoingInterestSchema
OutgoingInterestSchema.description:
One yes you sent, and when it lapses.

``expires_at`` is on the row from the moment it was created, and the client
**renders** it rather than computing it: the TTL behind it is ruleset
configuration and never crosses as a number.

cap.title: Cap
cap.description: The most you may have in flight for this sport at once. **Read it from here, never hardcode it** — it is ruleset configuration and may move between releases.

ttl_days.title: Ttl Days
ttl_days.description: How many days a yes you send in this sport stays live before it lapses. **Read it from here, never hardcode it** — it is the same ruleset number that dates every `expires_at`, sent so a screen can say *your yeses stay live for N days* without holding N. Every yes still carries its own `expires_at`; render that for a row, and this for the sentence.

OutstandingSchema.title: OutstandingSchema
OutstandingSchema.description:
How many yeses you have in flight for one sport, and the cap in force.

**Outstanding means sent, unexpired and not yet mutual** — a mutual has been
answered and is no longer in flight. The pair travels together on every read,
because a cap you cannot see is a refusal you cannot predict.

shade.description: `BRIGHT` — everybody on the card is free together for a whole hour of it; `DIM` — all but one (never on a two-person card); `DARK` — fewer.

OverlapShade.title: OverlapShade
OverlapShade.description: How many of the card's people are free together in a cell.

PairingAbsence.title: PairingAbsence
PairingAbsence.description:
Why a court came back with no cards on it. **Two codes, and a third
answer that is their absence** (``docs/adr/0143`` §6).

Three answers rather than two, because an outage drawing the *identical*
absence as an unrated sport is the collapse ADR-0141's Consequences refused
in as many words. And refusing the whole read with a 503 is worse than
either: it turns an unrelated matchmaking outage into *you cannot answer your
challenge*, and answering is not gated.

**The codes are the contract and the client writes both sentences**
(``docs/adr/0106``).

method.description: The saved method, or `null` — *Not set up*.

terms_needed.title: Terms Needed
terms_needed.description: `true` when the bank moved the saved card to another brand: it cannot be charged until the player accepts the terms again (`POST …/terms` with no setup open). Always `false` with no method.

terms_version.title: Terms Version
terms_version.description: The version of the terms in force.

PaymentMethodResponse.title: PaymentMethodResponse
PaymentMethodResponse.description: The player's payment method, as You › Payments draws it.

PaymentRefusal.title: PaymentRefusal
PaymentRefusal.description:
Why a seat's share could not be held — the payment's own words, spelled
here in this context's (the mechanics §12.2, §19).

setup_id.title: Setup Id
setup_id.description: The setup the phone's provider fields confirm. **Its secret is not here**: it is the answer to accepting the terms, and nothing can be saved without it.

publishable_key.title: Publishable Key
publishable_key.description: The key the provider's fields are opened with. Not a secret: it collects details and can charge nothing.

terms_version.title: Terms Version
terms_version.description: The version of the payment terms in force — the words the client must show before *Accept and continue*, and send back.

PaymentSetupResponse.title: PaymentSetupResponse
PaymentSetupResponse.description: A setup opened: what the phone opens the provider's card fields with.

terms_version.title: Terms Version
terms_version.description: The version of the words the player was shown. Anything but the terms in force is `409 payment_terms_outdated`.

client_secret.title: Client Secret
client_secret.description: The secret the phone confirms the open setup with — its **only** appearance on any response. `null` when the terms were accepted again for the method already saved, after its bank moved it to another brand: there is nothing to confirm.

PaymentsToConfirmResponse.title: PaymentsToConfirmResponse
PaymentsToConfirmResponse.description:
*Confirm your payment to keep your seat*, every one the reader owes,
soonest game first.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Permanent id — what the profile commit carries

url.title: Url
url.description: Short-lived signed URL that reads this photo. Not a stable address: it is signed for one player, for one window, and there is no public bucket behind it.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: When the URL stops working. Ask for the photo again to get another; there is no way to extend one.

review.description:
What the on-court check concluded about this photo, or `null` where this response carries no verdict.

**`null` is not `allowed`, and it means two different things on the two routes.** On the upload it is *the reviewer could not be asked* — our outage, and never a statement about the photograph. On the read it is *this route does not carry one*, which it never does. A client that has not been told anything must warn about nothing, and both readings collapse to that.

**A warning and nothing else.** `flagged` does not refuse, delete or hold back a photo: it is stored, it keeps its id, and a profile commit takes it like any other. The check is wrong sometimes, and the cost of being wrong is a sentence rather than a signup.

A code, not copy — the words belong to the client.

PhotoResponse.title: PhotoResponse
PhotoResponse.description:
One photo: the id a profile commit will carry, and a URL that reads it.

The same shape from the upload and from the read, so a client renders a tile
it has just filled and a tile it is restoring with one code path.

**The URL is not an identifier and must not be stored as one.** It carries a
signature and stops working at ``expires_at``; the id is what is permanent.

## The verdict crosses; the evidence does not

``review`` is the on-court check's conclusion and it is a **code**, never a
sentence: the backend emits codes and the client owns the words
(``docs/adr/0022``). ``review-note`` — the model, the prompt-set fingerprint
and the raw similarity vector — stays on the object. It is evidence for us
rather than a fact about the player, and a confidence score on the wire is an
invitation to a client that renders one.

**The upload carries it and the read does not**, which is why the field is
optional and why ``null`` is not ``allowed``. Two reasons, and neither is
that the read is harder. A warning belongs to the moment a player *chose* a
photograph; a tile being restored is a photograph they already kept, and
saying it again is a screen re-litigating a decision the player made. And the
read would have to pay for it: ``GET /photos/{id}`` proves existence and signs
a URL, and no part of it looks at what the store holds beside the bytes — the
verdict is user metadata, which every S3-compatible store answers with a
request per object. So the shape stays one shape and the tile stays one code
path, exactly as the paragraph above promises; what differs is whether this
response has anything to say about the check. Where the owner reads what
**stands** beside each of their photographs is the profile read's ``photos``
list (`ProfilePhotoResource`, ``docs/adr/0179`` §8) — the one screen whose
question is the check's answer, paying that request for at most three
objects rather than per tile.

**The upload can also carry nothing, and that is not the read's ``null``**
(``docs/adr/0138``). A reviewer that could not be asked concludes nothing, so
an outage answers ``null`` here rather than ``allowed``: fail-open used to
spell *nothing to warn about* with the only word it had, and that word now
means *checked and passed* somewhere else — on a player card, to somebody who
is not this photograph's owner. Both absences reach a client as *say
nothing*, which is what makes the collapse safe on this route and the
distinction load-bearing on the other one.

PhotoReviewDecision.title: PhotoReviewDecision
PhotoReviewDecision.description:
What the review port concluded about an image.

Two values, and there is deliberately no ``REJECTED``. The on-court check
**soft-warns rather than hard-blocks** (``docs/adr/0091``): a false reject
stops a real player on their first day, and that cost does not fall now that
the other side of the trade has got heavier. Adding a blocking value later is
an addition; shipping one now would be a behaviour nothing has earned.

There is also no value for *the reviewer could not be asked*, and there is
now a third state rather than two. This enum says what the reviewer
**concluded** about an image; *nobody looked* is not a conclusion about an
image, so it is spelled as the **absence** of one of these — ``None`` on a
verdict, no key on the object, no field on the wire (``docs/adr/0138``).
ADR-0133 already spelled the uploader's third state that way rather than
folding it into ``allowed`` at the boundary that knows least; the stored
verdict is the boundary that was folded, and this is where it is unfolded.
See `verdict_when_unreviewable` and `decision_on_record`.

PhotosResponse.title: PhotosResponse
PhotosResponse.description:
The photographs as the profile now holds them, in their order.

Ids and nothing else: the verdict beside each is the profile read's to
serve (`ProfilePhotoResource`), paid for once there rather than on every
rearrangement here.

PlanListResponse.title: PlanListResponse
PlanListResponse.description:
One row for every court you may plan, written or not.

**No `read_at`, and that is deliberate.** A plan folds nothing against the
clock, so there is no instant for it to have been folded against — the card
is folded against `GET /games`' own `read_at`, which is what keeps Now on one
clock by construction (``docs/adr/0148`` §10).

**A court with nothing agreed is a row with three nulls** (``docs/adr/0164``
§4), not an absence: a row is what says there is a plan to draw and what
carries the anchor to draw it with, and absence is reserved for one thing —
a court you hold no accepted seat on.

challenge_id.title: Challenge Id
challenge_id.description: The challenge this plan is for. **A plan is one challenge's, for ever**, and the game it becomes inherits it — join it against `GET /conversations` by `challenge_id` and against `GET /games` by the game's own `challenge_id`.

place.title: Place
place.description: Where these people are meeting, as somebody typed it. **Short free text, one line** — never an id, a lookup, an autocomplete, a reuse or a geocode, and **nothing anywhere reads it**. It is a note between the people on the court and never a place the platform knows.

day.title: Day
day.description: The local day, in the platform's one zone (`Europe/Warsaw`). **A wall-clock fact, drawn literally and never counted down** — nothing expires at the end of it.

hour.title: Hour
hour.description: The local clock time. **The agreement itself, not a guess at a booking**: nothing on this platform will ever hold a court, so nothing can contradict it.

agreed_point.title: Agreed Point
agreed_point.description:
The moment this plan names, **derived and never stored**. The agreed instant when the day and the hour are both recorded; the **start of the following local day** when only the day is; `null` when no day is.

Coarsened **later, never earlier**, so nobody is asked for a result before they could have played. It is sent because it is a timezone conversion the client must not redo.

anchor.title: Anchor
anchor.description:
The instant this plan's horizon runs from: a day may be set up to **7 days past it**, and the row of day chips is clamped to that. **The challenge's send until the game exists, then the game's `planned_at`** — it only ever moves later, so a day chosen under the first is still valid under the second and the chips widen when the court fills rather than shrinking.

Sent rather than derived on the client because the client would otherwise need the game to draw a plan, and a court that is not whole has none.

locked_at.title: Locked At
locked_at.description:
The moment somebody agreed this plan, or `null` while nobody has.

**A locked plan is not a frozen one.** Any member may still move any slot afterwards, and each move writes its own system line — there is no un-agreeing to fear, only re-agreeing. The plan stays locked and the line trail is the friction, as it already is for every change.

**There is no unlock**, and this never returns to `null`. The lock is a thing that happened.

**It is not the slot count under another name**: a plan with all three slots filled is one everybody *could* agree, and this says somebody did.

PlanSchema.title: PlanSchema
PlanSchema.description:
One court's plan: three slots, the moment they name, and the anchor.

**Keyed on the challenge and on nothing else.** A plan has no id of its own —
``challenge_id`` identifies it, for ever, and a second identity beside that
would be a second name for one thing. The game the challenge becomes carries
the same id, which is how Now joins the two.

Each slot is nullable and an empty one is spelled ``null``. **A slot is never
emptied**, so a ``null`` here is a slot that has never been filled and never a
slot somebody cleared; the client draws the slot's name in its place. A row
with all three ``null`` is a court nobody has written on yet, and it is a row
because the court is one the reader may plan.

PlayIntent.title: PlayIntent
PlayIntent.description:
What kind of game a player wants, in one sport.

Declared per ``(player, sport)`` — see ``play_intent_declaration.py`` for
why that is its own aggregate rather than a field on the profile.

PlayIntentDeclarationResponse.title: PlayIntentDeclarationResponse
PlayIntentDeclarationResponse.description:
The standing declaration for one player in one sport.

The **surface is not served back**. It is recorded beside the fact for us,
and a response that carried it would invite a client to render *where you
last said this*, which is a fact about the app and not about the player.

PlayIntentSurface.title: PlayIntentSurface
PlayIntentSurface.description:
Which screen a declaration was made on.

``ConsentSurface``'s precedent in this same context, and it obeys the same
rule about what it is *for*: it is context recorded beside a fact, never a
thing any decision branches on.

**It is client-asserted and a client could lie about it** (ADR-0094). That
is accepted because the client is the only party that knows which screen it
was, and nothing load-bearing reads it — which is exactly the condition
under which a self-reported field is safe to keep.

**It widened rather than renaming, and the reason was cost** (#280). The
deck earned the fifth member: ``POST /deck`` has no mode to read, so it
reads the declaration, is refused with ``play_intent_not_declared`` exactly
as a search is, and draws the same interstitial. Reporting that as
``SEARCH_SWITCH`` was a small untruth in the one field whose whole job is to
say which screen it was. The alternative argued was to rename
``SEARCH_SWITCH`` to ``PLAY_SWITCH`` — one value true of both Play surfaces
rather than two that each name one — and it lost on cost, not on taste: the
code is stored verbatim in ``PlayIntentDeclared`` and read back through
``PlayIntentSurface(event.surface)``, so a rename is an event migration
bought on a field nothing branches on, while a widening is one member and
leaves every code already in a stream meaning what it meant when it was
written.

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole name, and **nothing may derive a familiar form from it** — every sentence naming somebody uses the whole name or names nobody (``docs/adr/0171``). Never the nickname: a handle is drawn on a record and their own You tab, and said nowhere.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: The first photo — order is meaning in a photo list. **The id is what is stored**: a presigned link cannot live in a record kept for ever, so the record keeps this one and the link beside it is minted per response. **Omitted** when the player has no photo, and the client draws the generated court poster.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description:
Short-lived signed URL that draws that photo. **Minted per response and stored nowhere**: it dies within minutes, and two reads of the same search carry two different links to the same photograph.

**You cannot sign one yourself.** `GET /photos/{photo_id}` signs only *your own* photos and refuses a stranger's id deliberately, and a card's photo is by definition somebody else's — so this is the only address this photograph has.

**Present exactly when `photo_id` is.** A link that has expired is not an error to report: draw the generated court poster, which is what a player with no photo gets in any case.

review.description:
What the on-court check concluded about `photo_id`, or **omitted** where this photograph has not been checked.

**Omitted is not `allowed`, and only `allowed` earns a shield.** Three answers, not two: checked and passed, checked and flagged, and *nobody looked* — a photo that arrived while the reviewer could not be reached, or before the check existed at all. A client that drew a tick on the absence would be claiming a check happened on every photograph on the platform.

**A fact about this photograph and not about the player.** It is present only beside `photo_id`, it is search-time like every other fact on this card, and `flagged` blocks nothing — the photo is stored, it is shown, and the check is wrong sometimes.

**The evidence never crosses.** No confidence, no similarity vector, no model, no prompt-set fingerprint: those are collected so the threshold can be re-derived, and they are not a number a player can do anything with. A code, not copy — the words belong to the client.

area_code.title: Area Code
area_code.description: Their coarse area, as a machine code

social_tags.title: Social Tags
social_tags.description: The Social tag ids they hold

intro.title: Intro
intro.description:
One line this player wrote about themselves — their **intro** — verbatim: at most 100 characters, no line breaks, in whatever language they wrote it. **Omitted where they wrote none**, and never an empty string: the intro is optional and a player who skipped has no line, so the card closes up rather than drawing a blank quotation.

**A fact about the person, assembled by `player_profile`** — the one field this closed list has gained, under its own admission rule: it is what its subject published, it does not change with who is looking, and it is projected to the candidate index like the tags. It is **never scored**: no term reads it and the scorer's fence refuses the word.

**Fenced at the write, not here.** A line carrying a phone number, an email, a URL or an `@handle` was refused before it was stored, so what arrives is a line about a player and not a way to reach one. What it says is theirs; a line you object to is what a block is for.

**Drawn on the deck card and the record sheet, and not on Find a game's cards** — those are about the game, and the line is about the person. Never spoken as the player's name and never truncated: the cap is what makes an ellipsis unnecessary.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level, as RacketSkill published it

range.description: The **likely range** their Level sits in, μ ± σ as RacketSkill published it. Always present: a card that stated a Level without it would show two players at the same Level with no way to tell that one of them is a guess. **The band's numeric edges are not here** — they are not a second range to compare this one against.

player_score.title: Player Score
player_score.description:
Their **Player Score** out of a hundred — reliability, as the platform watched it: whether games arranged for them were played, and whether challenges sent to them were answered inside their window.

**The published figure and never a re-derivation of it.** It is the same number this player's own profile prints, at the same player-facing weights, because a card explaining a match with a figure their own screen disagrees with is worse than a card that says nothing.

**Omitted where the platform has watched nothing**, which is most people today. Never `0`: somebody nothing was ever arranged for has not failed to turn up, and the absence is what lets *Most reliable* sort them last instead of first.

counted_games.title: Counted Games
counted_games.description:
How many **counted** games they have played. A friendly is not one — it was never evidence about anybody, by the choice of the people who arranged it — and a game nobody agreed a score for **is**: an unscored game is an evening rather than evidence, so it says these people were on a court and it moves nobody's Level.

**Omitted where they have played none**, and never `0`. Absence has one spelling on this card.

last_five.title: Last Five
last_five.description:
Their last five counted results, **oldest to newest** — the run of form a card draws left to right. Only games whose result was agreed are here; an unscored one moved nobody's Level and is in `counted_games` instead.

**Fewer than five is a real answer and it is never padded.** Three entries means three counted results, and the client draws the gap rather than filling it.

**There are no dates here, at any granularity.** This is a run of outcomes in order, and a moment beside one of them would be activity recency, which no card carries in any shape.

**Omitted where nothing of theirs has been counted and agreed.**

PlayerCardSchema.title: PlayerCardSchema
PlayerCardSchema.description:
Who this person is, on a card. **A closed list with one permanent gap.**

**No activity recency at any granularity** — not a timestamp, not *active
today*, not a green dot. Liveness reaches a screen the one way it is
sanctioned to: as a reason code. The other gap the list was closed with —
*no bio, and no free-text field of any kind* — was opened by exactly one
field, `intro`, on the terms that refusal set: its own decision with a
moderation story attached (``docs/adr/0170``). Still no bio, no paragraph,
no second field, and no free text that is scored.

**The last three fields are the record block, and every one of them is
omitted rather than nought.** They are what the platform has watched this
person do — a Player Score, a count of counted games and a run of form — and
a nought printed for somebody it has watched do nothing would be a claim
where there is a gap. ``last_five`` is the one that has to keep the recency
