rule while carrying five events: it is **outcomes in order and no dates**,
which is a run of form rather than a statement about when anybody was last
here.

PlayerProfileOptionsResponse.title: PlayerProfileOptionsResponse
PlayerProfileOptionsResponse.description:
Everything a client needs to *render* the profile steps, in one round trip.

A handful of facts rather than one endpoint each, because they are the same
kind of thing — closed, read-only, and needed by the same part of onboarding
at the same moment.

**Fields are only ever added.** A shipped mobile app parses this document for
months after it stops being built, so a new field goes on the end and the
ones already here keep their names and their types.

weekly_hours.title: Weekly Hours
weekly_hours.description: The hours of the week this player has ticked, in the platform's own reading order — day, then hour. **An empty list is a real answer** — a player may clear their week — and it means *we do not know when they play*, never *never*.

search_radius_km.title: Search Radius Km
search_radius_km.description: Whole kilometres. What the search screen's slider opens at.

play_intents.title: Play Intents
play_intents.description:
What this player declared, per sport. **Only sports they have declared in appear** — an undeclared sport is absent and is never a `null` value, because there is no unanswered Play intent (`NO_PREFERENCE` is an explicit answer).

*Rated but not yet declared* is a set difference the client computes against `GET /ratings`, which it is already fetching to build the sport chips. A search by a player with no declaration for that sport is refused with `play_intent_not_declared`, so this is what lets a client open the one-tap interstitial before the refusal rather than after it.

social_tags.title: Social Tags
social_tags.description: The Social tag ids this player holds, **in the vocabulary's order** whatever order the picker sent them in. Required at commit, so never empty and never absent.

photos.title: Photos
photos.description: The photographs, **in the player's order** — the first is the profile photo — each with the verdict its uploader is owed. **An empty list is a real answer**: a profile may hold none, and the client draws the generated court poster.

intro.title: Intro
intro.description: The line this player wrote about themselves, as recorded, or **omitted** where none was written. Never an empty string (`docs/adr/0170`).

proposals_opt_in.description: The standing answer to the proposals question: what was answered, when, against which words and from which surface. Always present — a profile cannot be committed without one.

gender.description:
The owner's own answer to the gender question. **Served here and on no other response shape** (`docs/adr/0179` §4) — what one player is told about another never carries it.

**Omitted** on a profile committed before the question existed, and never read as `PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY`, which is an answer a player gives: a client pre-selects nothing rather than something.

gender_preference.description: Who the owner is willing to be matched with — their own setting, served here and on no other response shape (`docs/adr/0179` §4). Always present: it defaults to `ANY` at commit, so there is nothing for its absence to mean.

PlayerProfileReadResponse.title: PlayerProfileReadResponse
PlayerProfileReadResponse.description:
Every fact a player declared, in one round trip — what the Play screens
read and, since ``docs/adr/0179``, what the You tab draws its rows from.

**The gender and the preference are served here, and on no other shape.**
ADR-0096 §6's *no response shape carries a gender value out* is about
responses that describe one player to another, and its walk still refuses
both words on every one of those. A player reading their own answer on a
route scoped to ``me`` is not what that rule protects, and a screen that
asks *who should we match you with* with nothing pre-selected is a screen a
player cannot trust (``docs/adr/0179`` §4). ``gender`` is **omitted** on a
profile committed before the question existed — never ``PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY``,
which is an answer a player gives.

**The one thing still withheld is the location area**, and nothing stands
in for it: a profile cannot be committed without an area, so a
``has_location`` could never be false, and a branch nobody can take is a
branch nobody tests.

Absence has one spelling here and it is **omission** (``OMITTED``): an intro
never written, a photograph nobody looked at, a gender never asked. The one
absence that is served rather than omitted is **an empty ``photos`` list**,
because a profile may legally hold none and that is a real answer.

**No ``player_id``.** The resource is ``/players/me``, so the caller is the
bearer token and echoing it back would say nothing. ``GET /users/me`` is
where an id comes from.

**Fields are only ever added.** A shipped mobile app parses this document for
months after it stops being built. ``weekly_hours`` is the one replacement,
of the part-of-day ``availability`` it succeeded (``docs/adr/0189`` §5), made
while no build had shipped anywhere but ``local``.

PlayerProfileResponse.title: PlayerProfileResponse
PlayerProfileResponse.description:
A player's profile as it now stands.

The same body whether the commit created the profile or replayed an earlier
one, so a client that only wants its profile needs no branch on the status.

**No gender value comes back out of this body**, and that is a rule rather
than an oversight (``docs/adr/0096`` §6): a preference crosses the wire
*in*, on a search; no response that describes one player to another carries
a gender out and no card renders one. This body is only ever the caller's
own profile, so nothing here would leak a third party's answer — the field
is left off anyway, because *which* shapes may carry it is a line rather
than a judgement made per endpoint, and the line is **exactly one shape**:
the owner's own read, ``PlayerProfileReadResponse`` (``docs/adr/0179`` §4).
The profile editor that reads it back is the You tab, and it reads that
route; the commit's answer stays what it was.

**Fields are only ever added.** A shipped mobile app parses this document for
months after it stops being built. ``weekly_hours`` is the one replacement,
of the part-of-day ``availability`` it succeeded (``docs/adr/0189`` §5), made
while no build had shipped anywhere but ``local``.

is_self.title: Is Self
is_self.description:
Whether this is the reader's own record. **The server's answer, and the client never derives it** by comparing the id it asked about against its session — the sheet retitles to *How others see you* and drops the distance and the fit pill, and getting that wrong is most visible on the one screen it matters on. It decides the title and nothing on the sheet: every zone, what other players said included, is the same fact whoever is reading.

`true` on `/players/me/record` always, and on the parameterised route when a client asks about itself.

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole name, and **nothing may derive a familiar form from it** — every sentence naming somebody uses the whole name or names nobody (``docs/adr/0171``). The title of the sheet.

nickname.title: Nickname
nickname.description: Their handle, drawn as `@nickname` under the name. **The record and the You tab are the only two places it is drawn** — never on a row, a card, a sentence, a sheet, a toast, a seat label or a spoken name — because two people may share a name and this is the screen a friend tells them apart on.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: The first photo — order is meaning in a photo list. **Omitted** when the player has no photograph, and the client draws the generated court poster rather than a placeholder.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description:
Short-lived signed URL that draws that photo. **Minted per response and stored nowhere** — this context stores nothing at all — so two reads of one record carry two links to one photograph.

**You cannot sign one yourself.** `GET /photos/{photo_id}` signs only *your own* photos and refuses a stranger's id deliberately, so this is the only address this photograph has.

**Present exactly when `photo_id` is.**

review.description:
What the on-court check concluded about `photo_id`, or **omitted** where this photograph has not been checked.

**Omitted is not `allowed`, and only `allowed` earns a shield.** Three answers, not two: checked and passed, checked and flagged, and *nobody looked* — a photo that arrived while the reviewer could not be reached, or before the check existed at all. A client that drew a tick on the absence would be claiming a check happened on every photograph on the platform.

**A fact about this photograph and not about the player**, present only beside `photo_id`. `flagged` blocks nothing — the photo is stored, it is shown, and the check is wrong sometimes. The evidence behind the verdict never crosses on any route.

area_code.title: Area Code
area_code.description: Their coarse area, as a machine code. **An identifier and never a name** — nothing here can turn a coordinate into the name of a neighbourhood. What it licenses is the one comparison a client makes for itself: two players in the same square share a code, which is what *in your area* is drawn from.

social_tags.title: Social Tags
social_tags.description: The Social tag ids they hold, in the vocabulary's own order. **Which of them the reader also holds is the client's own comparison** — the platform states no overlap here, so a record opened without a search behind it draws them untinted and claims nothing about common ground.

intro.title: Intro
intro.description:
One line this player wrote about themselves — their **intro** — verbatim, drawn under the name. **Omitted where they wrote none**, and never an empty string: the intro is optional, and a player who skipped has no line rather than an empty one.

The same field the player card carries (`player_card.intro`), read off the profile as it stands rather than off a search record; today the two cannot differ, since the line is written once at onboarding and not editable yet. Fenced at the write against a phone number, an email, a URL or an `@handle`, so what arrives is a line about a player and never a way to reach one. Present on your own record as on anybody else's — it is what strangers read, shown back to you.

sports.title: Sports
sports.description:
One pill per sport they hold a rating in, **in the sport registry's own order** — the same order every list of sports on this surface takes, so a client never sorts one.

**Empty for somebody rated in nothing**, which is an ordinary state part way through onboarding rather than an error. It is empty exactly when `skill` is absent.

skill.description:
The skill card, for the one sport this sheet is about.

**Which sport is resolved here and stated back on the panel.** The `?sport=` you asked with wins where they are rated in it; otherwise it falls back to the sport they have played most, ties broken by the sport registry's own order. A fallback on their *highest* Level would make the header a boast about a sport nobody asked about.

**Omitted where no sport resolves** — that is, where they are rated in nothing at all. The header draws the poster with no Level on it, and there is no panel of noughts to mistake for a bad record.

reliability.description:
**What the platform watched them do** — the reliability pill and the metered rows it is the mean of.

**Omitted where nothing has ever fallen due for them**, which is most people today, and never a section of noughts: nobody has failed to turn up who was never due to. When it is omitted there is no `player_score` to draw a red pill from and no empty `strands` to head a card with.

**A third absence, asking a third question.** Not `skill`'s — somebody rated in four sports may have had nothing fall due at all. Not `variety`'s either, and they do not move together: a plan that dissolved and a seat that ran out are opportunities here and neither is a game anybody played.

It is about **no sport**, like `variety`: `?sport=` does not move it. Turning up is a habit, not a padel habit.

variety.description:
How widely they spread their games — **the raw pair, over their whole record.**

**Omitted where no counted game has ever been recorded for them**, which is not a nought and not `0 / 0`: a habit nobody has been observed having is not a narrow one. It is a **different absence from `skill`'s** — somebody rated in nothing may have played all week, and somebody rated in four sports may never have had a game counted.

**It is about every sport**, unlike `skill.last_five` above it. `?sport=` does not move it: a person who plays padel with the same four faces and squash with twenty has one habit, and a figure narrowed to one sport would be a different statistic under the same word.

sportsmanship.description:
**What other players said** — the average out of five and how many different people it rests on.

**Its own zone, deliberately apart from `reliability`.** That card promises *counted by the system, not written by people*, and this is the one thing here people wrote. Two headings, no lie.

**Omitted where nobody has rated them**, which is most people and is never a nought: rating is a favour, ignoring the card costs nothing, and nothing anywhere records that somebody did not answer. It is a **fourth absence** and asks a fourth question — not `skill`'s, not `variety`'s and not `reliability`'s, since a plan that dissolved and a seat that ran out are opportunities and neither is an opinion anybody offered.

**On your own record too, and it is the same figure.** What you read about yourself under *Sportsmanship, by players* is what a stranger reads about you — `4,3 / 5 · 12 players` — with nothing coarsened and no count withheld. The three-step band that used to stand in for it on your own sheet is gone from this shape; ADR-0179 §5 decides that and names what it costs.

**It is about no sport**, like `variety` and `reliability`: `?sport=` does not move it. How somebody is to play with is not a padel fact.

**The matcher never reads it.** A low figure hides nobody and demotes nobody — Pass and Block are the controls that act, and both are deliberate.

PlayerRecordResponse.title: PlayerRecordResponse
PlayerRecordResponse.description:
Everything the platform will say about one person, to this reader.

**Read through a prior disclosure and never about a person at large.** A
record opens for somebody a search of yours returned, somebody you share an
open challenge, a game or a group with, and yourself. Anybody else — and
anybody a live gate no longer admits — is `404`, in one shape that names
nothing.

matched.title: Matched
matched.description: Tag ids they both hold, in this column

PlayingStyleEvidence.title: PlayingStyleEvidence
PlayingStyleEvidence.description:
What the two of them are like during the hour on court.

The split from social vibe is **by relationship, not by tag group**: every
matrix row carries its own column, so a tag can be read for the hour on court
in one row and for the evening around it in another.

A pair with nothing firing is *different, not incompatible* — the term's zero
is a real clash, never an absence of relationship.

radius_km_used.title: Radius Km Used
radius_km_used.description: The searcher's own radius, in whole kilometres

players_in_range.title: Players In Range
players_in_range.description: How many candidates cleared every gate. **Post-gate, always** — a pre-gate count beside this one would be the delta a mutual preference hid, per searcher.

window.description: When a game found on this grid would plausibly be played, as a code. Derived by the backend from the grid the search ran on; there is no window picker anywhere.

post_gate.title: Post Gate
post_gate.description: Always true. It travels so the count cannot be misread.

remaining.title: Remaining
remaining.description: **On a deal only.** How many people are eligible for your deck beyond this hand — after every deck exclusion, and not in the cards you were just dealt. It is what lets a counter say *N left* and be true of the whole pool rather than of ten; it drops by a hand as hands are dealt. Omitted on every other surface and on a read-back, where a count about a pool that has moved on would be a number about nothing.

want_to_play_you.title: Want To Play You
want_to_play_you.description: **On a deal, and on a reading.** How many people have a live *Let's play* towards you in this sport that **the deck would deal** to you: every one of the deck's gates passed, not passed on by you within the pass window, not cooling off after a court you shared, and not already mutual. Somebody dealt this morning and unanswered still counts — the dealt memory is not applied. **On a reading it is the deck's number, computed by the deck's rule**, so the chip on either pane of Players is one number — and somebody the radar draws whom the deck would never deal is not in it, though their card says they said yes. **A count and never a list**: nothing on any route names who. On a deal `0` is a measured nought; on a reading it is omitted at zero, so a chip is drawn at one and above either way.

PoolSchema.title: PoolSchema
PoolSchema.description:
What the searcher is told about the pool this answer came from.

Sent on **every** search and not only on empty ones: a thin pool and a broken
floor are indistinguishable without it.

level_low.title: Level Low
level_low.description: The narrowed lower bound; `null` is the engine's own.

level_high.title: Level High
level_high.description: The narrowed upper bound; `null` is the engine's own.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start, as listed.

PostRequest.title: PostRequest
PostRequest.description:
*Post — you're In*: the four controls and the court hour picked on a
sheet. **Types only**: who it may be for and which court hours are offered
are the domain's to refuse, each with its own code.

share_grosze.title: Share Grosze
share_grosze.description: What a seat costs if it fills.

challenger.description: Who posted it — `null` once they withdrew.

people_in.title: People In
people_in.description: Everybody In, in the order they said yes. No court number.

PostStillFillingSchema.title: PostStillFillingSchema
PostStillFillingSchema.description:
Somebody else's post still filling that the poster could join — **I'm
in** is `POST /proposals/{proposal_id}/yes`, free until it fills.

versions.title: Versions
versions.description: How many versions it was dealt in, up to 3.

dealt_to.title: Dealt To
dealt_to.description: How many best fits were dealt it.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: The seats open beside the poster.

PostedResponse.title: PostedResponse
PostedResponse.description: The post, In with its poster — its id is the game's, in *You're In*.

fits_free.title: Fits Free
fits_free.description: How many of the poster's best fits are free **together with them** at `best_starts_at` — the best hour in the range that has a free court, or with none, the best hour of the range — never people who overlap the poster at different hours. The client caps it at *5+*.

best_starts_at.title: Best Starts At
best_starts_at.description: The hour the number is read at; `null` with no hour ahead.

court_free.title: Court Free
court_free.description: A court the post could be made at is free in the range — the cell can be picked when somebody fits too.

full_game.title: Full Game
full_game.description: A full game's worth are free: `fits_free` reaches `open_seats`. Pickable with a court but not full is *only 2 fit · may not fill*.

outside_your_hours.title: Outside Your Hours
outside_your_hours.description: The poster's own week covers no hour the number could be read at: dimmed and dashed, still pickable.

happening.title: Happening
happening.description: The red dot: a rescue the poster is offered, or somebody else's post still filling they could join, starts in the range.

PostingCellSchema.title: PostingCellSchema
PostingCellSchema.description:
One day's range on the posting grid. **The client draws the nine looks
from these values** (the screens A5.2): *dead* is `fits_free` nought; *few*
or *enough* by `full_game`; a court glyph by `court_free`; *outside your
hours*, *past* and the red dot by their own flags. *Your pick* is the
client's.

day.title: Day
day.description: The day on the club's clock.

week.title: Week
week.description: `1` starts today; `2` is the seven days after.

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The instant every cell was read against.

level_range.description: The range the others' Levels were counted in.

engine_level_range.description: The engine's own window for the kind around the poster's Level — the steppers' starting bounds, which may be narrowed in 0,05 steps and never widened.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: The seats besides the poster: three in doubles, one in singles.

PostingGridResponse.title: PostingGridResponse
PostingGridResponse.description: **WHEN** — one week of the posting grid (the mechanics §9.1 step 5).

fits.title: Fits
fits.description: The best fits free at the cell's best hour, best fit first.

free_courts.title: Free Courts
free_courts.description: **Home club first**, then by hour. Tapping one picks it.

rescues.title: Rescues
rescues.description: **Already happening here**, first: booked games in the range with a seat offered to the poster — *I'm in · `share_grosze`* pays at once (`POST /bookings/{id}/seats`).

posts.title: Posts
posts.description: Then: posts still filling in the range the poster could join.

PostingSlotResponse.title: PostingSlotResponse
PostingSlotResponse.description: A cell's sheet (the mechanics §9.1 step 6; the screens A5.3).

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: The platform's confidence transform over the combined σ, as a whole percent. Never 100: the platform cannot tell a player it is certain.

PredictedBalanceEvidence.title: PredictedBalanceEvidence
PredictedBalanceEvidence.description:
How even the game is forecast to be, and how sure of that the platform is.

``pct`` is the forecast the player is shown; ``confidence`` is the platform's
existing σ transform and never a second spelling of certainty.

photo_id.title: Photo Id
photo_id.description: Permanent id — what a photos write carries

review.description:
What the on-court check concluded about this photograph, or **omitted** where nobody looked.

**Omitted is not `allowed`.** Three answers, not two: checked and passed, checked and flagged, and *nobody looked* — a photo that arrived while the reviewer could not be reached, or before the check existed. This is the owner's own reading of the verdict the upload showed them once; `GET /photos/{id}` deliberately carries none. `flagged` blocks nothing — the photo is stored and shown, and the check is wrong sometimes. The evidence behind the verdict never crosses on any route.

ProfilePhotoResource.title: ProfilePhotoResource
ProfilePhotoResource.description:
One of the owner's photographs, and what the on-court check said about it.

**The same words as ``PhotoResponse``** — ``photo_id`` and ``review``, the
same code under the same name — so a client keys a tile from this list and
from ``GET /photos/{id}`` by one id and reads one vocabulary, even though the
two shapes spell *no verdict* differently (there ``null``, here omitted).
What differs is which route carries the verdict: the upload says it at
the moment the photograph was chosen (``docs/adr/0133``), the per-photo read
says nothing, and this list says what **stands** — because the You tab's
photos row is the one screen whose question is *what did the check conclude
about mine*, and a warning a player was shown once at upload has to be
findable again on the screen that lets them change the answer.

Three answers and only two values (``docs/adr/0138``): ``allowed``,
``flagged``, and **omitted** for *nobody looked*. Omitted is not
``allowed`` — a photograph that arrived while the reviewer was unreachable,
or before the check existed, has had nothing concluded about it, and a
client that drew a tick on the absence would be claiming a check happened.
``flagged`` blocks nothing: the photo is stored, it is shown, and the check
is wrong sometimes.

Prompt.title: Prompt
Prompt.description:
What the app is offering to ask. **Codes, never sentences.**

The kernel's rule reaches the matcher unchanged (``docs/adr/0022``): the
backend emits a code and the client writes the words. *"Keep 15 km?"* is one
phrasing of ``KEEP_THIS_RADIUS`` in one language, and a backend that shipped
it would own the copy for every client that ever exists.

slots.title: Slots
slots.description: The week this search actually ran on, in the same two named fields every other week on the wire crosses in — because the sheet **draws** this one on the seven-by-sixteen grid beside the profile's own and quotes its count off the same list. **An empty list is a cleared week** — the player unticked every hour, which is a legal edit and a legal thing to be offered — where the field being absent means this is not the times prompt at all.

mode.description: The mode your recent searches keep choosing

PromptSchema.title: PromptSchema
PromptSchema.description:
A question the app is offering to ask. **It never changes a value.**

The platform notices that you improvised a week, that you keep widening to
the same radius, that your searches disagree with what you declared, or that
the week on your profile is months old — and in every case it asks. The
payload is the value already in play, so the sheet can show the change rather
than describe it.

challenger.description: The poster of a challenge; `null` on a pick, and once its poster withdrew.

status.description: `FILLING` — seats are open: *Filling · `in_count` of `seats` in*. `WAITING_FOR_THE_CLUB` — every seat is In and an On request club has still to say yes; nobody pays until it does, and the book-by no longer ends it. `FILLED` — booked: `GET /bookings/{proposal_id}`. `EXPIRED`, `WITHDRAWN`, `COURT_HOUR_LOST` — it ended unfilled. `TURNED_DOWN` — its On request club refused it or did not answer: nobody paid, and the people In are dealt a new card first.

actions.title: Actions
actions.description: What the reader may do now, in the screen's order: `YES` and `NO` (*I'm in* / *Not this time*), `WITHDRAW` when they are In, `LEAVE` in its place while the club decides — *Leave the game* with its sheet, sent as the withdrawal, `DELETE /proposals/{id}/yes`, which also calls off the request to the club — and `CONFIRM_PAYMENT` when their seat waits on a refused payment (`your_payment`). Empty once the game is over or their answer is final.

your_payment.description: The payment to confirm to take the seat back — present exactly when `actions` holds `CONFIRM_PAYMENT`.

in_count.title: In Count
in_count.description: People In on the whole game.

seats.title: Seats
seats.description: Four in padel and badminton, two otherwise.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start; games are 1 h.

where.description: The club and its distance — never a court, given at booking.

book_by.title: Book By
book_by.description: When the game leaves unfilled — *book by Sat 13:00*.

no_free_cancellation.title: No Free Cancellation
no_free_cancellation.description: The club's cut-off has already passed for this game.

club_confirms.title: Club Confirms
club_confirms.description: An On request club: a full game waits for its yes.

sides.description: Everybody drawn, the reader on their own side: for a reader still deciding, their own card as the deck deals it; for a reader In, everybody In — the client draws the open seats empty.

forecast.description: How even the game drawn is forecast — `null` where it cannot be read.

ProposalDetailsResponse.title: ProposalDetailsResponse
ProposalDetailsResponse.description:
A game still filling, as the reader opens it — the deck's card turned
into a screen.

ProposalStatus.title: ProposalStatus
ProposalStatus.description: Where a proposal stands for its details (the mechanics §14.2).

accepted.title: Accepted
accepted.description: The player's answer. `null` means the question was not answered, which is refused — it is never read as `false`.

copy_version.title: Copy Version
copy_version.description: Identifier of the exact copy the player was shown. Not the copy itself — the words are the client's and are never stored here.

ProposalsOptInRequest.title: ProposalsOptInRequest
ProposalsOptInRequest.description:
The answer to the proposals question, and the words it was given against.

``accepted`` is **nullable and required**, which is the shape of a question
that has no default. Null means *not answered* and is refused by the commit
with ``proposals_opt_in_not_answered``; it is not a quiet ``false``, because
a recorded refusal and an unanswered question are different facts and only
one of them is consent (``../../../../CONTEXT.md`` — *Skipping is not
consent*).

``copy_version`` identifies the exact wording the player was shown. It is
required because consent gathered against one sentence is not consent to a
different one, and a consent record that cannot name its words cannot
evidence anything.

copy_version.title: Copy Version
copy_version.description: The copy this answer was given against

ProposalsOptInResponse.title: ProposalsOptInResponse
ProposalsOptInResponse.description:
The standing answer, and the evidence recorded with it.

This is the *current* answer. The **history** — every answer this player ever
gave, against which words and on which surface — is the stream, and nothing
serves it yet because nothing has asked for it.

token.title: Token
token.description: The phone's Expo push token — `ExponentPushToken[…]` or `ExpoPushToken[…]` — as the notifications library hands it out.

QuestionResponse.title: QuestionResponse
QuestionResponse.description: A question in reading order: category, situation, question, answers.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level in that sport, as published

RatedSportSchema.title: RatedSportSchema
RatedSportSchema.description:
One sport somebody is rated in, and the Level they hold there — a card's
sport chip (``docs/adr/0174`` §2). The Level and nothing else: the record
is where a band, a range and a certainty are drawn.

RatingResponse.title: RatingResponse
RatingResponse.description:
One sport's Skill rating.

``mu`` and ``sigma`` are the Level and the Uncertainty — the same spelling
``ResultResponse`` already puts on the wire for the same two numbers, so a
client never has to learn that the rating it was just shown and the rating it
later reads back are described in two vocabularies.

RatingsResponse.title: RatingsResponse
RatingsResponse.description: Every sport this player is rated at — empty when they are rated at none.

ReadAs.title: ReadAs
ReadAs.description:
What the text was read as — so an empty answer can say which empty it is:
*no match for "…"* for text, *nothing at that link* for a link (#500
stories 37 and 38).

sport.description: Which sport this reading is for

ReadRadarRequest.title: ReadRadarRequest
ReadRadarRequest.description:
What a reading is asked for. **The sport, and that is the whole
contract** (``the-radar.md`` §2).

**There is no `mode`**, because there is none: the radar scores every
pairing under the deck's ruler, and a mode on this body would be the field
the telemetry constraint refuses. **There is no radius**, because the reach
is your own Search radius and there is no city; the slider on Find a game
is where it moves. **There is no position**, because the server holds your
area and puts it on a cold start. And **there is no week**: a reading ranks
nobody, so there is nothing for a grid to rank on.

ReaderAction.title: ReaderAction
ReaderAction.description: What the reader may do from the details.

seat_charge_id.title: Seat Charge Id
seat_charge_id.description: The payment. A share refunded has two rows under one id — the charge and the refund — told apart by `kind`.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `CHARGE` — a share paid (✓). `REFUND` — a share given back (↩): less the card fee to a player who left before the cut-off, whole on a game called off at its cut-off.

amount_grosze.title: Amount Grosze
amount_grosze.description: What was paid, or what came back, in grosze — always positive.

card_fee_grosze.title: Card Fee Grosze
card_fee_grosze.description: On a `REFUND`, the card fee the provider kept back — nought on a refund in full. `null` on a `CHARGE`.

paid_at.title: Paid At
paid_at.description: When the money moved: taken, or — on a `REFUND` — given back.

ReceiptSchema.title: ReceiptSchema
ReceiptSchema.description:
One share the reader paid, or got back — *the club named as the
seller*.

RecordLikelyRangeSchema.title: RecordLikelyRangeSchema
RecordLikelyRangeSchema.description:
The **likely range** a Level sits in — μ ± σ, clamped to the scale.

**Named for its surface, because the contract is one namespace and this
arrived second.** ``matchmaking`` already publishes a ``LikelyRangeSchema``
on the player card; a second class of that name does not shadow it, it
*renames* it — the emitted document qualifies both by module and every
generated type a shipped app already holds moves. It is ``games``' rule for
``GameStanding``, applied to the wire: the cost of a shared word is paid by
whoever arrives second.

The shape is deliberately identical to the card's. Two edges of one value,
both rounded by the engine, and a client computes neither.

sport.description: Which sport this card was for

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Whose card you are passing on

search_id.title: Search Id
search_id.description: The deal this person was dealt to you in. **Required** — a pass with no origin is refused rather than recorded with a null link.

RecordPassRequest.title: RecordPassRequest
RecordPassRequest.description:
One *not today*, and where the card came from. **Write-only.**

Nothing is returned by this route and no route anywhere returns a pass — not
to you, not as a count, not as *"you have passed on twelve people"*.

`search_id` is the **Origin key** and is required, exactly as it is for a
yes: a pass citing a search that is unknown, that belongs to somebody else or
that never showed that person is refused rather than recorded with an empty
link. **The position is not sent** — the backend reads it off the cited
search's own rows.

**How long it lasts is not yours to name**, and there is no field here for
it. A pass keeps somebody out of *your deck* only, for a window this backend
decides; it never reaches a shortlist, a line-up or a forecast, it never
touches their deck, and a second pass buys exactly the same window and no
more. The control that removes a person from a person is a **block**, and it
is deliberately a heavier gesture.

prompt.description:
Which question you are answering, as the code the search sent you.

**`KEEP_THESE_TIMES` is refused** — an improvised week is a different week next Tuesday, so that one is asked again and the app does not offer *not now* for it.

sport.description: Which sport's screen raised it. **It is not the key**: a play intent is declared per sport, so declining that one is per sport, while a search radius and an availability grid are one fact each for the whole player — those go quiet everywhere.

RecordPromptDeclineRequest.title: RecordPromptDeclineRequest
RecordPromptDeclineRequest.description:
One *not now*, about a question. **Write-only.**

Nothing is returned by this route and no route anywhere returns a decline —
not to you, not as a count, not as *"you have said no to this four times"*.

**There is no `search_id` and no idempotency key.** A pass carries an origin
because *pass rate on re-shown profiles* is unmeasurable without one; nothing
a decline is measured by needs one, and two of these questions are raised by
a background loop that has no search to cite. A second *not now* is a second
row with its own moment, exactly as a second pass is, and it buys the same
month the first did.

**How long it lasts is not yours to name**, and there is no field here for
it. What it buys is that this question is not raised at you again for a
while; it retires nothing — the standing prompt still expires on its own —
and it changes no value on your profile. Saying *yes* is a write through the
route that owns the value, and it is a different request entirely.

average.title: Average
average.description:
The mean of what other players said, **out of five, to one decimal.** Served rather than derived: there is one mean and one rounding of this record on the platform, and it rounds halves up.

**One to five, and never nought.** There is no zero on the scale a player taps — a rating that reads as *worthless* is a weapon out of proportion to a tap — so a person nobody has rated is **absent** here rather than sitting at the bottom of it.

raters.title: Raters
raters.description:
How many **different people** the figure rests on. Always drawn beside it.

**People and not ratings.** Only a rater's most recent stars about somebody count, so ten evenings with the same partner contribute one. A high count is therefore evidence of breadth rather than of repetition, and it cannot be inflated by volume.

**At most fifty**, which is the window: the fifty most recent raters, each contributing the one answer that stands.

RecordSportsmanshipSchema.title: RecordSportsmanshipSchema
RecordSportsmanshipSchema.description:
What other players said — **the one thing here nobody counted.**

**Named for its surface, because the contract is one namespace.** The word
belongs to ``sportsmanship``, which has a surface of its own; a class simply
called ``SportsmanshipSchema`` here would not shadow whatever that context
publishes next, it would *rename both* — and every generated type a shipped
app already holds would move. It is ``RecordLikelyRangeSchema``'s rule.

**Its own heading, and never mixed with the rows above.** The record card is
headed *counted by the system, not written by people*, which is the promise
every metered row under it rests on; a number people typed sitting beneath
that title would make the title false. Draw this under *What opponents said*
and the two apart.

**Both numbers, always, from the very first rating.** There is no minimum
because the count does a minimum's work honestly: `4,7 / 5 · 17 players` and
`3,0 / 5 · 1 player` are the same field, and the second one visibly reads as
one person's opinion. Print them together — a figure drawn without its count
is this field's one way of lying.

**`raters` is people, not ratings.** Only somebody's most recent stars about
a person ever count, so a weekly partner is **one** rater however many
evenings they play. That is what makes a high count evidence of *breadth*.

**It is the fifty most recent raters and nothing is trimmed.** Somebody can
recover from a bad patch by playing with fifty other people; nobody's rating
is discarded for being an outlier, because deciding which raters were wrong
is a larger claim than publishing the number.

**The matcher does not read it, and you should say so if you draw it beside
the pill.** A low figure here does not hide anybody, demote anybody or narrow
anybody's search results — the reliability pill is the counted-only number
and is exactly what the platform acts on.

**On your own record too, at this resolution.** The person it is about
reads the same figure and the same count a stranger does; the coarse band
that used to stand in for it on their own sheet is gone from the shape. See
the field on the response for why.

Relationship.title: Relationship
Relationship.description:
What one seat is to the searcher. **Stated, never inferred from a side.**

``the-two-contracts.md`` §5: the whole partner/opponent asymmetry hangs on
it, and a client deriving it from which side somebody sits on would be a
second implementation of a domain rule.

RelaxationAsk.title: RelaxationAsk
RelaxationAsk.description:
Which of the searcher's own asks a rung relaxes.

The vocabulary is closed at two because there are exactly two asks a searcher
makes: when they can play, and how far they will go. A third value would be
the engine relaxing something the player never asked for, which is the line
``docs/adr/0099`` draws.

strands.title: Strands
strands.description: The strands that produced a reading, over the closed six

floor_breached.title: Floor Breached
floor_breached.description: Whether the published score sits under the reliability bar

ReliabilityEvidence.title: ReliabilityEvidence
ReliabilityEvidence.description:
What the candidate's record says about turning up and following through.

``score`` is the **published Player Score** — the number on the player's own
profile — and never the matcher's private per-mode blend of the same six
strands. A penalty justified by a figure that exists nowhere a human can look
is unexplainable, and a player who works their visible score back up must be
able to see the penalty lift.

player_score.title: Player Score
player_score.description:
Their **Player Score** out of a hundred — the same figure the player card prints and the reliability floor prices, at the same player-facing weights.

**It is the weighted mean of the `pct`s beneath it**, taken over the strands that are actually there: a name with nothing behind it costs nothing rather than dragging the number down. Read it rather than blending the rows yourself.

strands.title: Strands
strands.description:
The rows behind the figure, **in the strand vocabulary's own order** — never sort them.

**Only the strands this person has.** A strand nobody on this platform can measure and a strand nothing has fallen due under for *them* are the same absence here, and neither is a `0`: *we have not seen enough* and *they are bad at this* are different facts. There is always at least one row, because a panel with none is omitted whole.

ReliabilitySchema.title: ReliabilitySchema
ReliabilitySchema.description:
What the platform watched — the pill, and the rows it is the mean of.

**Counted by the system, not written by people.** Every row under this
heading is a ratio the platform observed. What opponents said about somebody
is not here and will not be: an opinion under this title would make the title
false.

**The pill is exactly the number the matcher acts on**, at the player's own
published weights. That is what makes the screen worth having — somebody who
works their record back up can watch the penalty lift — and it is why the
weights themselves are **not** on this response: they are a fact about how
the number is made, not about the person, and a client that had them could
print one strand as worth more than another, which no screen here claims.

ReliabilityStrand.title: ReliabilityStrand
ReliabilityStrand.description:
The six strands a reliability reading is built from, read separately.

They are weighted **per mode** and the two vectors order people oppositely —
a candidate strong on *answers about results* and weak on *sportsmanship*
wins in competitive and loses in for fun. A single blended score cannot
express that, which is the whole argument for the decomposition, and it is
justified for exactly as long as such a pair exists (``ranking-weights.md``
§6).

**The inversion is watched rather than assumed, and it widened again.** It
was 24/4 against sportsmanship's 5/16 while *confirms results* was here; the
strike left 18/7 against 15/17, and *answers about results* restores the wide
pair at 24/4 against 5/16 (``docs/adr/0160``). It is asserted in
``tests/unit/test_matchfit_terms.py``, and the day no pair inverts, the
decomposition has stopped paying for itself and the argument for it is due
again.

**The sixth name is not the one that was struck, and the difference is the
whole of ``docs/adr/0160``.** *Confirms results* asked whether a game reached
an agreed score, which is a fact about a **pair**, and every denominator
tried on it docked somebody ADR-0049 protects — both sides of an honest
disagreement included (``docs/adr/0137``). *Answers about results* asks
whether **this person** replied to a score put in front of them, and a
counter is as good an answer as an acceptance, so disagreeing costs nothing
and only silence is priced.

**Three different blends of these six exist in this system and confusing
them is a live risk:** the published Player Score at 35/20/15/12/10/8, and
these two. The reliability *floor* reads the published one — the one
deliberate exception, because a penalty justified by a figure that exists
nowhere a human can look is unexplainable.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who did not come — somebody else on the game's court.

deadline.title: Deadline
deadline.description: When the seat leaves the board — the club's cut-off while it is ahead, then the start.

fills_by_the_cut_off.title: Fills By The Cut Off
fills_by_the_cut_off.description: *fills by Fri 16:00* — before the cut-off, the game is off unless its seats are taken by `deadline`; `false` is *offered until the start*. Switches by itself at the cut-off.

RescueOfferSchema.title: RescueOfferSchema
RescueOfferSchema.description: The open seat, offered to a reader not on the game (#545).

sport.description: Which sport's deck to deal whole again

ResetDeckRequest.title: ResetDeckRequest
ResetDeckRequest.description:
One *Show them again*, for one sport. **Write-only.**

Nothing is returned by this route and no route anywhere returns a reset.

**The sport is the whole ask.** The button is on a deck and a deck is one
sport, so a padel reset says nothing about tennis. There is no field for
*what* to clear: the three things a reset lifts — every pass suppression,
the day's dealt memory and the cool-off — lift together, and a client that
could pick would be a client that could clear the cool-off and keep its
passes, which is not a thing the product offers.

confidence_ceiling.title: Confidence Ceiling
confidence_ceiling.description: The highest `confidence` this engine version can reach, as a whole percent — a questionnaire has an irreducible limit, so a rating at this value was held by the ceiling and one below it by its own evidence. Absent only for a rating replayed from an engine version that has since been retired, which is the same case that carries no `confidence_reason`: such a rating keeps its numbers and loses its explanation. Do not hold a local copy of this number — it is version-scoped and may be retuned without a client release.

sport.description: Which sport this line-up is for. **Required, except beside `completing_challenge_id`** — a challenge already knows what game is being arranged, and sending both is refused.

mode.description:
Competitive or for fun — the weight vector for this one search. It selects the **group** vector too, which inverts against the shortlist's: for fun puts more weight on how the four get on than on how even the sides are.

**Required, except beside `completing_challenge_id`**, and refused there. A challenge sent with a mode keeps it — a competitive court must not have its last seat filled by a for-fun search — and one sent without a mode takes yours, resolved from your declared Play intent. **There is no mode picker anywhere.**

locked_seats.title: Locked Seats
locked_seats.description:
Players you have already seated by hand, **in seat order**. Send none and the engine fills every seat; send one or two and it fills the rest **around them**, which is when it starts optimising for the group rather than for you — `search.optimised_for` says so.

Everybody named must be somebody this search can still seat, and they must be able to share a court **with each other** — every gate binds all six pairs. Either refusal is `locked_seat_not_available`, naming nobody, rather than a quiet replacement.

Nobody twice, and never more than the sport seats.

**Refused beside `completing_challenge_id`.** The people already on that court are its locked seats, read off the challenge.

completing_challenge_id.title: Completing Challenge Id
completing_challenge_id.description:
The half-built challenge this fill completes. **Send it and send nothing else about the court**: the sport, the kind of evening and the locked seats are all read off it.

**Any live member may fill; ending a court is a different act** — removing one that was never a game is the organiser's while nobody has joined and nobody's once somebody has, and calling off the game a court became is any player's on it. A challenge born of two mutual yeses has an organiser who is only whoever said yes second, and leaving the other one unable to finish the four would be an arbitrary tiebreak deciding whose game it is.

The people who accepted come back as **ordinary candidate rows**, so the builder can draw them; the open-challenge gate steps aside for this one challenge and for nothing else, and the four fail-closed gates are untouched — so somebody blocked, held or deactivated since they accepted is still `locked_seat_not_available`.

Everybody who has already **answered** this challenge is out of its own pool, including the people who declined it.

**The window is never re-stamped**, and a challenge born of a mutual yes has none at all: a newly-invited player answers against the label the original send derived, and the plan is the authority on when anybody actually plays.

availability_override.title: Availability Override
availability_override.description: The week to run **this one line-up** against. Omit to use the grid on your profile — **omit it, never send `null`**.

offered_by_search_id.title: Offered By Search Id
offered_by_search_id.description: The search whose relaxation offer this one accepts. Taking a rung is a **new search citing the one that offered it**.

rung.description: Which rung of that search's offer you are taking. Sent with `offered_by_search_id` or not at all.

RunLineupRequest.title: RunLineupRequest
RunLineupRequest.description:
⚡ *Fill the seats.* **The line-up and fill-seats are one request.**

They differ by `locked_seats` being non-empty, which is a property of what
you send rather than of where you send it — so hand-seating somebody and
pressing ⚡ is the same shape as ⚡ on an empty court, and there is no second
route for a client to get wrong.

There is **no seat count** here and there never will be: how many people sit
down is the sport's own fact. There is no radius either, for the reason the
shortlist has none.

**A fill names the challenge it completes and says nothing else about the
court** (`ADR-0150`). Send `completing_challenge_id` and `sport`, `mode` and
`locked_seats` are **refused** beside it rather than made optional: all three
are facts that challenge already holds, and a caller supplying one is
offering a second place for a fact to be true — which is how somebody who is
not in the challenge gets locked, or somebody who is gets forgotten.

sport.description: Which sport this search is for

mode.description: Competitive or for fun — the weight vector for this one search, and nothing else. Two values, where a Play intent has three.

availability_override.title: Availability Override
availability_override.description:
The week to run **this one search** against, when the player edited it on the search screen. Omit to use the grid on your profile — **omit it, never send `null`**.

**It is an ask and never a correction.** Nothing here writes your profile; the app offers to save it afterwards.

offered_by_search_id.title: Offered By Search Id
offered_by_search_id.description: The search whose relaxation offer this one accepts. **Taking a rung is a new search citing the one that offered it**, never a silent change to your saved preferences.

rung.description: Which rung of that search's offer you are taking. Sent with `offered_by_search_id` or not at all — and the widening itself is **not** sent: the backend reads it off the offer it made.

RunSearchRequest.title: RunSearchRequest
RunSearchRequest.description:
What a client may send. **Asks only, never a fact about the searcher.**

There is deliberately **no radius here, and there never will be.** The
searcher's ask *is* their profile radius, read at request time; widening
happens only by taking a rung offer. A radius supplied by a phone is a gate
evaluated on a lie, and this is the field it would arrive through.

Rung.title: Rung
Rung.description:
Which rung of the ladder an offer is.

Three values and no more. They are letters rather than numbers because
``docs/adr/0099`` rebuilt the ladder from scratch and a rung ``1`` would
invite a reader to line it up against §9.8's struck rung 1, which relaxed
something else entirely.

rung.description: Which rung. The list is in the engine's recommended order — times first, because a slot you were already free in costs nothing where distance costs travel on every game forever — but the order is a recommendation and any rung may be taken directly.

ask.description: Which of **your own** asks it relaxes. A rung never touches a measurement, a term, a weight, or the quality floor.

candidates_above_floor.title: Candidates Above Floor
candidates_above_floor.description: How many people would clear the quality floor at this rung, from a genuine re-run. The number on the button is true.

window.description: This rung's **own** window. A challenge sliding from `WEEKEND` to `THIS_WEEK` is part of what widening costs, and you see it before you pay it.

radius_km.title: Radius Km
radius_km.description: The widened radius, on a `RADIUS` rung. Always inside the same 1-50 km your own slider holds: a relaxation never offers a radius you could not have set yourself, so a searcher already at 50 km is offered no radius rung at all.

slot.description: The one hour this rung would add to your week, on a `TIMES` rung, and **for this search only**. The same two named fields every other hour crosses in, because this one is drawn on the same seven-by-sixteen grid the player just filled in — ticked there as belonging to this search and to no later one.

RungOfferSchema.title: RungOfferSchema
RungOfferSchema.description:
One rung of the relaxation ladder, priced. **Offered, never applied.**

The engine computes what relaxing one of *your own* asks would be worth and
hands you the number; it never takes the offer for you, because only you can
say truthfully that you are free on a Saturday.

**The count is real.** It comes from re-running the whole search at this
rung — not from an estimate, and not from the strict count plus something.

brand.title: Brand
brand.description: The card network as the provider names it, lower case — `visa`, `mastercard`, `unknown` for one it does not recognise. An open set: draw a plain card for a brand you have no badge for.

last_four.title: Last Four
last_four.description: The last four digits of the card number.

wallet.description: The phone's wallet it was saved through, or `null` for a card typed in.

admitted.title: Admitted
admitted.description: Everybody the switch to `ANYONE` admitted, **in the order they asked**. Empty for every other save.

SavedSettingsResponse.title: SavedSettingsResponse
SavedSettingsResponse.description: The group as its settings left it, and who the save let in.

ScoreSchema.title: ScoreSchema
ScoreSchema.description:
The sets, in the order they were played.

**A score names a winner**, and a level score is refused: none of the four
sports produces a draw, and *Last 5* is win or loss with no third column to
put one in. A *set* here is whatever the sport calls its unit — a set in
tennis and padel, a game in squash and badminton.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: The **renormalised** weight — this term's share of a hundred over the terms that actually fired.

contribution.title: Contribution
contribution.description: The weight times the value. The contributions sum to the Fit.

ScoredTermSchema.title: ScoredTermSchema
ScoredTermSchema.description: One term that produced a reading, and what it was worth here.

search_id.title: Search Id
search_id.description: The answer's identity. Minted server-side and recorded before this response was returned.

mode.description: Null exactly on the deck and the radar, which have no mode and score every pairing under one ruler.

my_area_code.title: My Area Code
my_area_code.description:
**Your own** coarse area, as the code the candidate's card carries one in, and as this search ran on it.

It is here so a card can say *in your area* — a comparison between two codes, which is the one sentence an `area_code` licenses a client to write. The card is handed both codes rather than reading the profile for the second: a card that reached for a value nobody passed it would be drawing from global state.

**Omitted on a search recorded before it was kept**, and on those only. It is the search's area rather than the profile's current one, so a read-back reproduces the answer that was given rather than the one that would be given now — and an absent code drops the sentence, where an empty one would quietly claim *never in your area*.

index_stale.title: Index Stale
index_stale.description: Whether the candidate index was more than fifteen minutes behind the log. The search was served either way; past a day it would have been refused instead.

radius_clamp.title: Radius Clamp
radius_clamp.description: Whether a widening offer hit the profile slider's own ceiling. False on a search that widened nothing.

sorts_available.title: Sorts Available
sorts_available.description: Which re-sorts the client may draw over rows it already holds. **A sort that would reorder nothing is not in this list**, and the control is not drawn — a visible control that does nothing is the product lying quietly. Re-sorting costs no round trip.

rung_offers.title: Rung Offers
rung_offers.description:
What relaxing your own asks would be worth, each with a real count from a genuine re-run.

**`null` means the offers were not computed at all** — your shortlist was long enough that nobody needed them. An empty list means they were computed and there is nothing left to offer, which is the honest empty state: the pool beside it is the whole answer.

**A search that took a rung is offered none**: one climb per search screen, so the widest any accepted offer reaches is twice the radius you saved. That search's list is empty rather than `null`, and `rung_taken` beside it is what tells the two empties apart.

prompts.title: Prompts
prompts.description: Questions this search raises, each of which changes nothing until you answer it. Present on a search and **omitted on a read-back**, where a month-old question would be asked about a value that has since moved.

SearchEnvelope.title: SearchEnvelope
SearchEnvelope.description:
Every fact about *the search*, as opposed to about a candidate.

One object, identical on every route that creates a search: one renderer, one
type.

SearchMode.title: SearchMode
SearchMode.description:
What kind of evening this search is for. **Two values, never three.**

``PlayIntent`` is the *candidate's* declaration and has three values;
``SearchMode`` is the *searcher's* setting — which tab they are on, right
now — and has two. ``app/modules/player_profile/domain/play_intent.py`` says
where this type belongs when it arrives: *"it belongs to the matcher and not
to this module"*. Here it is.

**There is never a ``NO_PREFERENCE`` weight vector.** A candidate who
declared ``NO_PREFERENCE`` is indifferent about the kind of evening, so their
reverse fit runs under the *searcher's* mode: ``NO_PREFERENCE`` never selects
a weight vector, it inherits one (``ranking-weights.md`` §9). The arities
differ on purpose, so the likeliest bug in the matcher is a type error rather
than a paragraph in a document.

minimum_km.title: Minimum Km
minimum_km.description: Smallest radius a player may hold

maximum_km.title: Maximum Km
maximum_km.description: Largest radius a player may hold

SearchRadiusBoundsResource.title: SearchRadiusBoundsResource
SearchRadiusBoundsResource.description:
The range a Search radius may take, in whole kilometres.

The unit is in every field name on purpose: a bare ``minimum`` is one
refactor away from being read as metres.

SearchRadiusResponse.title: SearchRadiusResponse
SearchRadiusResponse.description: The radius as the profile now holds it.

SearchSurface.title: SearchSurface
SearchSurface.description:
Which terminal stage ran. Five values, and pooling their rates is how
every number the engine is judged by becomes meaningless — ``FILL_SEATS`` is
not even optimising for the searcher, and ``RADAR`` ranks nobody at all.

``SHORTLIST`` and ``DECK`` could be written from the start; the two line-up
surfaces arrived with their route, and the **reading** with the radar
(``docs/adr/0174`` §1). The first four were declared before any of them
could be written, because ``surface`` is a stored column and a vocabulary
that grows one value per ticket is a vocabulary whose old rows cannot be
read against the new ones — and the fifth is the one surface that was
argued for after the column existed, which is what an ADR is for.

SeatAnswer.title: SeatAnswer
SeatAnswer.description:
What the person in this seat did about being asked — or, having said yes,
about the game.

Four values and not five: *awaiting* is the absence of an answer, and giving
it a name would make ``None`` and ``AWAITING`` two spellings of one state
with nothing to choose between them.

``LAPSED`` is recorded by the sweep and is **never** a decline. They do the
same thing to the line-up and they are different facts: *answers challenges*
is a Strand over challenges that got an answer inside their window, and it is
unmeasurable if silence is filed as judgement.

``LEFT`` is the one answer written **over** another (``docs/adr/0162``,
``docs/adr/0165`` §1): an accepted seat whose occupant has since left it,
on a court that had become a game or on one that had not. It opens the
seat exactly as the other two do and is neither of them — leaving a court
you agreed to is not declining an invitation, and nothing prices it yet.

SeatCardSchema.title: SeatCardSchema
SeatCardSchema.description: The card for one seat: who they are, and what you make of them.

proposal_id.title: Proposal Id
proposal_id.description: The game it was for — a booking takes the same id.

status.description: `AUTHORISED` held, `FAILED` refused and waiting for its player, `TAKING`/`CAPTURED` paid, `RELEASING`/`CANCELLED` let go untaken.

refusal.description: Why it was refused: `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` — confirm it in the app; `DECLINED` — confirm it with another card; `TERMS_NEEDED` — accept the terms again, then say yes; `NO_METHOD` — save a method, then say yes. `null` unless it was refused.

to_confirm.description: Present exactly while the payment waits for its player: confirm it with this, then `POST /seat-charges/{id}/confirmation`.

SeatChargeResponse.title: SeatChargeResponse
SeatChargeResponse.description: One of the reader's own seat charges.

SeatChargeStatus.title: SeatChargeStatus
SeatChargeStatus.description: Where a charge stands, as its stream leaves it.

side.description: Which side of the net this seat is on

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who is to sit here, or omitted for a seat nobody was put in. The organiser holds one of these like anybody else.

SeatChoiceSchema.title: SeatChoiceSchema
SeatChoiceSchema.description:
One position on the court as the organiser left it.

**An empty seat is a seat**, so ``player_id`` is genuinely optional: an A-side
full with a B-side short is a different court from the reverse, and the next
invitee's side is not a free choice.

There is no origin field and no position. Where each invitation came from is
resolved server-side against the cited search, because a position a client
sent would be true only while the client was honest about where it had
scrolled to.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who holds this seat. ``null`` on a seat nobody was put in.

answer.description: What they did about being asked. ``null`` while they have not answered, and on a seat nobody was put in. **A lapse is not a refusal** — they are different facts and the platform counts them apart.

answer_by.title: Answer By
answer_by.description: When this seat's answer stops being wanted. Past it the seat reads as lapsed whether or not anything has swept it, and a late answer is refused rather than accepted late. ``null`` exactly when nobody was asked: an empty seat, the organiser's, and both seats of a challenge born from a mutual yes.

name.title: Name
name.description:
The whole name, and **nothing may derive a familiar form from it** — every sentence naming somebody uses all of it or names nobody (``docs/adr/0107``, ``docs/adr/0171``). Never the nickname, which is a handle drawn on a record and said nowhere.

``null`` on a seat nobody was put in, and ``null`` where ``users`` no longer has the account — never for an unnamed player, whom the entry gate holds at the naming step. The seat stays either way: a seat with no name is still a position on the court, and the screen has a side to name instead.

**A name is the whole of what a challenge borrows about a person here.** A Level, a band, an area and a photograph are a card's, and a card is drawn on the detail read alone.

SeatSchema.title: SeatSchema
SeatSchema.description:
One seat: a side, its occupant, their answer and their own deadline.

``answer_by`` is **this seat's own**, dated when this seat was invited — a
seat filled later starts its own day and cannot inherit a deadline from a send
it was not part of. It is absent exactly when nobody was asked: an empty seat,
the organiser's, and both seats of a challenge born from a mutual yes.

booking_id.title: Booking Id
booking_id.description: `POST /bookings/{id}/seats` takes the seat — *I'm in · `share_grosze`* — and `GET /bookings/{id}` is its details as the reader sees it from outside.

kind.description: Competitive, or for fun (*· friendly* on the title).

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start; games are 1 h.

court_name.title: Court Name
court_name.description: What the club calls the court.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: The dashed **?** squares after the players' posters.

deadline.title: Deadline
deadline.description: When the row leaves the board — the club's cut-off while it is ahead, then the start.

fills_by_the_cut_off.title: Fills By The Cut Off
fills_by_the_cut_off.description: *fills by `deadline`* before the cut-off; `false` is *offered until the start*. Switches by itself at the cut-off.

players.title: Players
players.description: Everybody on the game, each *paid* — the small posters, first side first. Long-press a poster for their record.

SeatToFillSchema.title: SeatToFillSchema
SeatToFillSchema.description:
One *Seats to fill* row: a booked game that lost a player, and the
reader fits and is free for it.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who holds this seat. ``null`` on a seat somebody has **left** and nobody has filled yet: the seat stays, drawn empty, and the game is awaiting a player before it can be recorded as played. **Always present** — a seat is never dropped.

name.title: Name
name.description:
The whole name, and **nothing may derive a familiar form from it** — every sentence naming somebody uses all of it or names nobody (``docs/adr/0107``, ``docs/adr/0171``). Never the nickname: a handle is drawn on a record and said nowhere.

``null`` where ``users`` no longer has this account, and on an open seat — never for an unnamed player, whom the entry gate holds at the naming step. The seat stays: dropping it would publish a three-person doubles game, and the screen has a side to name instead.

SeatingSchema.title: SeatingSchema
SeatingSchema.description:
One position on one side: a person, or a seat somebody has left.

**The court is frozen until somebody leaves it** (``docs/adr/0162``). An
open seat is drawn, never dropped — `player_id` is `null` and the seat keeps
its place — so a four with one seat open is still a four and the client
folds *Needs a player* from it. Nothing on the wire names that rung.

**A name, and nothing else about them** (``docs/adr/0141``). A Level, a
band, an area and a run of form are what a *searcher* reads to decide about a
game that might happen, and a gate decided they may see them; this is the
record of a game that did, and it re-publishes nobody's profile off the back
of it. The court is the whole of the permission — ``GET /games`` answers
about games you were on the court of — so nothing here is re-gated against
who is reading.

name.title: Name
name.description: The club's name; `null` for a club that no longer exists.

SellerSchema.title: SellerSchema
SellerSchema.description: The club a share is paid to — the seller, named on every receipt.

search_id.title: Search Id
search_id.description: The search this court was built from. **Required** — every invitee must have appeared in it, and each seat cites where they sat.

court.title: Court
court.description: The sides as you arranged them, in the court's own order: every **A** seat, then every **B**. It must be the sport's shape and you must be in it.

SendChallengeRequest.title: SendChallengeRequest
SendChallengeRequest.description:
One press. **The court, and the search it was built on.**

``search_id`` is the origin, and it is one search for the whole court: the
arrangement was built and forecast against a single answer, and a court
assembled out of two searches is a court no forecast was ever computed for.

**The sport, the kind of evening and the week are not sent.** All three are
read off that search's own record — there is no window picker anywhere
(``docs/adr/0100``), and a player changes their window by changing their grid.

text.title: Text
text.description: What to say. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed; empty after trimming is `message_is_empty`, and past the cap is `message_is_too_long`. **Neither is silently fixed** — a shortened message is one the sender believes they sent whole.

client_message_id.title: Client Message Id
client_message_id.description:
An id you generate for this send, **in the body rather than an `Idempotency-Key` header**, because it does two jobs: it makes a retry safe, and it is what you reconcile your optimistic bubble on.

**Send the same one on a retry.** A repeat answers `200` with the same message and the same `seq`, and records nothing — so a send that paused offline and resumed can never become two messages.

SentChallengeResponse.title: SentChallengeResponse
SentChallengeResponse.description:
What a send answers with. **An id, and deliberately nothing else.**

Not the challenge: nobody has answered it yet, so every seat says exactly
what the organiser just sent, and a body repeating their own arrangement back
at them is a round trip that says nothing. The id is what the client keeps.

day.title: Day
day.description: A local day in the platform zone, **clamped to 7 days past the row's `anchor`** — so a plan can never name a day past the entry window once there is a game, and the row of days a client offers shrinks as the week runs out.

hour.title: Hour
hour.description: A local clock time in **30-minute steps between 06:00 and 23:00**, validated server-side. Bounded chips the platform offered, never a free instant: the grid a client draws is a convention, and this is what makes it true.

place.title: Place
place.description:
Where you are meeting. Runs of whitespace collapse to one space, so the value is one line; empty after that is `the_place_is_empty`, and past 120 characters is `the_place_is_too_long`. **Neither is silently fixed** — a shortened note is one the person who typed it believes they wrote whole, in front of the other people on the court.

**The cap is not declared here on purpose.** A `maxLength` would make an over-long note a `422` about a field, where it is a refusal this context owns and names — the same shape `POST /conversations/{id}/messages` already takes.

a.title: A
a.description: GameSide A's games in this set

b.title: B
b.description: GameSide B's games in this set

SetScoreSchema.title: SetScoreSchema
SetScoreSchema.description:
One set, **absolute**: what side A took, and what side B took.

Never relative to the reader. A score stored from one point of view has to be
flipped by whoever reads it next, and the first reader to forget publishes a
loss as a win.

weekly_hours.title: Weekly Hours
weekly_hours.description: Every hour still ticked. **The list is the week** — what is absent is unticked — and an empty list clears it, which is a legal value rather than a refusal.

SetWeeklyHoursRequest.title: SetWeeklyHoursRequest
SetWeeklyHoursRequest.description:
The weekly hours, replaced whole — *Save your week*.

**No floor, and that is the difference from the commit.** An empty list is a
cleared week and is recorded; ``weekly_hours_empty`` refuses the answer a
player is *asked for* at the end of onboarding, not every later edit of it.

Repeated hours are collapsed rather than refused, and the response carries
the week as it was stored — so a client that sent the same hour twice, or
sent the week in its own order, can see what the profile now holds.

day.title: Day
day.description: ISO weekday — 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday. The grid is Monday-first.

hour.title: Hour
hour.description: The hour that cell starts at, wall clock — 19 is 19:00 to 20:00

SharedSlot.title: SharedSlot
SharedSlot.description:
The next hour of the week both players ticked.

**The grid is never rendered to anybody as a calendar.** Only the count of
shared hours and the name of the next shared one are ever shown, because
overlap is a fact about a pair where a calendar is a fact about a person.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description:
Ranked. **An empty list is a `200`** — the honest empty state is an answer, not a failure.

A read-back may carry withheld rows: the record is immutable and the gates are live, so a row the product has since agreed not to show keeps its place and states that it is withheld. Branch on `withheld` — a fresh search never carries one.

ShortlistResponse.title: ShortlistResponse
ShortlistResponse.description:
The whole answer: one envelope, and at most twenty rows.

**Bounded and unpaginated.** There is no page two; past the last row there
are rung offers or an honest empty state. The bound is ruleset data, so a
client never reads twenty from anywhere — it renders the rows it is given.

Side-Input.title: Side
Side-Input.description:
Which side of the net. The organiser is always on ``A``.

This context's own, and deliberately a second spelling of
``matchmaking.domain.lineups.Side``: the matcher's is *the searcher's side of
a line-up it is ranking*, this one is *a position on a court somebody has
been asked to sit in*, and ``challenges`` may not import ``matchmaking``.
The two strings are equal on purpose, so the mapping at the seam is identity
rather than a table.

SidesSchema.title: SidesSchema
SidesSchema.description:
The two sides of the net. **You are always on `A`.**

There is no arrangement in which the searcher crosses the net, because
*which side am I on* is not a question a builder asks: what varies is who is
beside you.

sport.description: Which sport this panel is about — **the resolved one, not the one asked for.** They differ whenever the subject holds no rating in the sport you arrived from.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level, as RacketSkill published it.

band.title: Band
band.description: The band's published name, as a key. The band's numeric edges are **not** here: they are not a second range to compare `likely_range` against.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description:
How sure the platform is, as a whole percentage — `rating`'s own figure and never re-derived here.

**It travels with `counted_games` and is meaningless without it.** A confident-looking number built on three games must not read like one built on forty, which is the whole reason both cross.

counted_games.title: Counted Games
counted_games.description:
**How many confirmed counted results have moved this Level, in this sport.** Deliberately not the player card's `counted_games`, which is how much they have *played*, over every sport, and includes an evening nobody agreed a score for.

This one is what the certainty rests on, so it comes off the same stream as the Level beside it and moves in step with it. **`0` is a real answer here** and is not an absence: a rating from the questionnaire that no game has tested yet is exactly what it says.

likely_range.description: The range their Level probably sits in, μ ± σ as the engine rounded it. Always present: two people both showing 2,75 are told apart by how wide this is.

last_five.title: Last Five
last_five.description:
Their last counted results **in this sport**, oldest to newest — the run of form drawn left to right.

**Per sport, which is the fix.** A run built across every sport and drawn beneath a single sport's Level was squash results under a padel number.

**Fewer than five is a real answer and is never padded**: three entries means three counted results, and the client draws the gap. An empty list means none of theirs has been counted and agreed.

**There are no dates here, at any granularity.** A moment beside one of these would be activity recency, which no surface on this platform carries in any shape.

SkillPanelSchema.title: SkillPanelSchema
SkillPanelSchema.description:
The skill card, for the one sport this sheet is about.

**The sport is resolved by the server and stated back.** You asked with
`?sport=`; what you get is that sport where they are rated in it, and
otherwise the one they have played most — so read `sport` here rather than
assuming the answer is what you sent.

name.title: Name
name.description: Their Name, whole; `null` for an account that can no longer be named.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their published Level in the sport.

forecast.description: How even a game of the poster and them is forecast — `null` where it cannot be read.

SlotFitSchema.title: SlotFitSchema
SlotFitSchema.description: One of the poster's best fits free then — *2,75 · 93*.

SocialTag.title: SocialTag
SocialTag.description: The closed set of tag ids. An id here is permanent.

SocialTagGroup.title: SocialTagGroup
SocialTagGroup.description: The three groups, which are about the game and nothing else.

SocialTagGroupResource.title: SocialTagGroupResource
SocialTagGroupResource.description: One of the three groups, with its tags in the order they are rendered.

SocialTagResource.title: SocialTagResource
SocialTagResource.description:
One tag, as an id and nothing else — for now.

An object rather than a bare string deliberately: retiring a tag is
anticipated (an id is honoured forever and hidden from the picker), and a
tag that carries a field one day is an addition here, where an array of
strings would have to change element type — which breaks a shipped client.

minimum_tags.title: Minimum Tags
minimum_tags.description: Fewest tags a player may hold — the picker's floor

maximum_tags.title: Maximum Tags
maximum_tags.description: Most tags a player may hold — the picker's ceiling

SocialTagSelectionBoundsResource.title: SocialTagSelectionBoundsResource
SocialTagSelectionBoundsResource.description:
How many Social tags a selection must hold to be one.

The unit is in both field names for the reason it is on the radius bounds:
a bare ``minimum`` beside a list of eighteen tags reads as a count of
