something, and which something is exactly what a client would guess wrong.

social_tags.title: Social Tags
social_tags.description: In the vocabulary's order, whatever order was sent.

SocialTagsResponse.title: SocialTagsResponse
SocialTagsResponse.description:
The tags as the profile now holds them — in the vocabulary's order.

A body rather than a ``204`` for the week's reason: the order stored is the
platform's and not the picker's, so a client that kept what it sent would
hold a selection in an order the profile does not.

matched.title: Matched
matched.description: Tag ids they both hold, in this column

SocialVibeEvidence.title: SocialVibeEvidence
SocialVibeEvidence.description:
What the two of them are like around the game.

The same shape as playing style and deliberately a **separate variant**: the
two terms carry different weights, invert between the modes, and a client
renders them under different headings. One variant with a column field would
make *which term is this* a value the client has to branch on rather than a
type it can dispatch over.

SortOption.title: SortOption
SortOption.description:
The re-sorts a client may offer over rows it already holds.

**Server-driven, and a sort that would reorder nothing is not drawn.** A
client deriving offerability from ``degraded_terms`` would be encoding a
sort-to-term mapping, which is the objection that promoted ``distance_km``
out of the distance evidence in the first place.

``MOST_RELIABLE`` reads the **published** Player Score, and it is offered on
a search whose candidates have one and withheld on a search whose candidates
do not — a fact about *that* search, re-derived per search rather than
hardcoded. Most people have no record yet, so most searches still do not draw
it, and that is the derivation working rather than a gap. ``EVENEST`` reads
``would_be_forecast``, which no shortlist carries.

your_side.title: Your Side
your_side.description: Your half's combined strength, on the Skill scale. **You are always side `A`** — there is no arrangement in which you cross the net.

gap.title: Gap
gap.description:
`your_side` − `their_side`, **signed**. Served rather than left to a subtraction: a client subtracting two rounded figures and an engine subtracting two unrounded ones disagree at the boundary, and the card prints all three.

Signed because the bar takes an *advantage* — an unsigned gap would leave the client deciding which half of it is bigger, which is the same arithmetic in a smaller disguise.

SplitSchema.title: SplitSchema
SplitSchema.description:
The two side strengths this arrangement's forecast was read from.

**The evidence behind the percentage**, and never a second score
(``docs/adr/0136``). ``pct`` says *how even*; this says *between what and
what*, on the Skill scale a player already reads levels on — which is
``matchmaking-engine.md`` §12 rule 1 applied to the figure that was already
crossing, exactly as it put ``sigma_group`` beside ``pct``. The group
objective stays where ADR-0117 left it: recorded, and never returned.

**On the arrangement rather than on the forecast.** ``ForecastSchema`` is
*one type, everywhere it appears* and rides on every shortlist row's
``would_be_forecast``; a response carries at most three arrangements and tens
of candidate rows, and this is a fact about an arrangement.

**These are numbers only the engine has.** A side's strength is not the mean
of the two people on it, so a client averaging seated levels would print a
different pair — which is the arithmetic ``the-play-screens.md`` §11.3
refuses, in the one check that looks for arithmetic rather than reading
intent.

Sport.title: Sport
Sport.description: The four sports Raketa rates, as a closed enum.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level in it, as RacketSkill published it.

SportLevelSchema.title: SportLevelSchema
SportLevelSchema.description: One sport somebody is rated in, and their Level in it.

sport.description: Which sport. The client draws its own dot and short form.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their Level in it, as RacketSkill published it.

band.title: Band
band.description: The Level band's published name. **A key and never derived from the Level** — a client mapping a number to a band would be a second set of drawing constants, and the day the boundaries move the two would disagree.

SportPillSchema.title: SportPillSchema
SportPillSchema.description:
One sport this person is rated in, as a pill: the dot, the Level, the band.

**Narrower than the panel below it, deliberately.** A pill answers *what else
do they play*; how sure the platform is and what that rests on belong to the
one sport the sheet is about, and repeating them four times would be four
skill cards drawn as jewellery.

players.title: Players
players.description: Number of players the sport is played for

SportResource.title: SportResource
SportResource.description: One sport as served: how many play it and the durations it is sold in.

Standing.title: Standing
Standing.description: The seven standings, as codes. A client's words are the client's own.

side.description: Which side put this score on the table

answer_by.title: Answer By
answer_by.description: When the other side's silence becomes agreement. **Nothing happens at this moment** — no job runs and nothing is written; the game simply reads as confirmed from here on.

settles_at.title: Settles At
settles_at.description: When an acceptance of this score would become final. Earlier than `answer_by`, and it is the grace an opponent who has not read the score yet is given: inside it a disagreement still wins.

StandingProposalSchema.title: StandingProposalSchema
StandingProposalSchema.description:
One side's score, on the table and not yet settled on.

**At most one per side**, which is what bounds an argument to two rounds. Two
of them is the disagreement this platform does not resolve — and it does not
resolve it by *arbitrating*, not by hiding it: both scores travel, either
side may agree with the other's, and that is the only end short of the game
going unscored.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: One of the other players on that court — in doubles an opponent or your partner, in singles the one opponent.

stars.title: Stars
stars.description: One to five whole stars. There is no zero and there are no halves.

StarsGivenSchema.title: StarsGivenSchema
StarsGivenSchema.description:
One player on the card, and the stars they were given.

``stars`` is declared as a plain integer **on purpose**. The range is one to
five whole stars and it lives in the domain, where a seed, a test and a
request all meet the same refusal; a Pydantic bound restating it here would
be a second copy of the rule, and the first of the two to be edited would win
silently for whichever callers went through it. A number off the scale comes
back as `stars_are_one_to_five`.

score.description: The score you say was played

StateResultRequest.title: StateResultRequest
StateResultRequest.description:
*This is the score.*

**One request for three acts**, and the record decides which: the first score
entered, a correction of your own side's while nobody has answered it, or
your side's disagreement with the other's. A client that named which would be
a client that could name it wrongly, and a mislabelled correction is a
proposal nobody may make.

**There is no rejection here and there is no body without a score.** An
objection carrying nothing would be free and always optimal for the loser.

StrandReading.title: StrandReading
StrandReading.description:
One reliability strand that produced a reading.

A strand with too few observations **stands down and is absent from the
list** rather than present at zero: *we have not seen enough* and *they are
bad at this* are different facts, and a term may never be honestly neutral.

strand.description:
Which strand this row is. **Key your copy off this code**, never off the row's position: a strand with nothing behind it is absent from the list entirely, so the rows you get are the rows this person has.

Three of the six names have no provider on this platform today and never appear here. They are listed on the enum because the vocabulary is closed and shared with the Fit breakdown, not because they are coming.

good.title: Good
good.description:
How many of those opportunities went the way the strand is named for — a game that was played, a booked game that was kept, a score that got a reply.

**A no is a good outcome on `ANSWERS_RESULTS`.** Countering a score you believe is wrong *is* answering it; what the strand prices is silence. **`KEEPS_PLANS` is broken only by leaving** a booked game so that it is called off at its cut-off, or after the cut-off with nobody taking the seat.

opportunities.title: Opportunities
opportunities.description:
How many times this fell due. **An opportunity and never a total**: a game still awaiting its entry, a booked game whose hour has not come and a score still inside its window are in neither half of this row, because publishing them either way would state a conclusion the clock has not reached.

**`ANSWERS_RESULTS` counts the last twelve months and the other rows count a career.** It is the one strand that forgets, so a player can work a bad month off it.

Never `0` — a row with nothing behind it is not drawn at all.

pct.title: Pct
pct.description:
The figure out of a hundred for this strand. **Served, never derived** — dividing `good` by `opportunities` yourself produces a fourth rounding of one record: this one rounds halves up, and the day a client rounds differently the two disagree by a point on exactly the values a player notices.

**Not the Fit breakdown's `StrandReading.value`**, which is the matcher's own reading of the same strand between 0 and 1. Two scales, two surfaces, two names — and `pct` is this contract's existing word for a whole percentage, as on the balance forecast.

StrandRowSchema.title: StrandRowSchema
StrandRowSchema.description:
One metered row: what fell due, what came of it, and the figure shown.

**All three cross, and the third is not a convenience.** `good` and
`opportunities` are the raw pair — a perfect record over nine and one over
forty are different claims, and a bar alone hides which. `pct` is the figure
the platform itself acts on, served so that a client is not the fourth place
this record gets rounded.

code.title: Code
code.description:
What happened, as a machine code the client renders a sentence from. Nine: **`SEAT_ACCEPTED`**, **`SEATS_INVITED`**, **`SEAT_LEFT`**, **`GAME_PLAYED`**, the Plan's **`PLACE_RECORDED`**, **`DAY_RECORDED`**, **`HOUR_RECORDED`** and **`PLAN_LOCKED`**, and **`SIDE_FORMED`**.

**`SIDE_FORMED` is the one line a room is born with, and only a doubles room** (ADR-0169 §8). Two yeses that met in a doubles sport seat both people on one side with a whole side still to fill, and this says so at `seq` 1: *You two are a side. Fill the seats to find your opponents.* A singles mutual's room carries no such line. It names no actor and carries no values.

**A seat leaving is one code with the answer as a value**, because *that seat is open again* is the same news each way — and a lapse is still not a decline, which is what `values.departure` keeps apart. Somebody **leaving a game they had agreed to** is the third way, since ADR-0162, and the one whose actor was a member until this very line.

**A slot set and a slot moved are one code told twice**, which is the opposite rule for the opposite case: three slots are three facts, so they are three codes, and there is no value telling a first fill from a change because they are the same fact.

**`PLAN_LOCKED` is the Plan's fourth and it carries no values at all.** The three slots are the value and the room already holds a line for each. It is an act rather than a slot — a complete plan is one everybody *could* agree, and this says somebody did — and there is no unlocked code, because a slot moved afterwards keeps the lock and writes its own line.

**There is no *Game on* line.** Everybody having accepted is an arrangement of the seats, so a line announcing it would be a second place for a folded standing to be true. What appears instead is the plan card and membership stopping — drawn, not announced.

actor_id.title: Actor Id
actor_id.description: Who did it, or `null`. **Render `{name}` from the `people` on the response that carried this line** — the name is never repeated here, so a corrected one fixes the whole backlog. Not from `members` alone: the actor of a `SEAT_LEFT` line is by definition no longer one, and `people` is where the read put their face. `null` on `SIDE_FORMED`, which is about both people on the side and names neither.

values.title: Values
values.description: What the sentence needs beyond a name, and **nothing membership already says**. `SEATS_INVITED` carries `count`; `SEAT_LEFT` carries `departure`, one of `DECLINED`, `LAPSED` or `LEFT`; the three plan codes each carry `value` — the place as it was typed, the day as `YYYY-MM-DD`, the hour as `HH:MM`. `SEAT_ACCEPTED`, `GAME_PLAYED` and `SIDE_FORMED` carry nothing.

SystemLineSchema.title: SystemLineSchema
SystemLineSchema.description: What happened, as a code and its values. **Never a sentence.**

TagPair.title: TagPair
TagPair.description:
Two tag ids one relationship row fired on.

Ids only. The row's kind is the field it sits under, its column is the term
it sits under, and its strength or severity is a ruleset number the player is
not shown — what is owed here is *which two things about you two this reads*.

Term.title: Term
Term.description:
The eight terms of Fit, weighted per mode and renormalised per comparison.

Eight and not seven: the prototype's single ``vibe`` merges what the split
below keeps apart, and intent alignment is the term the prototype never had.
**The split between playing style and social vibe is by *relationship*, not
by tag group** — every matrix row carries its own column
(``ranking-weights.md`` §1).

Day one **reliability stands down** and the live seven renormalise; that is
the basis every judged reading and the quality floor were computed on.

TranscriptEntryResponse.title: TranscriptEntryResponse
TranscriptEntryResponse.description: One answered question: the question as it was asked, and what was chosen.

UncertaintyFactorResponse.title: UncertaintyFactorResponse
UncertaintyFactorResponse.description: Something that widened the range instead of moving the estimate.

UncountedReason.title: UncountedReason
UncountedReason.description: Why a game ended uncounted without anybody disagreeing about a score.

UnfilledReason.title: UnfilledReason
UnfilledReason.description:
Why a seat is empty, and why the four-way week is.

``the-group-objective.md`` §5.1's closed vocabulary. **A partial line-up is
always a `200`**: *three of four* is an honest answer, and *nobody* is the
same shape with three seats carrying a reason rather than a separate empty
state.

``NO_ADMISSIBLE_COMBINATION`` is the one ``docs/adr/0116`` added and it is
load-bearing: without it a six-pair gate is indistinguishable from a thin
pool, on the screen and in the telemetry — and after
``docs/adr/0113`` it is also how a screen says *nobody at their level yet*
about a newcomer's first four rather than *nobody*.

adult_attested.title: Adult Attested
adult_attested.description: The player's own claim that they are an adult. Required, and required to be `true`: the platform is adults only and that is a precondition of holding an account. `false` is refused with `adult_attestation_required`, and the client writes the sentence. **Not a date of birth and not age verification** — this records that the question was asked and answered, and nothing more.

UserCreateRequest.title: UserCreateRequest
UserCreateRequest.description:
Sign-up: credentials and the attestation, and nothing about who you are.

The nickname left this payload with ``docs/adr/0171`` §2 — it is asked in
onboarding, beside the name, with :class:`NameRequest`. **Extra fields are
refused** rather than ignored, so a client still sending one meets the
validation envelope instead of a sign-up that quietly dropped what it said.

name.title: Name
name.description: What this player is called — what every screen says. `null` until the naming — except on an account an invitation opened, which carries the name the club typed. The entry gate's first destination is **not named in full**: no name, or no nickname — and the naming step asks only for what is missing.

nickname.title: Nickname
nickname.description: The handle, unique across the platform, drawn as `@nickname` under the name on the You tab and nowhere else. `null` until the naming.

is_tester.title: Is Tester
is_tester.description: Whether this account carries the **tester mark**: a real player who may be given a feature before anyone else. Set and cleared by an admin command, never by the player, and `false` for every account until then. **Not a role** — `authority` does not move with it. The player app passes it to flag evaluation as `isTester`, so no published datafile ever has to name a tester.

has_player_profile.title: Has Player Profile
has_player_profile.description: Whether this player has committed a Player profile — the fourth branch of the entry gate. Read from the profile's own event stream rather than from a projection, so it is correct immediately after the commit that creates one. False on a response that is not about the authenticated player, such as the one registration returns.

UserResponse.title: UserResponse
UserResponse.description:
The account, plus the one fact about it onboarding's entry gate needs.

``has_player_profile`` is not a property of a ``User`` and the domain layer
has no idea it exists — it is answered by the Player profile context and
joined here, on the response, because the gate reads it on every cold launch
and a second round trip for one boolean would be a second thing to fail
(``docs/adr/0090``).

``name`` and ``nickname`` are **null until the naming** — and each on its
own since ``docs/adr/0185`` §4, because an account an Invitation opened
carries the club-typed name and no nickname — and this is the one read
where either may be null (``docs/adr/0171`` §2): a player on any
surface that names another player has necessarily been named, because the
gate holds an unnamed account at the naming step. On ``/me`` they are read
from the player's own stream, as ``has_player_profile`` is, so they are
right the instant after the commit the gate reads them after.

**It is not an "onboarded" flag.** The rating context's invariant against one
stands: whether a player has been through onboarding *for a sport* is asked
by asking whether a rating exists for that sport, and this field cannot
answer it. This asks a genuinely per-player question, because a profile is
one per player and has no sport dimension at all.

Wallet.title: Wallet
Wallet.description:
The phone's own wallet a card was saved through. Only the two the setup
offers (the mechanics §12.4): Apple Pay on an iPhone, Google Pay on Android.
A card saved through any other wallet is recorded as a plain card.

day.title: Day
day.description: ISO weekday — 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday. The grid is Monday-first.

hour.title: Hour
hour.description: The hour the cell starts at, wall clock — 19 is 19:00 to 20:00. The week runs 07:00 to 23:00, so the first cell is 7 and the last is 22.

WeeklyHourResource.title: WeeklyHourResource
WeeklyHourResource.description:
One ticked hour of the week — a day, and the hour its cell starts at.

Two named fields rather than the single joined code the event stream stores.
The stream's code is a *storage* encoding chosen so a replay folds strings;
this is a contract a client renders a grid from, and a client that had to
split ``"3:19"`` would be parsing our persistence format.

**Every cell, and there is no exception.** The rule was twice read as
covering only the cells a player *chose* — the one a times rung offers
(#283), and the week a raised ``KEEP_THESE_TIMES`` quotes back (#286) — on
the argument that a payload handed back is not a resource. Both crossed as
codes, and in both cases a client ended up splitting one. What decides this
is not whose value it is but **what is done with it**: a cell that gets
drawn on the seven-by-sixteen grid crosses in these two fields, and the engine
holding it as a code is a fact about the engine. This side of the boundary
owns the encoding, so this side is where it is read.

WeeklyHoursResponse.title: WeeklyHoursResponse
WeeklyHoursResponse.description:
The weekly hours as the profile now holds them.

A body rather than a ``204`` because the value stored is not always the
value sent: repeated hours are collapsed and the order is the platform's
reading order, so a client that kept what it sent would hold a week the
profile does not.

name.title: Name
name.description: The club's name; `null` for a club that no longer exists.

distance_km.title: Distance Km
distance_km.description: From the reader's Location area to the club, one decimal, never below a tenth — *3,1 km*. `null` for a reader with no Location area.

WhereSchema.title: WhereSchema
WhereSchema.description: WHERE: the club, and how far it is from the reader.

Who.title: Who
Who.description: Who a post is for (the mechanics §9.1 step 3).

Window.title: Window
Window.description:
When a game found on a week would plausibly be played. **A code, never a
sentence** — *"tonight"* is the client's word (``docs/adr/0022``).

**Derived, never chosen** (``docs/adr/0100``). There is no window picker
anywhere: a player changes their window by changing their week, which is the
same act that changes their matches. One control, one meaning.

It is a **label on the search**, not a proposed time — the week is still
never rendered to anybody as a calendar, and this says only how soon the week
it ran on comes round.

WireInclusionReason.title: WireInclusionReason
WireInclusionReason.description:
Why this person is in the list at all — **and it is a union of one.**

The store keeps three values and the wire publishes this one, which is the
whole of ``the-two-contracts.md`` §4's *the store is open where the wire is
closed*. Only an **interest lift** admits anybody; the other two **reorder**,
and a reorder is not a reason a searcher is owed:

- ``NEWCOMER_WINDOW`` reaches the client as a Liveness reason instead, which
  is where a printable reorder belongs.
- ``ZERO_EXPOSURE`` never crosses at all. *You are seeing this person because
  nobody has been shown them all week* is a third party's unpopularity, and
  the searcher is owed no version of it.

It stays an enum of one rather than a bare literal so the next reason that
genuinely **admits** somebody has somewhere to go.

withheld.title: Withheld
withheld.description: Always `true`. This row was recorded and is no longer shown: the fail-closed gates were re-evaluated at read time and one of them excludes it now. **Which one is deliberately not said.**

WithheldRowSchema.title: WithheldRowSchema
WithheldRowSchema.description:
A row that was recorded, and that the live gates no longer admit.

**Stated, never vanished.** A read-back that quietly returned nineteen rows
where twenty were recorded is the same class of lie as a breakdown that
quietly stops adding up, and worse for being invisible — so the row keeps its
place in the list and says what happened to it.

**It names no gate, and it carries no person.** The four fail-closed gates
are a block either way, a hold, an account that may not be shown, and the
mutual gender preference; naming which one fired would tell a searcher that a
particular person blocked them, was suspended, or changed a safety setting.
``docs/adr/0095`` is explicit that *neither party is ever notified and the
other side sees no trace anywhere in any response*, and that rule does not
weaken because the surface has a longer memory. So this shape has one field,
and there is nowhere on it for a reason, an id, a card or a breakdown to be
written.

The searcher loses nothing they are owed: they saw this row when they ran the
search, and what has changed since is only that the product will no longer
show it to them.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: Seats nobody is In on yet, this player's yes counted. Nought on a game that booked — and on a full game an On request club has still to confirm. A payment that could not be held opens its seat again.

booked.description: Present when this yes booked the game: every seat was charged, and the booking and its Game are open. `null` otherwise.

waiting_for_the_club.title: Waiting For The Club
waiting_for_the_club.description: This yes filled the game at an **On request** club: it went to the club, which confirms it within its time to confirm, and nobody pays until it does — the charge and *It's a game!* follow its yes. The game is on Home as `WAITING_FOR_THE_CLUB`.

your_payment.description: Present when **this player's** share could not be held: nobody paid and the game did not book. `null` otherwise — including when somebody else's could not, which leaves `open_seats` above nought.

YesAnswerResponse.title: YesAnswerResponse
YesAnswerResponse.description:
What a yes left on the game — and, when it was the last, what the fill
did.

seat_charge_id.title: Seat Charge Id
seat_charge_id.description: The refused payment: `GET /seat-charges/{id}` for what the phone confirms it with, then `POST /seat-charges/{id}/confirmation`.

refusal.description: `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` — the bank wants the player to confirm; `DECLINED` — confirm with another card; `TERMS_NEEDED` — accept the terms again, then say yes; `NO_METHOD` — save a method, then say yes.

YourPaymentSchema.title: YourPaymentSchema
YourPaymentSchema.description:
This player's share could not be held when the game filled: nobody paid,
and their seat is open again until they confirm it or somebody takes it.

app__modules__challenges__domain__seats_.title: Side
app__modules__challenges__domain__seats_.description:
Which side of the net. The organiser is always on ``A``.

This context's own, and deliberately a second spelling of
``matchmaking.domain.lineups.Side``: the matcher's is *the searcher's side of
a line-up it is ranking*, this one is *a position on a court somebody has
been asked to sit in*, and ``challenges`` may not import ``matchmaking``.
The two strings are equal on purpose, so the mapping at the seam is identity
rather than a table.

app__modules__matchmaking__domain__lineu.title: Side
app__modules__matchmaking__domain__lineu.description: Which side of the net. The searcher is always on ``A``.

client_secret.title: Client Secret
client_secret.description: The payment's secret. Confirm it in the provider's own fields.

connected_account_id.title: Connected Account Id
connected_account_id.description: The club's account at the provider — a direct charge is confirmed on the seller's account.

app__modules__payments__presentation__sc.title: PaymentToConfirmSchema
app__modules__payments__presentation__sc.description:
What the phone confirms a refused payment with, on the club's account:
the provider's own confirmation, with ``client_secret`` and the seller's
account — **asked of the provider now and never recorded**.

seat_charge_id.title: Seat Charge Id
seat_charge_id.description: The payment to confirm: `GET /seat-charges/{id}` for what the phone confirms it with, then `POST /seat-charges/{id}/confirmation`.

refusal.description: `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` — the bank wants the player to confirm; `DECLINED` — confirm with another card.

book_by.title: Book By
book_by.description: The latest moment the game can fill; past it the seat is gone.

app__modules__proposals__presentation__s.title: PaymentToConfirmSchema
app__modules__proposals__presentation__s.description:
A game still filling whose last yes could not hold this player's share:
their seat is open until they confirm the payment, or somebody takes it.
